blocks.title: Raw Supari Feeding & Pre-Cleaning
desc: Raw betelnut is first fed into the system where initial impurities such as dust, leaves, and light foreign particles are removed.
blocks.note: Ensures removal of large and light impurities before further processing.

blocks.title: Fine Cleaning & Destoning
desc: The material is then passed through advanced cleaning systems to remove stones, sand, and heavy contaminants.
blocks.note: Critical step to protect downstream machinery and ensure product purity.

blocks.title: Supari Cutting / Size Reduction
desc: Clean betelnuts are processed through cutting machines to achieve desired size and shape depending on product requirement (chips, granules, etc.).
blocks.note: Precision cutting ensures uniform size for consistent mixing and roasting.

blocks.title: Grading & Air Classification
desc: After cutting, the material is graded to separate different sizes and remove fine dust or unwanted particles.
blocks.note: Ensures uniformity and improves final product quality.

blocks.title: Roasting / Drying Process
desc: The graded supari is roasted or dried to reduce moisture content and enhance flavor, texture, and shelf life.
blocks.note: Controlled temperature ensures perfect crunchiness and consistency.

blocks.title: Cooling Process
desc: Post roasting, the product is cooled to stabilize moisture and prevent condensation.
blocks.note: Maintains product integrity before further processing.

blocks.title: Flavoring & Mixing (Optional)
desc: Depending on the final product, supari is mixed with flavors, perfumes, and additives.
blocks.note: Ensures uniform coating and flavor distribution.

blocks.title: Final Sieving & Quality Check
desc: Final screening is done to remove any inconsistencies and ensure premium quality output.

blocks.title: Packaging
desc: Finished product is packed into pouches or containers using automated packaging systems.
blocks.note: High-speed packing suitable for commercial-scale production.

metaDesc: Elaichi (green cardamom) processing machinery for mouth freshener lines: cleaning, grading, dehusking, sugar coating, drying, blending and pouch packing.
intro: Elaichi, or green cardamom, is processed into a mouth freshener by cleaning and grading the dried capsules, separating the seeds from the husk, and coating those seeds with sugar syrup before drying, blending and packing. ART Mechatronics supplies the cleaning, dehusking, coating, drying and packing machinery for elaichi mukhwas lines, as individual machines or as a complete plant.

blocks.text: Elaichi, or green cardamom, is processed into a mouth freshener by cleaning and grading the dried capsules, separating the seeds from the husk, and coating those seeds with sugar syrup before drying, blending and packing. ART Mechatronics supplies the cleaning, dehusking, coating, drying and packing machinery for elaichi mukhwas lines, as individual machines or as a complete plant.

blocks.title: Intake & Pre-Cleaning
desc: Dried cardamom capsules arriving from the curing house are lifted into the line and screened to remove dust, stalk pieces, stones and tramp metal.
Cleaning at intake protects the grading, dehusking and coating machines further down the line.

blocks.title: Grading & Colour Sorting
desc: Cleaned capsules are graded by size and sorted by colour, since the bold green capsules are held back for whole-spice sale and the smaller or discoloured lots are routed to the mouth freshener line.
Light and immature capsules are pulled out here as well, and keeping the seed size uniform matters for even coating later.

blocks.title: Dehusking & Seed Separation
desc: The capsule is cracked open and the inner seeds are separated from the light outer husk, which is drawn off by air.
Husk fragments and fines released here are captured by the extraction system so the working area stays clean.

blocks.title: Sugar Syrup Preparation & Coating
desc: Sugar syrup is prepared in a heated vessel and applied to the tumbling cardamom seeds in a coating pan, building up the coated layer in successive passes.
Silver leaf, colour or menthol is worked in at this stage for the mishri-elaichi and silver-coated varieties.

blocks.title: Drying & Conditioning
desc: Coated seeds are dried to set the sugar shell and bring the moisture down, then cooled before they are handled again.
Cardamom loses its aroma if it is overheated, so drying is kept gentle and the room is held dry.

blocks.title: Blending & Final Sieving
desc: Coated elaichi is blended with the other mukhwas ingredients and given a final screening to take out broken coating, fines and any loose husk.
Dust drawn off at the blender and sifter is collected rather than released into the hall.

blocks.title: Weighing, Packing & Inspection
desc: The finished product is weighed out and filled into sachets, pouches or jars, then checked for weight and for metal contamination before dispatch.
Sachet and pouch formats are used for retail counters, while jars serve bulk and catering supply.

blocks.title: Leaf Intake & Cleaning
desc: Baled or bagged tobacco leaf is opened and fed to the line, and stones, metal and loose trash are taken out before cutting.
Stems are separated so that only the lamina goes forward to the cutter.

blocks.title: Cutting & Shredding
desc: The cleaned leaf is cut into fine strands, which is the form hookah tobacco is sold in.
Oversize pieces are returned for re-cutting through the sifter.

blocks.title: Washing & Conditioning
desc: Many hookah blends are made from washed leaf, so the cut tobacco is rinsed and then brought back to working moisture.
Steam and jacketed vessels are used to condition the leaf before it meets the syrup.

blocks.title: Syrup Preparation & Blending
desc: Molasses, glycerine and flavouring are prepared as a syrup and then mixed through the cut leaf until the strands are evenly coated.
Mixing continues until colour and moisture read the same across the batch.

blocks.title: Maturation & Holding
desc: The blended tobacco is held so the syrup soaks right through the strands before packing.
Batches move in bins and trolleys, and are kept cool where the recipe calls for it.

blocks.title: Filling, Sealing & Packing
desc: Matured product is filled into tins, jars or pouches, sealed and coded.
Sealed units are collated into cartons for despatch.

metaTitle: Nicotine Extraction Plant & Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Nicotine extraction plant and machinery - milling, alkali conditioning, extraction, separation, drying and filling, with fume and effluent handling.
intro: Nicotine is an alkaloid recovered from tobacco leaf, stem and dust, which are dried, milled and treated with alkali before the nicotine is taken into a liquid phase. The extract is separated from spent solids, clarified and concentrated, then filled as a liquid or dried to a powder. ART Mechatronics supplies the plant for each stage, including fume and effluent handling.

blocks.text: Nicotine is an alkaloid recovered from tobacco leaf, stem and dust, which are dried, milled and treated with alkali before the nicotine is taken into a liquid phase. The extract is separated from spent solids, clarified and concentrated, then filled as a liquid or dried to a powder. ART Mechatronics supplies the plant for each stage, including fume and effluent handling.

blocks.title: Raw Material Preparation & Milling
desc: Tobacco leaf, stem and dust are received, dried where needed and reduced to a coarse powder so more surface is presented for extraction.
Milling runs under dust collection, as tobacco dust is fine and readily airborne.

blocks.title: Alkali Conditioning
desc: The milled material is wetted and treated with alkali, the usual way of releasing nicotine from its bound salt form.
Conditioning is carried out in jacketed vessels with heating and continuous agitation.

blocks.title: Extraction
desc: The conditioned mass is contacted with the extraction liquid and agitated under heat so the nicotine passes into solution.
Heat is drawn from the plant's steam and heat exchange circuit.

blocks.title: Separation & Clarification
desc: Spent tobacco solids are separated from the nicotine-bearing liquor, and the liquor is clarified before it moves on.
Clarified liquor is held in tanks ahead of concentration, and the spent solids are conveyed away.

blocks.title: Concentration & Drying
desc: The clarified liquor is concentrated, and where a solid grade is wanted the concentrate is dried to a powder.
Vacuum drying is used where the product should not be exposed to open heat.

blocks.title: Filling & Packing
desc: Liquid nicotine is filled into bottles or drums, capped, coded and labelled; powder grades are filled and sealed as dry product.
Filled containers are checked for leaks before despatch.

blocks.title: Fume & Effluent Handling
desc: Vapour, fume and process air from the extraction and drying sections are scrubbed before release.
Spent solids and process residues are handled as separate controlled waste streams.

blocks.text: Caffeine is an alkaloid extracted from tea waste, green coffee and similar raw materials, which are cleaned, milled and steeped in hot water. The liquor is clarified and concentrated, the caffeine is crystallised out and dried, and the crystals are milled and sieved to the grade required. ART Mechatronics builds the extraction, drying, milling and packing sections as one line.

blocks.title: Raw Material Intake & Cleaning
desc: Tea waste, green coffee or similar caffeine-bearing material is received and cleaned of stones, husk and light trash.
Density separation takes off the remaining heavy and light fractions, and the cleaned material is then metered forward at a steady rate.

blocks.title: Size Reduction
desc: The cleaned material is crushed and milled so that hot water can reach the caffeine held inside it.
Milled material is screened, and dust is drawn off at the mill.

blocks.title: Hot Water Extraction
desc: Milled material is steeped in hot water in stirred, jacketed vessels so the caffeine passes into solution.
Heating is taken from the plant's steam and heat exchange circuit.

blocks.title: Clarification & Concentration
desc: Spent solids are separated from the extract and the clarified liquor is concentrated.
The concentrate is held in tanks ahead of crystallisation.

blocks.title: Crystallisation & Drying
desc: The concentrate is cooled so that caffeine separates out as crystals, which are then dried.
Chilled water for the cooling stage comes from the plant's own circuit.

blocks.title: Milling & Grading
desc: Dried caffeine is milled and classified to the powder or granular grade the buyer has specified.
Sieving takes off oversize and keeps the grade consistent between batches.

blocks.title: Weighing & Packing
desc: Graded caffeine is weighed into bags or drums, sealed and coded.
Metal detection is run on the finished pack before despatch.

h1: Snus Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Snus Processing Plant & Pouching Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Snus plant and machinery - tobacco grinding, blending with water and salts, heat treatment, cooling, flavouring, portion pouching and can filling.
intro: Snus is a moist oral tobacco made by grinding tobacco to a flour, blending it with water, salt and alkaline salts, and heat-treating the mixture before flavouring and cooling. The finished snus is portioned into small pouches or filled loose into cans and held chilled. ART Mechatronics builds the grinding, mixing, heat-treatment, pouching and canning stages as one line.

blocks.text: Snus is a moist oral tobacco made by grinding tobacco to a flour, blending it with water, salt and alkaline salts, and heat-treating the mixture before flavouring and cooling. The finished snus is portioned into small pouches or filled loose into cans and held chilled. ART Mechatronics builds the grinding, mixing, heat-treatment, pouching and canning stages as one line.

blocks.title: Grinding to Tobacco Flour
desc: Cured tobacco is ground to a flour, which is the base of every snus recipe.
Ground material is sifted and moved under enclosed conveying to keep dust down.

blocks.title: Blending with Water & Salts
desc: Tobacco flour is blended with water, salt and alkaline salts against a set recipe.
Ingredients are weighed and dosed into the mixer under recipe control.

blocks.title: Heat Treatment
desc: The wet blend is heat-treated with steam, the step that separates snus from air-cured oral tobaccos.
It is run as a batch process in jacketed equipment fed by the plant's steam circuit.

blocks.title: Cooling & Flavouring
desc: The treated mass is cooled, and flavouring is folded in afterwards so the aroma is not driven off by heat.
Cooled batches are held until the pouching line calls for them.

blocks.title: Portion Pouching
desc: Portion snus is dosed into small oral pouches, which are sealed, counted and stacked ready for canning.
Loose snus skips this stage and goes straight to can filling.

blocks.title: Can Filling, Coding & Chilled Storage
desc: Pouches or loose snus are filled into cans, which are then labelled and coded.
Finished cans are weight-checked and moved into chilled storage.

metaDesc: Snuff plant and machinery - leaf drying, fine grinding, sieving and grading, scenting, maturation and tin or sachet packing, with dust collection.
intro: Snuff is a dry powdered tobacco made by ageing and drying cured leaf, then grinding it to a fine powder and sieving it to a consistent particle size. The powder is scented, allowed to mature and filled into tins, sachets or small containers. ART Mechatronics builds the drying, fine-grinding, sieving, blending and packing sections, with dust collection across the line.

blocks.text: Snuff is a dry powdered tobacco made by ageing and drying cured leaf, then grinding it to a fine powder and sieving it to a consistent particle size. The powder is scented, allowed to mature and filled into tins, sachets or small containers. ART Mechatronics builds the drying, fine-grinding, sieving, blending and packing sections, with dust collection across the line.

blocks.title: Leaf Conditioning & Ageing
desc: Cured leaf is opened out, de-stemmed and held to age, which is what develops the character of snuff.
Batches move through the ageing area in bins and trolleys.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Aged leaf is dried down before grinding, since snuff is a dry powder and damp leaf will not mill cleanly.
Moisture is checked on the batch before it is released to the mill.

blocks.title: Fine Grinding
desc: Dried leaf is ground to a fine powder, the defining step for snuff.
Grinding is enclosed and vented because the powder is very light.

blocks.title: Sieving & Grading
desc: The ground powder is sieved and classified so the fineness stays consistent from batch to batch.
Oversize is returned to the mill.

blocks.title: Scenting & Maturation
desc: Scents and flavour oils are blended through the powder, and the blend is then left to mature.
Blending is kept gentle so the powder is not compacted.

blocks.title: Filling & Packing
desc: Matured snuff is dosed into tins, sachets or small containers, sealed and coded.
Filled packs pass metal detection before they are cartoned.

blocks.title: Dust Control Across the Line
desc: Snuff is handled as a fine powder throughout, so extraction points are taken at the mill, sifter, mixer and filler.
Collected dust is returned or disposed of according to the plant's own procedure.

blocks.title: Leaf Drying & Conditioning

h1: Turmeric Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Turmeric Processing Plant & Machinery | Turnkey Turmeric Line by ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Turmeric processing plant and machinery: washing, boiling and curing, drying, polishing, grading, grinding and packing systems supplied by ART Mechatronics.
intro: Turmeric processing converts freshly harvested rhizomes into dried fingers, polished bulbs and fine turmeric powder. The rhizomes are washed, boiled or cured, dried, and polished to remove the wrinkled outer skin, then graded and ground. ART Mechatronics supplies plant and machinery for turmeric washing, curing, drying, polishing, grinding, sieving and packing.

blocks.text: Turmeric processing converts freshly harvested rhizomes into dried fingers, polished bulbs and fine turmeric powder. The rhizomes are washed, boiled or cured, dried, and polished to remove the wrinkled outer skin, then graded and ground. ART Mechatronics supplies plant and machinery for turmeric washing, curing, drying, polishing, grinding, sieving and packing.

blocks.title: Washing & Sorting
desc: Harvested rhizomes are fed from a hopper and washed to remove field soil, loose roots and stones.
Damaged fingers and foreign matter are taken out before the material goes for curing.

blocks.title: Boiling & Curing
desc: Cleaned rhizomes are boiled or steamed until they soften, which gelatinises the starch and spreads the colour evenly through the finger.
Curing also shortens the drying time and gives the cooked aroma associated with turmeric.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Cured rhizomes are dried in warm air until the moisture is low enough for storage and milling.
Even drying prevents case hardening, where the outside sets hard while the core stays wet.

blocks.title: Polishing & Grading
desc: Dried fingers are polished so the rough outer skin is rubbed away and the smooth, bright surface buyers look for is exposed.
Polished turmeric is then graded by size and separated by colour.

blocks.title: Grinding & Sieving
desc: Polished fingers are milled into turmeric powder, with the mill kept under extraction because the powder is fine and strongly staining.
Sieving returns oversize particles to the mill so the finished mesh stays consistent.

blocks.title: Packing
desc: Powder is filled into consumer pouches or bulk bags, coded and passed through metal detection before dispatch.

metaDesc: Chilli processing plant and machinery: de-stemming, cleaning, colour sorting, flake making, dust-controlled grinding and packing from ART Mechatronics.
intro: Chilli processing turns dried red chilli pods into flakes, coarse chilli powder and fine ground chilli. Pods are de-stemmed, cleaned of stones and dust, colour sorted, then crushed and ground under enclosed extraction because chilli dust is pungent and irritating to handle. ART Mechatronics supplies cleaning, de-stemming, grinding, sieving and packing machinery for chilli plants.

blocks.text: Chilli processing turns dried red chilli pods into flakes, coarse chilli powder and fine ground chilli. Pods are de-stemmed, cleaned of stones and dust, colour sorted, then crushed and ground under enclosed extraction because chilli dust is pungent and irritating to handle. ART Mechatronics supplies cleaning, de-stemming, grinding, sieving and packing machinery for chilli plants.

blocks.title: De-Stemming & Pre-Cleaning
desc: Stalks are broken off the dried pods and the loose calyx, dust and field debris are screened away.
Stones and mud balls are removed before the pods reach any cutting equipment.

blocks.title: Colour Sorting & Grading
desc: Discoloured, blackened and mould-marked pods are rejected optically, since chilli is bought largely on colour.
Sound pods are graded so each variety and size runs as its own batch.

blocks.title: Crushing & Flake Making
desc: Pods are broken into flakes and the seed fraction is separated from the pod wall.
Seed can be held back, reduced or added again depending on the pungency and colour the buyer has specified.

blocks.title: Grinding Under Dust Control
desc: Flakes are milled to powder in a closed circuit, with the airborne fraction drawn off and recovered rather than released into the room.
Enclosed handling protects operators from capsaicin-laden dust and keeps the powder off the plant floor.

blocks.title: Sieving & Inspection
desc: Ground chilli is sifted to the ordered mesh and passed over magnets to catch tramp metal from the mill.

blocks.title: Packing
desc: Flakes and powder are weighed into pouches, coded, weight checked and cased for despatch.

blocks.title: Seed Cleaning
desc: Incoming seed is screened to take out straw, dust and undersize, then passed over a de-stoner and gravity separator so stones and light chaff leave the stream.
Magnets catch tramp metal picked up during threshing and transport.

blocks.title: Grading & Sorting

Grading keeps whole-seed lots uniform, which matters for buyers who sell coriander unmilled.

The loosened husk is drawn off by aspiration so it does not carry through to the mill.

blocks.title: Grinding & Sifting
desc: Seed is milled to the required mesh and the sifter returns oversize to the mill until the whole batch passes.
The powder is separated from the conveying air in a cyclone before it reaches the packing floor.

intro: Pepper processing converts harvested pepper berries into whole black pepper and ground pepper. ART Mechatronics supplies washing, blanching, drying, cleaning, grading, grinding and packing machinery for pepper processing plants.

blocks.text: Pepper processing converts harvested pepper berries into whole black pepper and ground pepper. blocks.title: Washing & Blanching
desc: Berries are washed clear of stalk, leaf and field dirt, then dipped in hot water.
Blanching loosens the skin and helps the berry blacken evenly during drying instead of drying patchy.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Blanched berries are dried in warm air until the skin shrinks and wrinkles and the moisture is safe for storage.
Moisture is checked through the run so batches are neither over-dried nor left prone to mould.

blocks.title: Cleaning & Density Separation
desc: Light pinheads, dust and stalk pieces are aspirated away and stones are taken out on a de-stoner.
Gravity separation splits heavy sound berries from light ones, which is how bulk density grades are made.

blocks.title: Steam Sterilisation
desc: Whole pepper is steam treated to reduce the microbial load carried in from open field drying.
The treated berries are dried back down before they go anywhere near the mill.

blocks.title: Grinding
desc: Whole pepper is milled to table grind, restaurant grind or fine powder and sifted to the ordered mesh.
Closed conveying keeps the volatile aroma in the product rather than in the room.

blocks.title: Filling & Packing
desc: Whole and ground pepper are filled into bottles, jars or pouches, capped, labelled and coded.

blocks.text: Mango processing in the spice trade produces amchur, the sour powder made from unripe green mango. The fruit is washed, peeled, de-stoned and cut into thin slices, the slices are dried until brittle, and the dried slices are milled into a pale, acidic powder. ART Mechatronics supplies washing, peeling, slicing, drying, grinding and packing machinery for amchur plants.

blocks.title: Washing & Peeling
desc: Raw green mangoes are washed and rinsed to remove latex, dust and spray residue.
The skin is removed, since peel left on darkens the finished powder.

blocks.title: De-Stoning & Slicing
desc: The stone is separated from the flesh and the flesh is cut into thin, even slices.
Uniform slice thickness is what allows the whole load to dry at the same rate.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Slices are dried in warm air until they are brittle enough to snap and to mill cleanly.
Air is dehumidified so the load keeps losing moisture instead of stalling at high humidity.

blocks.title: Milling & Sifting
desc: Dried slices are milled to amchur powder and sifted to a uniform mesh.
Oversize and fibrous pieces are returned to the mill rather than passed on.

blocks.title: Packing
desc: Amchur draws moisture from the air, so it is filled and sealed promptly in barrier pouches.
Filled packs are metal checked and coded before casing.

desc: Incoming seed is fed at a controlled rate and screened free of straw, dust and undersize.

blocks.title: Roasting & Grinding
desc: For roasted cumin powder the seed is roasted first to develop the aroma, then cooled before it goes to the mill.
Cumin seed carries oil, so it is milled in stages with sieving between them to keep the powder free flowing.

h1: Cinnamon Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Cinnamon Processing Plant & Machinery | Turnkey Cinnamon Line by ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Cinnamon processing plant and machinery: bark cleaning, cutting and chipping, staged milling, classification and packing from ART Mechatronics.
intro: Cinnamon processing works with the dried inner bark of the cinnamon tree, which reaches the plant as quills, quillings or broken bark. The bark is cleaned, cut into short chips, milled in stages because it is fibrous and hard, then sieved and packed as quills, chips or powder. ART Mechatronics supplies cutting, grinding, sieving and packing machinery for cinnamon.

blocks.text: Cinnamon processing works with the dried inner bark of the cinnamon tree, which reaches the plant as quills, quillings or broken bark. The bark is cleaned, cut into short chips, milled in stages because it is fibrous and hard, then sieved and packed as quills, chips or powder. ART Mechatronics supplies cutting, grinding, sieving and packing machinery for cinnamon.

blocks.title: Cleaning & Inspection
desc: Quills and bark pieces are inspected and cleaned of dust, mould-marked bark and foreign matter.
Magnets remove tramp metal introduced during baling and transport.

blocks.title: Cutting & Chipping
desc: Quills are cut to short lengths and chipped, because whole rolled bark cannot be fed straight into a fine mill.
Cut size is kept even so the mill downstream is loaded steadily.

blocks.title: Coarse Milling
desc: Chips are reduced to a coarse meal in a first milling pass that breaks down the fibrous bark structure.
The mill runs under extraction, with the light fraction recovered in a cyclone.

blocks.title: Fine Grinding & Classification
desc: The coarse meal is ground to powder and classified so only on-specification particles leave the circuit.
Coarse and fibrous material is recirculated rather than allowed through to packing.

blocks.text: Clove processing handles the unopened flower buds of the clove tree, which arrive from the field with stalks still attached. blocks.title: De-Stemming & Winnowing
desc: Clove stalks are separated from the buds, since stalk sold as clove is an adulteration buyers test for.
Light stalk pieces and leaf are blown clear of the heavier buds.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Buds are dried in warm air until they darken and become brittle.
Even drying avoids the pale, soft buds that are downgraded on arrival.

blocks.title: Cleaning & Grading

Optical sorting removes off-colour and mould-marked buds before grading by size.

blocks.title: Milling

The powder is collected through a cyclone and filter so the aroma-carrying fines are recovered.

blocks.title: Packing

blocks.text: Cardamom processing turns freshly harvested green capsules into cured, graded cardamom and ground cardamom. blocks.title: Washing & Preparation
desc: Freshly picked capsules are washed and rinsed clear of field soil and leaf.
Loose stalk and immature capsules are taken out before curing begins.

blocks.title: Curing & Drying
desc: Capsules are cured in warm air, which dries them while holding the green colour buyers look for.
Air is dehumidified so drying continues steadily without scorching the capsule wall.

blocks.title: Polishing
desc: Cured capsules are polished to rub off the remaining calyx, stalk ends and surface residue.
The rubbed-off dust is drawn away so it does not settle back on the capsules.

blocks.title: Grading & Sorting
desc: Capsules are graded by size, which is how bold cardamom lots are made up, and separated by colour.
Shrivelled, split and discoloured capsules are rejected.

blocks.title: Milling
desc: Cardamom is milled either as the whole capsule or as seed after the husk has been separated.
Milling is kept short and sifted, because the seed is oily and the aroma is volatile.

blocks.title: Packing
desc: Whole capsules and ground cardamom are packed in tins, canisters or vacuum packs and labelled.

blocks.title: Washing & De-Watering
desc: Cut herb is washed and rinsed to remove field soil, grit and insects.

blocks.text: Paprika processing turns sweet, low-pungency red pepper pods into the deep red powder used for colour and mild flavour. Pods are washed, the stalks and seeds removed, dried, colour sorted, then milled, with the seed fraction blended back in a controlled proportion to set the shade. ART Mechatronics supplies washing, seed removal, drying, sorting, grinding and packing machinery for paprika.

blocks.title: Washing & Stem Removal
desc: Pods are washed clear of soil and dust and the stalks and calyx are taken off.
Split, blemished and immature pods are removed at the same point.

blocks.title: Seed & Rib Separation
desc: Seeds and the inner ribs are separated from the pod wall, as they carry less colour than the flesh.
The seed fraction is kept aside so it can be reintroduced only in the proportion the recipe calls for.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Pod wall and seed are dried separately in warm air until they are brittle enough to mill.
Moisture is monitored, because over-drying dulls the colour that paprika is bought for.

blocks.title: Colour Sorting
desc: Scorched, browned and discoloured pieces are rejected optically before anything reaches the mill.
Sorting at this point is what allows a consistent shade to be held from batch to batch.

blocks.title: Milling & Shade Blending
desc: Pod and seed fractions are milled separately and then blended back to the shade and pungency ordered.
The blend is sieved so the finished powder is even in both particle size and colour.

blocks.title: Packing
desc: Paprika is filled into pouches or doypacks, weight checked and coded; nitrogen flushing is used where colour has to be held in storage.

metaDesc: Food flavour processing plant and machinery from ART Mechatronics - emulsion preparation, spray drying, dry blending, sieving, dust control and sachet packing.
intro: Food flavour processing turns oleoresins, essential oils, spice extracts and dry carriers into free-flowing seasoning powders for snack, beverage, ready-meal and retail brands. Liquid flavour is emulsified with a carrier and spray dried, or dry blended with salt, sugar and spice, then sieved, mixed to an even batch and packed. blocks.text: Food flavour processing turns oleoresins, essential oils, spice extracts and dry carriers into free-flowing seasoning powders for snack, beverage, ready-meal and retail brands. Liquid flavour is emulsified with a carrier and spray dried, or dry blended with salt, sugar and spice, then sieved, mixed to an even batch and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies plant and machinery for each stage.

blocks.title: Raw Material Intake & Weighing
desc: Liquid flavour concentrates, dry carriers, salt and spice powders are received, checked and weighed out to the batch recipe.
Weighing is the stage that decides whether one batch tastes like the last one.

blocks.title: Emulsion Preparation
desc: Liquid flavour is dispersed into a carrier solution and worked down to a fine, stable emulsion before it goes to the dryer.
An emulsion that separates in the feed tank produces powder with flavour spread unevenly through it.

blocks.title: Spray Drying
desc: The emulsion is atomised into a hot air stream so that the water evaporates and the flavour is left held inside dry carrier particles.
Fines carried out with the exhaust air are taken to the cyclone and filter section rather than to atmosphere.

blocks.title: Dry Blending
desc: Spray dried flavour is blended with salt, sugar, MSG and ground spice to build the finished seasoning recipe.
Blending is kept gentle so that the dried flavour particles are not broken open in the mixer.

blocks.title: Sieving & Lump Breaking
desc: The blend is sieved to break up lumps and take out agglomerates formed during drying and mixing.
Foreign body checks are made here, before the powder is released to packing.

blocks.title: Packing & Coding
desc: Finished flavour powder is filled into sachets, pouches or bulk packs, sealed, coded and check weighed.
Filling is kept enclosed and barrier film is used, because flavour powders are open to air and moisture until the pack is sealed.

blocks.text: Salt processing converts raw solar, rock or brine derived salt into clean, graded edible and industrial salt. The salt is washed to take out sand and insoluble matter, crushed and screened to crystal size, dried, dosed with iodine and free flow additives, then blended and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies plant and machinery for each stage.

blocks.title: Raw Salt Intake & Washing
desc: Raw salt arrives carrying sand, clay and other insoluble matter, which is washed out with saturated brine.
The washed salt is drained and carried forward for size reduction.

blocks.title: Crushing & Sizing
desc: Lumps are broken down and the salt is screened into the crystal sizes used for table, food grade and industrial salt.
Oversize goes back to the crusher and the fines are drawn off separately.

blocks.title: Drying & Cooling
desc: Washed salt still holds surface moisture, which is driven off in a hot air dryer before any additive is applied.
The salt is cooled after drying so that moisture does not settle back into the crystal bed.

blocks.title: Iodisation & Additive Dosing
desc: Iodine solution and free flow or anti caking agents are dosed onto the dried salt and worked through the bed.
Iodine is dosed steadily and worked through the whole batch rather than added at one point in the bed.

blocks.title: Storage & Final Screening
desc: Treated salt is held in silos and given a final screen before packing to remove lumps formed in storage.
Salt draws moisture from the air, so storage and transfer are kept enclosed.

blocks.title: Packing
desc: Salt is filled into consumer pouches, jars or bulk sacks, then weighed, sealed and stitched or coded as the pack calls for.
Retail packs are check weighed and inspected before they go into cartons.

blocks.text: Sugar processing takes crystal sugar and works it into the grades food manufacturers buy: granulated, caster, icing and cube. The crystal is cleaned of tramp metal, conditioned, milled to the fineness required, sieved into grades, blended or pressed into cubes and packed, with dust extraction on every transfer point. ART Mechatronics supplies plant and machinery for each stage.

blocks.title: Intake & Cleaning
desc: Crystal sugar is tipped, screened for lumps and passed over magnets to take out tramp metal picked up in handling and transport.
Transfer is kept enclosed so the sugar stays dry and the dust stays inside the plant.

blocks.title: Conditioning & Drying
desc: Sugar that has picked up moisture is dried and cooled so that it grinds cleanly instead of caking inside the mill.
Dry air is supplied to the handling area to keep humidity away from the open product.

blocks.title: Grinding to Caster & Icing Grades
desc: Granulated sugar is milled down to caster and icing fineness, with the mill chosen to suit the grade being made.
Sugar dust is combustible, so grinding is run with dust collection connected directly to the mill.

blocks.title: Sieving & Grading
desc: Milled sugar is separated into grades and the oversize is returned for regrinding.
The particle spread set here is what decides how the sugar dissolves and how it behaves in a dry blend.

blocks.title: Blending & Cube Forming
desc: Icing sugar is blended with an anti caking agent, while cube lines press dampened sugar and cut it to shape.
Formed cubes are dried and cooled before they are collated for packing.

blocks.title: Dust Control
desc: Mills, transfer points and packing machines are put under suction so that airborne sugar dust is captured where it is created.
Collected fines are discharged through a controlled point instead of settling across the plant.

blocks.title: Packing
desc: Finished sugar is filled into sachets, sticks, pouches or sacks, then sealed and coded.
Retail packs are cartoned for despatch, while bulk grades go straight into sacks.

blocks.text: MSG, or monosodium glutamate, is produced by fermenting a starch or molasses feedstock and then recovering the glutamate as a crystal. The broth is separated and crystallised, and the crystal is dried, screened into mesh grades, milled where a powder is wanted, then blended and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies plant and machinery for each stage.

blocks.title: Broth Handling & Separation
desc: Fermented broth is held, kept moving and separated so that cell mass and insoluble matter are taken out before crystallisation.
How cleanly this separation is done shows up later in the colour and clarity of the crystal.

blocks.title: Crystallisation
desc: The clarified liquor is concentrated under vacuum and then cooled, so that glutamate crystals form and grow.
Mother liquor is drawn off for recovery and a wet crystal cake is left behind.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Wet crystal is dried until the surface moisture is gone and the material runs freely again.
Carry over from the dryer is collected in the cyclone rather than allowed into the room.

blocks.title: Screening & Crystal Grading
desc: Dried crystal is screened into the mesh grades the trade asks for, from coarse crystal down to fine.
Oversize is diverted to milling and the fines are collected on their own.

blocks.title: Milling to Powder Grades
desc: Where a powder grade is called for, crystal is milled and classified to the fineness the buyer has specified.
Milling runs enclosed so that the powder does not take up moisture from the room.

blocks.title: Blending
desc: Graded crystal or powder is blended to an even batch, and mixed with salt or other carriers where a seasoning base is being made.
Charging is kept enclosed to keep foreign matter out of the blend.

blocks.title: Packing & Inspection
desc: MSG is filled into pouches, jars or bulk sacks, then sealed and coded.
Sealed packs are inspected for metal or foreign bodies before they are cased.

blocks.text: Penne processing turns durum wheat semolina into short, tube-shaped pasta cut at an angle at both ends. blocks.title: Semolina Intake & Sifting
desc: Bagged or bulk semolina is tipped, screened and passed over magnets before it reaches the dough system.
Removing foreign matter and lumps at intake protects the extruder dies further down the line.

blocks.title: Dough Mixing
desc: Semolina and water are dosed to a set recipe and worked into a stiff, crumbly dough.
Penne needs a firm dough so the tube walls hold their shape after the die.

blocks.title: Extrusion & Angle Cutting

The angled ends are produced by a knife cutting across the extrudate at the die face.

blocks.title: Drying & Cooling

Uneven drying is what causes cracking and breakage in short-cut pasta.

blocks.title: Weighing & Packing

The flour is sifted and weighed, mixed with water into a crumbly dough, extruded through a helical die that twists the strand, cut to length, then dried in stages and packed. blocks.title: Flour Handling & Dosing
desc: Semolina is drawn from storage, lifted, screened and dosed into the mixer against the recipe.

blocks.title: Dough Mixing & Hydration
desc: Water is added to the semolina and the mass is worked until it is uniformly hydrated.
A consistent dough is what keeps the coil tight and even after extrusion.

blocks.title: Helical Extrusion & Cutting
desc: The dough passes through a die that imparts the corkscrew twist, and the twisted strand is cut to short lengths as it leaves the die face.

blocks.title: Staged Drying

Air humidity is managed alongside temperature during the hold stages.

intro: Fusilli is a spiral pasta made from durum semolina, formed by extruding dough through a die that gives the strand its twist before it is cut short. blocks.text: Fusilli is a spiral pasta made from durum semolina, formed by extruding dough through a die that gives the strand its twist before it is cut short. The cut spirals are shaken loose, dried slowly to avoid cracking, cooled and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies dough mixing, extrusion, shaping, drying and packaging equipment for fusilli lines.

blocks.title: Raw Material Preparation
desc: Semolina is tipped, screened for foreign matter and conveyed to the mixing station under dust control.

blocks.title: Mixing & Kneading
desc: Semolina and water are combined and kneaded into a plastic dough suitable for a shaped die.
Recipe dosing is held to a fixed ratio so the spiral pitch stays consistent through the run.

blocks.title: Spiral Forming & Cutting
desc: The dough is extruded through a spiral-forming die and cut into short pieces, then separated so the freshly cut spirals do not stick to one another.

blocks.title: Slow Drying & Stabilisation
desc: Fusilli is spread on trays and dried slowly, then held so moisture equalises across the twisted section.
The thick and thin parts of a spiral dry at different rates, which is why the hold stage matters.

blocks.title: Potato Washing & Peeling
desc: Incoming potatoes are washed, stones and soil are separated out, and the skin is removed.
Gnocchi begins with a root crop, so the front of the line is a vegetable line rather than a flour line.

Macaroni is often made on refined flour rather than pure durum, so hydration is adjusted to the flour in use.

blocks.title: Dough Mixing

A sheet dough is kept softer than a short-cut pasta dough so it rolls without tearing.

blocks.title: Flat Drying

blocks.text: Ravioli is a filled pasta: a savoury filling is enclosed between two thin dough sheets, then sealed and cut into individual pockets. blocks.title: Filling Preparation & Cooling
desc: Cheese, vegetable or meat ingredients are size-reduced, cooked and blended into a filling, then cooled before it meets the dough.
A warm filling would soften the sheet and break the seal, so the filling is chilled first.

blocks.title: Dough Mixing & Sheeting
desc: A separate dough is mixed and formed into two thin, even sheets, one for the base and one for the cover.

blocks.title: Depositing, Sealing & Cutting
desc: Filling is deposited at fixed intervals on the base sheet, the cover sheet is laid over it, and the pockets are pressed, sealed and cut apart.
Seal integrity decides whether the ravioli survives boiling without bursting.

blocks.title: Freezing

blocks.title: Extrusion & Spreading
desc: Dough is extruded through a fine round die and the continuous strands are draped over sticks that carry them through the plant.

Drying too fast leaves the strands brittle and they snap during handling.

blocks.title: Flour Blending & Dough Mixing
desc: Flour is sifted and blended with water, salt and alkaline salts, then mixed to a crumbly dough.
The alkaline solution is what gives chowmein noodles their springy bite and colour.

blocks.title: Sheeting & Slitting

blocks.title: Steaming

Pre-cooking at this stage is what allows the finished noodle to be stir-fried directly.

Handling is kept gentle through the dryer because thin strands break easily.

Plain vermicelli skips this step and moves straight to packing.

metaTitle: Walnut Processing Plant & Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Walnut processing plant machinery for hulling, washing, in-shell drying, cracking, shell and kernel separation, colour sorting and packing of walnut halves and pieces.
intro: Walnut processing takes freshly harvested in-hull nuts and turns them into graded kernels for retail packs and food manufacturing. The green hull is stripped off, the in-shell nuts are washed and dried, the shell is cracked and separated from the kernel, and the halves and pieces are graded by size and colour before hygienic packing.

blocks.text: Walnut processing takes freshly harvested in-hull nuts and turns them into graded kernels for retail packs and food manufacturing. The green hull is stripped off, the in-shell nuts are washed and dried, the shell is cracked and separated from the kernel, and the halves and pieces are graded by size and colour before hygienic packing.

blocks.title: Hulling & Washing
desc: The green outer hull is stripped from the freshly harvested nut and the in-shell walnuts are washed to remove hull residue, field soil and stones.
Clean shells dry more evenly and carry less staining onto the kernel.

blocks.title: In-Shell Drying
desc: The washed nuts are dried in warm air until shell and kernel reach a stable storage condition.
Drying holds off mould growth and loosens the kernel inside the shell ahead of cracking.

blocks.title: Sizing & Cracking
desc: Dried nuts are graded into size bands so the cracking gap can be matched to each band, and the shell is then broken open.
Sizing before cracking is what keeps whole halves intact instead of shattering them.

blocks.title: Shell & Kernel Separation
desc: The cracked mixture is separated so that shell fragments, light dust and unfilled nuts are drawn away from the kernel.
Air and density separation handle the bulk of this before any hand inspection.

blocks.title: Kernel Grading & Colour Sorting
desc: Kernels are separated into halves, quarters and pieces, then sorted by colour, since walnut trade grades run from light through to amber.
Optical and camera sorting take out shell fragments, shrivelled kernel and discoloured pieces.

blocks.title: Inspection & Packing
desc: Graded kernels pass metal and X-ray inspection, are weighed to pack size and filled into pouches or cartons.
Walnut kernel is high in oil, so gas-flushed and sealed formats are commonly specified for export packs.

metaDesc: Pecan processing plant machinery for in-shell cleaning, moisture conditioning, cracking, shell separation, drying back, sizing and packing of pecan halves and pieces.
intro: Pecan processing converts in-shell nuts into whole halves and pieces for bakery, confectionery and retail packs. Hull fragments and field debris are cleaned away, the nuts are conditioned with moisture so the kernel does not shatter, the shell is cracked and separated, and the kernels are then dried back, sized, sorted and packed.

blocks.text: Pecan processing converts in-shell nuts into whole halves and pieces for bakery, confectionery and retail packs. Hull fragments and field debris are cleaned away, the nuts are conditioned with moisture so the kernel does not shatter, the shell is cracked and separated, and the kernels are then dried back, sized, sorted and packed.

blocks.title: In-Shell Cleaning & Sizing
desc: Sticks, hull fragments, stones and light material are removed from the in-shell lot, which is then separated into size bands.
Cracking equipment is set band by band, so sizing comes before it rather than after.

blocks.title: Conditioning
desc: The in-shell nuts are wetted or steam-conditioned so the kernel takes up a little moisture and turns pliable.
A conditioned kernel flexes as the shell breaks instead of fracturing into small pieces, which is what protects the halves yield.

blocks.title: Cracking & Shelling
desc: The conditioned shell is cracked and then broken away from the kernel.
Pecan shell is thin and splinters readily, so shelling and fragment extraction run together with dust pick-up on the line.

blocks.title: Shell Separation
desc: Shell, mid-piece and kernel are separated by weight and by air flow, and the light shell fraction is drawn off.
What carries forward is a stream of halves and pieces with the bulk of the shell already removed.

blocks.title: Drying Back & Sizing
desc: The moisture added at conditioning is dried out again so the kernel is crisp, and the kernels are sized into halves and piece grades.
Halves are moved gently through this stage to avoid breaking the grade that has just been protected.

blocks.title: Sorting, Inspection & Packing
desc: Colour sorting and camera inspection remove shell fragments and dark kernel before the product is weighed and packed.
Bulk cartons for industry and sealed retail pouches are both run from the same finishing line.

intro: Hazelnut processing turns harvested in-shell nuts into raw kernel, blanched kernel, chopped hazelnut and paste. The husk is removed and the nuts are dried, cracked and separated from the shell; kernels are then roasted so the brown skin loosens, blanched, sorted, and either packed whole or cut and milled for bakery and confectionery buyers.

blocks.text: Hazelnut processing turns harvested in-shell nuts into raw kernel, blanched kernel, chopped hazelnut and paste. The husk is removed and the nuts are dried, cracked and separated from the shell; kernels are then roasted so the brown skin loosens, blanched, sorted, and either packed whole or cut and milled for bakery and confectionery buyers.

blocks.title: Husking & Drying
desc: The papery husk left after harvest is removed and the in-shell nuts are dried in warm air to a stable storage condition.
Drying protects the crop through storage and prepares the shell for cracking.

blocks.title: Sizing, Cracking & Shell Separation
desc: Nuts are graded into size bands and cracked band by band, after which shell and kernel are parted by air and density.
Hazelnut shell is brittle and light, so aspiration carries most of it away from the kernel stream.

blocks.title: Roasting
desc: Kernels are roasted in hot air, which develops flavour and dries and loosens the brown skin covering the kernel.
Roasted kernel is cooled before it moves on so it does not carry heat into the next stage.

blocks.title: Blanching & Skin Removal
desc: The loosened skin is rubbed off the kernel and the skin flakes are drawn away by suction.
Blanched kernel is the form most confectionery and bakery buyers specify.

blocks.title: Sorting & Inspection
desc: Kernels are sorted by colour and inspected for shell fragments, mouldy and shrivelled kernel and foreign matter.
Metal and X-ray checks run on the same line before the product is released to packing.

blocks.title: Cutting, Milling & Packing
desc: Part of the kernel is chopped or diced and part is milled into hazelnut meal and paste for industrial buyers, while the rest is packed whole.
Each stream is weighed, filled, coded and cased on the same finishing line.

blocks.text: Macadamia processing removes the green husk, dries the nut-in-shell in stages, cracks the thick hard shell and separates kernel from shell by density. Kernels are then graded into whole and half styles, colour sorted, roasted or left raw, and packed in sealed barrier formats because the kernel is high in oil.

blocks.title: Husking & Pre-Sorting
desc: The green husk is removed soon after harvest and immature, light and damaged nuts are taken out of the lot.
Husk left sitting on the nut holds moisture against the shell, so it is stripped before drying begins.

blocks.title: Staged Nut-In-Shell Drying
desc: Nut-in-shell is dried in stages, moving from ambient air through to warm air, so the kernel shrinks away from the inside of the shell.
A kernel that has pulled clear of the shell releases whole when the nut is cracked.

blocks.title: Sizing & Cracking
desc: Dried nuts are separated into size bands and fed to the cracker band by band, because the shell is thick and hard and the setting has to match the nut.
The output of this stage is a mixture of kernel, half shells and shell grit.

blocks.title: Kernel & Shell Separation
desc: Kernel and shell are separated by density and by air flow, and the shell fraction is collected separately for fuel and other uses.
Fine shell dust is drawn off at the same point rather than travelling with the kernel.

blocks.title: Kernel Grading & Sorting
desc: Kernels are graded into whole, half and piece styles and sorted by colour, with discoloured and immature kernel removed.
Camera and X-ray inspection catch shell that has travelled through with the kernel.

blocks.title: Roasting, Coating & Packing
desc: Kernel may be roasted and salted or coated before packing, or packed raw for industrial buyers.
Macadamia kernel is high in oil, so vacuum and gas-flushed packs are the usual export formats.

blocks.text: Pine nut processing extracts the seed from the pine cone, removes the hard seed shell and the thin inner skin, and grades the kernel for retail and food service. Cones are dried until the scales open, seeds are separated from cone debris, and the kernel is then shelled, peeled, dried gently, colour sorted and sealed.

blocks.title: Cone Drying & Seed Extraction
desc: Harvested cones are dried until the scales open and the seeds can be shaken free and separated out.
Cone scales, resin and stalk waste leave with the seed stream and are removed on the same pass.

blocks.title: Cleaning & Empty Seed Removal

Empty seed taken out here does not travel through the rest of the line or dilute the shelling yield.

Pine nut kernel is small and soft, so the handling through this stage is deliberately gentle.

Skin flakes and dust are drawn away by suction as they are released.

blocks.title: Sorting & Packing

Nuts are cured and washed, graded, peeled of shell and inner pellicle with steam, sorted, and then frozen for whole kernel or dried and milled into chestnut flour.

blocks.title: Curing & Washing
desc: Freshly harvested chestnuts are cured in water and washed, which lifts off field soil and floats away hollow and insect-damaged nuts.
Chestnut carries far more moisture than other nuts and spoils quickly without this first step.

blocks.title: Surface Drying & Grading
desc: Surface water is taken off and the nuts are graded into size bands.
Peeling equipment is set to a size band, so grading has to come before peeling rather than after it.

blocks.title: Peeling
desc: The hard outer shell and the inner pellicle are loosened with steam or heat and then taken off.
The pellicle clings tightly to the kernel, so shell and skin are usually removed in two separate passes.

blocks.title: Sorting & Inspection
desc: Peeled kernels are colour sorted and camera inspected so that shell, skin and blemished kernel are removed before preservation.
This is the last point at which defects can be taken out while the kernel is still loose.

blocks.title: Freezing or Drying
desc: Peeled chestnut is either frozen for whole-kernel supply or dried for the flour route.
Both routes exist because chestnut cannot be held at ambient the way a dry nut can.

blocks.title: Milling & Packing
desc: Dried kernel is milled into chestnut flour and sifted to grade, while frozen whole kernel goes to sealed packs.
Finished packs are weighed, coded and cased for cold chain or ambient distribution.

intro: Fig processing turns fresh or field-dried figs into graded dried fruit for retail packs, bakery use and fig paste. Fruit is sorted and washed, dried down to a stable condition, then steam treated so it becomes pliable again, stems are trimmed, and the figs are sized and either packed whole or pressed into layer and block formats.

blocks.text: Fig processing turns fresh or field-dried figs into graded dried fruit for retail packs, bakery use and fig paste. Fruit is sorted and washed, dried down to a stable condition, then steam treated so it becomes pliable again, stems are trimmed, and the figs are sized and either packed whole or pressed into layer and block formats.

blocks.title: Reception, Sorting & Washing
desc: Incoming fruit is sorted to take out spoiled, split and insect-damaged figs, then washed to remove dust, sand and field debris.
Sorting at the front of the line keeps damaged fruit out of the dryers altogether.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Figs are dried in warm air until the flesh is firm and the moisture is stable for storage.
Controlled mechanical drying is used where open sun drying is not reliable or is not accepted for the grade.

blocks.title: Steam Treatment & Conditioning
desc: Dried figs are steam treated, which sanitises the fruit and at the same time softens it so it can be handled and shaped.
A fully dry fig cracks when it is worked, whereas a conditioned one flexes.

blocks.title: Stem Trimming & Grading
desc: Stems are trimmed and the fruit is graded by size, since fig trade grades are set by count and size.
Off-grade fruit is diverted here to the paste and bakery streams instead of being packed whole.

blocks.title: Forming, Pressing & Paste
desc: Figs going into layer and block packs are flattened and pressed to shape, while whole figs pass through untouched.
Diverted off-grade fruit is milled into fig paste for bakery and filling manufacturers.

blocks.title: Inspection & Packing
desc: Metal and X-ray inspection run before filling, and the fruit is packed into trays, pouches or cartons and coded.
Sealed and gas-flushed formats are used where a longer ambient shelf life is required.

blocks.text: Apricot processing turns fresh apricots into dried halves and diced fruit. Fruit is washed and graded, split along the seam and the stone removed, treated so the flesh holds its orange colour, then dried in warm air, sorted and sized; part of the crop is diced or sliced instead of being packed as whole halves.

blocks.title: Washing & Grading
desc: Fruit is washed to remove orchard dust and spray residue and graded by size, with soft and damaged fruit sorted out.
Even-sized fruit dries at the same rate, which is why grading is done before the fruit is cut.

blocks.title: Halving & Stone Removal
desc: Apricots are split along the natural seam and the stone is pushed out, leaving the two halves.
Stones are collected separately because apricot kernel is a saleable by-product rather than waste.

blocks.title: Colour Treatment
desc: The halves are treated before drying so the fruit keeps its orange colour; untreated apricot dries to a dark brown.
The treatment chamber is enclosed and vented, with extraction handling the fumes.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Halves are dried cut side up in warm air until the flesh is leathery and the moisture is stable for storage.
Air flow is kept even across the load so the trays dry to the same condition.

blocks.title: Sorting & Sizing
desc: Dried halves are colour sorted and graded into trade sizes, with broken and darkened fruit diverted.
Camera inspection removes stone fragments and stalk that survived the earlier stages.

blocks.title: Cutting & Packing
desc: Part of the crop is diced or sliced for bakery, cereal and confectionery buyers and the rest is packed as whole halves.
Packs are weighed, metal checked and sealed before casing.

blocks.text: Raisin processing turns grapes into dried fruit ready for retail and bakery use. Grapes are dipped so the waxy skin dries faster, dried down, then de-stemmed and de-capped, washed, de-stoned and separated from stalk and cap fragments by air, graded by size, lightly oiled so the fruit does not cake, and packed.

blocks.title: Dipping & Drying
desc: Bunches are dipped in a hot alkaline emulsion that breaks the waxy bloom on the grape skin, and the fruit is then dried.
Dipped grapes dry faster and more evenly than untreated fruit of the same size.

blocks.title: De-Stemming & Cap Removal
desc: Dried fruit is separated from the stalks and the cap stems are pulled off each berry.
Stalk and cap material is taken out here rather than being left to show up as a defect at the packing end.

blocks.title: Washing & Cleaning
desc: Raisins are washed to remove field dust, sand and sugar bloom, and stones and tramp metal are separated out.
The washed fruit is surface dried again before it moves on to grading.

blocks.title: Air Separation & Grading
desc: Light stalk, cap and skin fragments are drawn off by air and the fruit is graded into size bands.
Berries that have stuck together during drying are broken apart as they pass through.

blocks.title: Colour Sorting
desc: Colour sorting takes out unripe green berries, sugared and darkened fruit, stones and foreign matter.
Camera inspection follows to catch stalk and cap that came through the air stage.

blocks.title: Oiling & Packing
desc: A light food-grade oil is applied so the fruit stays loose in the pack instead of caking into a block.
The raisins are then weighed and filled into pouches, cartons or bulk cases and coded.

metaDesc: Cranberry processing plant machinery for berry cleaning, slicing, sugar syrup infusion, draining, tunnel drying, oiling and cooling, cluster screening and pouch packing.
intro: Cranberry processing makes sweetened dried cranberries from fresh or frozen berries. Berries are cleaned and sorted, sliced so syrup can enter the fruit, infused with sugar syrup, drained and dried in warm air, then lightly oiled so the pieces stay loose, cooled, screened for clusters and packed for cereal, bakery and snack buyers.

blocks.text: Cranberry processing makes sweetened dried cranberries from fresh or frozen berries. Berries are cleaned and sorted, sliced so syrup can enter the fruit, infused with sugar syrup, drained and dried in warm air, then lightly oiled so the pieces stay loose, cooled, screened for clusters and packed for cereal, bakery and snack buyers.

blocks.title: Cleaning & Sorting
desc: Incoming berries are washed and leaves, stems, vine and soft fruit are taken out.
Frozen fruit is tempered before it goes forward so it cuts cleanly rather than crushing.

blocks.title: Slicing
desc: Berries are sliced or scored so the skin is opened, because an intact cranberry skin resists syrup.
The cut style chosen here decides whether the finished fruit is halves, slices or whole-berry style.

blocks.title: Sugar Syrup Infusion
desc: Cut fruit is held in sugar syrup so that syrup moves into the fruit while juice moves out of it.
Infusion is the stage that turns a sharply sour berry into a sweetened dried fruit.

blocks.title: Draining & Drying
desc: Surplus syrup is drained off and recovered for reuse, and the infused fruit is dried in warm air until stable.
Drying is kept gentle because the sugar now carried in the fruit scorches easily.

blocks.title: Oiling & Cooling
desc: A light food-grade oil is tumbled onto the dried fruit so the sticky pieces stay separate, and the fruit is then cooled.
Warm sweetened fruit packed straight off the dryer sets into a block.

blocks.title: Inspection & Packing
desc: Clusters are broken up and screened out, metal inspection runs, and the fruit is weighed and filled.
Resealable retail pouches and bulk cases for industrial buyers are both run on the line.

metaDesc: Prune processing plant machinery for plum washing and grading, whole drying with the stone in, bulk holding, steam rehydration, pitting, X-ray checking and resealable packing.
intro: Prune processing dries plums whole and pits them afterwards. Fruit is washed and graded, dried in warm air until the flesh is firm, held in bulk storage, then rehydrated with hot water or steam so it is soft enough to pit without tearing; the pitted fruit is checked for stone fragments, inspected and packed.

blocks.text: Prune processing dries plums whole and pits them afterwards. Fruit is washed and graded, dried in warm air until the flesh is firm, held in bulk storage, then rehydrated with hot water or steam so it is soft enough to pit without tearing; the pitted fruit is checked for stone fragments, inspected and packed.

blocks.title: Reception, Washing & Grading
desc: Plums are washed and graded by size, and split, bruised and under-ripe fruit is removed.
Drying time follows fruit size, so grading is done before the fruit reaches the dryers.

blocks.title: Whole Drying
desc: Whole plums, with the stone still in place, are dried in warm air until the flesh is firm and will hold in storage.
Prunes are dried before they are pitted, which is the opposite order to apricot and most stone fruit.

blocks.title: Bulk Holding & Size Grading
desc: Dried prunes are held in bulk and graded by count and size ahead of the finishing line.
Bulk holding lets a whole season's crop be finished to order rather than packed at harvest.

blocks.title: Rehydration & Tenderising
desc: Graded fruit is treated with hot water or steam so it takes moisture back and turns pliable.
A fully dry prune tears on the pitter, while a conditioned one releases the stone cleanly.

blocks.title: Pitting
desc: The stone is pushed out of the softened fruit and collected separately, and the pitted fruit is checked for stones left behind.
Pit and pit fragments are the defect this stage is judged on, so inspection sits directly after it.

blocks.title: Inspection & Packing
desc: Metal inspection and weight checks run before filling, and the fruit is packed into resealable pouches, trays or cases.
Each pack is coded so the lot can be traced back through the finishing line.

intro: Oats processing turns harvested oats into groats, steel-cut grains and rolled flakes fit for milling and packing. Raw oats are cleaned, graded, dehulled and heat-treated to stabilise the groat, then cut or flaked before packing. ART Mechatronics supplies cleaning, dehulling, kilning, flaking and packing lines for oat mills producing flakes, groats and oat flour.

blocks.text: Oats processing turns harvested oats into groats, steel-cut grains and rolled flakes fit for milling and packing. Raw oats are cleaned, graded, dehulled and heat-treated to stabilise the groat, then cut or flaked before packing. ART Mechatronics supplies cleaning, dehulling, kilning, flaking and packing lines for oat mills producing flakes, groats and oat flour.

blocks.title: Intake & Pre-Cleaning
desc: Incoming oats are tipped, elevated and passed over screens and aspiration to take out straw, chaff, dust and tramp metal.
Cleaning at intake protects the hulling and milling machines further down the line.

blocks.title: Grading & De-Stoning
desc: Cleaned oats are sized and separated by density so thin grains, light seeds and stones are removed before hulling.
Uniform kernels hull more evenly and leave fewer unhulled grains in the groat stream.

blocks.title: Dehulling & Hull Aspiration
desc: The hull is cracked away from the groat and the light hulls are drawn off in an air stream.
Grain that comes through still covered is returned for a second pass.

blocks.title: Steaming & Kilning
desc: Groats are steamed and heat-treated to stabilise the grain and develop the roasted note associated with oats.
They are then cooled and held before flaking so the kernel is conditioned for rolling.

blocks.title: Cutting, Flaking & Milling
desc: Groats are cut into steel-cut pieces or passed through rolls to make flakes, and part of the stream can be ground into oat flour.
Sifting after each stage separates fines and out-of-size material.

blocks.title: Weighing, Packing & Inspection
desc: Flakes, groats or flour are weighed, filled into pouches or bags, coded and checked before palletising.
Metal detection and check-weighing sit in line ahead of the pallet.

blocks.text: Millet processing prepares small grains such as pearl, foxtail, kodo and little millet for food use by cleaning, de-stoning, dehusking and grading them. Because millet grains are small and arrive mixed with soil and grit, sizing and density separation matter more than they do in larger cereals. ART Mechatronics builds millet cleaning, hulling, polishing and flour milling lines.

blocks.title: Intake & Screen Cleaning
desc: Millet is fed at a controlled rate over graded screens that separate oversize trash from undersize dust and broken seed.
Magnets take out ferrous pieces picked up during threshing and transport.

blocks.title: De-Stoning & Density Separation
desc: Small stones and mud balls close in size to millet are separated on a fluidised deck by weight rather than by screen aperture.
Light and immature seed is drawn off in the same pass.

blocks.title: Dehusking & Husk Removal
desc: Husked millets are passed through hullers that strip the outer husk from the kernel.
Husk and bran fines are aspirated away so only whole kernels and brokens carry forward.

blocks.title: Polishing & Grading
desc: Kernels are polished to remove the loose bran layer where a polished grade is required, and unpolished stock bypasses this stage.
Graded kernels are then sorted to take out discoloured and defective seed.

blocks.title: Flour Milling & Sifting
desc: Part of the kernel stream is ground into millet flour and sifted into the granulation the buyer asks for.
Dust generated during grinding is collected at source.

blocks.title: Packing of Grain & Flour
desc: Whole millet and millet flour are weighed and filled into retail pouches or bulk bags, then coded and inspected.

blocks.title: Seed Intake & Cleaning
desc: Field-run quinoa is screened to remove stalk, chaff, soil and stones before any saponin work begins.
Ferrous contamination is taken out at the same point.

blocks.title: Grading & Density Separation
desc: Seed is graded to size and separated by density so light, immature seed and weed seed leave the stream.
Even-sized seed scours more consistently in the next stage.

blocks.title: Saponin Removal by Scouring & Washing
desc: The saponin-bearing outer layer is abraded off dry, and a water wash follows where a fully de-bittered grade is wanted.
This is the stage that distinguishes a quinoa line from an ordinary grain cleaning plant.

blocks.title: Drying & Cooling
desc: Washed seed is dried back to a storable condition and cooled before it goes to sorting.
Moisture is checked on the line so the seed is neither over-dried nor left damp.

blocks.title: Optical Sorting & Inspection
desc: Dried seed is colour sorted to take out dark, stained and foreign seed, with rejects diverted automatically.
Metal detection runs ahead of packing.

blocks.title: Retail & Bulk Packing
desc: Sorted quinoa is weighed and filled into resealable retail packs or bulk bags, coded and cartoned.

blocks.text: Barley processing turns field barley into pearl barley, flakes, flour and malting-grade grain. The crop is cleaned and graded, then pearled so the husk and outer bran layers are abraded away, or steeped and germinated where malt is the product. Pearled and flaked barley is dried, sized and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies barley cleaning, pearling, flaking and packing plants.

blocks.title: Intake & Cleaning
desc: Barley is tipped into a receiving hopper, fed forward at a steady rate and cleaned of straw, awns, chaff and dust on screens and aspiration.
Magnetic separation removes ferrous material carried in from the field.

blocks.title: Sizing & De-Stoning
desc: Grain is graded into size fractions and de-stoned, since both pearling and malting are carried out on an even kernel.
Thin and broken corns are separated out for feed.

blocks.title: Pearling & Bran Removal
desc: Abrasive pearling removes the husk and successive bran layers from the kernel to give pot barley and pearl barley.
The bran dust released is captured at the machine.

blocks.title: Steeping, Germination & Kilning
desc: Malting is a separate route rather than a stage after pearling: cleaned, graded barley is steeped in water, allowed to germinate in a conditioned bed, and then kilned dry.
Conditioned, cooled air is passed through the germination bed to hold it steady.

blocks.title: Flaking & Milling
desc: Pearled barley is steamed and rolled into flakes, or milled and sifted into barley flour and grits.

blocks.title: Weighing & Packing
desc: Pearl barley, flakes and flour are weighed and filled into bags or sacks, stitched, coded and checked.

blocks.text: Durum wheat processing mills hard amber grain into semolina for pasta and couscous rather than into fine flour. Durum is cleaned, scoured and tempered with water so the bran peels away cleanly, then reduced on corrugated rolls and sifted so the coarse endosperm granules are recovered. ART Mechatronics supplies durum cleaning, tempering, milling and packing plants.

blocks.title: Intake, Cleaning & Storage
desc: Durum is received into silo storage and cleaned of straw, dust, stones and metal before milling.
Lots are kept separate so grain of different vitreousness can be blended deliberately.

blocks.title: Scouring & Tempering
desc: The kernel surface is scoured, then water is added and the grain is rested in tempering bins so the bran toughens and the endosperm mellows.
Moisture is checked before the grain goes to first break.

blocks.title: Break Milling on Corrugated Rolls
desc: Tempered durum is opened gradually between corrugated rolls so the endosperm is released as coarse granules instead of being crushed to flour.
Stock is elevated between passages and re-sifted each time.

blocks.title: Purification & Granulation Control
desc: Sifted stock is classified by size and by air so bran flakes and germ are lifted away from the heavier semolina granules.
This purification step is what sets a durum mill apart from a bread-flour mill.

blocks.title: Speck Sorting & Blending
desc: Semolina is sorted to remove dark specks of bran, then blended to a consistent grade before storage.

blocks.title: Packing & Bulk Despatch
desc: Finished semolina is dosed into bags for retail and trade, or loaded in bulk for pasta plants.
Bags are weighed, stitched, coded and palletised.

ART Mechatronics supplies sorghum cleaning, decortication, milling and packing lines for food and feed mills.

blocks.text: Sorghum processing cleans and decorticates jowar grain so the fibrous outer pericarp is abraded away before the kernel is milled into flour, grits or flakes. The crop arrives carrying soil, glumes and stalk pieces, so screening and density separation come first. ART Mechatronics supplies sorghum cleaning, decortication, milling and packing lines for food and feed mills.

blocks.title: Intake & Screening
desc: Sorghum is fed over screens that pull out stalk, glumes, dust and undersize seed.
Ferrous material is removed before the grain reaches any abrasive machine.

blocks.title: De-Stoning & Aspiration
desc: Stones and clods of the same size as the grain are separated by density, and light chaff is drawn off in the air stream.
Clean, even grain decorticates more consistently in the next stage.

blocks.title: Decortication & Bran Removal
desc: Abrasive decortication removes the pericarp and the testa layer that carries the bitter note in some varieties.
Bran and fines are drawn straight into dust collection so the working area stays clear.

blocks.title: Grading & Colour Sorting
desc: Decorticated kernels are graded to size and sorted to remove discoloured, mouldy and foreign grain.
Rejects are diverted automatically rather than picked by hand.

blocks.title: Milling into Grits & Flour
desc: Kernels are milled and sifted into grits, meal and jowar flour according to the grade being run.

blocks.title: Packing & Bulk Handling
desc: Flour and grits are weighed and filled into pouches or sacks, stitched and palletised for despatch.

metaTitle: Semolina Processing Plant & Machinery | Turnkey Semolina Line by ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Semolina plants for milling, sifting, air classification, roasting of rava, blending and packing of coarse, medium and fine semolina grades.
intro: Semolina is the coarse endosperm fraction recovered when durum or hard wheat is roller-milled, and a semolina plant exists to control its granulation. Milled stock is sifted and air-classified into coarse, medium and fine grades, roasted where rava is required, cooled and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies semolina milling, sifting, roasting, conveying and packing equipment.

blocks.text: Semolina is the coarse endosperm fraction recovered when durum or hard wheat is roller-milled, and a semolina plant exists to control its granulation. Milled stock is sifted and air-classified into coarse, medium and fine grades, roasted where rava is required, cooled and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies semolina milling, sifting, roasting, conveying and packing equipment.

blocks.title: Wheat Conditioning & Milling
desc: Conditioned wheat is scoured and reduced on rolls set to release granular endosperm rather than fine flour.
Stock is lifted between passages for repeated sifting.

blocks.title: Sifting & Granulation Control
desc: Milled stock is sifted across a stack of sieves so coarse, medium and fine semolina grades are separated cleanly.
Granulation is the property buyers specify, so this stage governs the whole plant.

blocks.title: Purification & Bran Separation
desc: An air stream lifts bran flakes and germ away from the heavier semolina particles.
Dust drawn off here is collected rather than released into the mill.

blocks.title: Roasting & Cooling
desc: Where roasted rava is being made, semolina is passed through a roaster and then cooled before it is stored.
Unroasted grades bypass this stage entirely.

blocks.title: Blending, Conveying & Storage
desc: Grades are blended to a consistent granulation and moved to silo storage by pneumatic and mechanical conveying.

blocks.title: Packing & Metal Inspection
desc: Semolina is dosed by auger into pouches, bags or cartons, coded, weighed and checked for metal before despatch.

intro: Lentil processing turns harvested whole lentils into cleaned, dehusked and split masoor dal ready for the kitchen. The seed is cleaned of stones, dust and metal, graded by size, conditioned to loosen the husk, then dehusked, split, polished and colour sorted before weighing and packing. ART Mechatronics supplies complete lentil milling lines, from intake handling to finished packing.

blocks.text: Lentil processing turns harvested whole lentils into cleaned, dehusked and split masoor dal ready for the kitchen. The seed is cleaned of stones, dust and metal, graded by size, conditioned to loosen the husk, then dehusked, split, polished and colour sorted before weighing and packing. ART Mechatronics supplies complete lentil milling lines, from intake handling to finished packing.

blocks.title: Intake & Pre-Cleaning
desc: Incoming lentils are received from bags or bulk tippers and lifted into the cleaning section.
Stones, mud balls, chaff, straw and stray metal are taken out before the seed reaches any milling machine.

blocks.title: Grading & Sizing
desc: Cleaned lentils are separated into size grades so that each fraction can be dehusked on its own setting.
Grading also lifts out shrivelled and immature seed that would otherwise break during milling.

blocks.title: Conditioning & Drying
desc: The seed is conditioned with water so that the husk loosens from the kernel, then dried back to a moisture level suited to milling.
Moisture is checked before the batch is released to the huller.

blocks.title: Dehusking & Splitting
desc: Conditioned lentils pass through the dehusking section, where the outer husk is abraded away from the kernel.
Unhulled seed is sifted out and returned to the huller, while the dehusked seed goes on to be split into its two cotyledons and the loose husk is drawn off by air.

blocks.title: Polishing & Grading of Dal
desc: Split lentils are polished to clean the surface and even out the appearance of the dal.
The dal is then separated into whole, split and broken fractions, each carried on its own stream.

blocks.title: Sorting & Inspection
desc: Optical sorting removes discoloured, stained and foreign-coloured grains from the finished dal.
A final metal check is made before the product enters packing, with rejected material diverted off the line automatically.

blocks.title: Weighing & Packing
desc: Dal is weighed into consumer packs or bulk bags and sealed.
Each pack is coded and check-weighed before it leaves the line.
