intro: Medicinal herb processing prepares roots, leaves, barks and seeds such as ashwagandha, tulsi and brahmi for use in ayurvedic and herbal formulations. The material is cleaned of stones and metal, washed, cut, shade or hot-air dried, then pulverised and sieved into a graded powder, or taken forward for extraction. ART Mechatronics supplies herb processing machinery for cleaning, cutting, drying, grinding and extraction.

blocks.text: Medicinal herb processing prepares roots, leaves, barks and seeds such as ashwagandha, tulsi and brahmi for use in ayurvedic and herbal formulations. The material is cleaned of stones and metal, washed, cut, shade or hot-air dried, then pulverised and sieved into a graded powder, or taken forward for extraction. ART Mechatronics supplies herb processing machinery for cleaning, cutting, drying, grinding and extraction.

blocks.title: Cleaning & De-Stoning
desc: Field-collected herbs carry soil, grit, stones and stray metal, which are separated on air-screen and density-based cleaners.
Cleaning first protects the cutters and mills further down the line.

blocks.title: Washing & Stem Removal
desc: Roots and rhizomes are washed to lift remaining soil, and woody stems are separated from leaf and flower material.
Only the plant part named in the formulation is carried forward.

blocks.title: Cutting & Shredding
desc: Cleaned herbs are cut or shredded to a uniform size so they dry evenly rather than case-hardening on the outside.
Hard roots and barks are chipped before they go to the dryer.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Cut herbs are dried in trays or on a moving band under warm filtered air to bring moisture down for safe storage.
Drying air temperature is kept moderate on aromatic herbs so the volatile fraction is not driven off.

blocks.title: Grinding & Sieving
desc: Dried herbs are pulverised and sieved into the mesh grade the formulation calls for.
Grinding is run with dust collection because dry herb powder is light and readily airborne.

blocks.title: Extraction & Extract Drying
desc: Where an extract is wanted rather than a raw powder, the herb is boiled or macerated in a jacketed vessel and the liquor is separated and concentrated.
The concentrate is spray dried onto a carrier to give a free-flowing extract powder.

blocks.title: Sterilisation & Packing
desc: Herb powders carry a natural microbial load, so batches are treated before packing.
Cleared powder is filled into pouches or sacks, metal-checked and cased.

intro: Facewash manufacturing blends water, surfactants, thickeners and skincare actives into a gel or cream cleanser that is filled into tubes and bottles. ART Mechatronics supplies the mixing, transfer, filling, capping and packaging machinery used on facewash lines, together with the controls that link them.

blocks.text: Facewash manufacturing blends water, surfactants, thickeners and skincare actives into a gel or cream cleanser that is filled into tubes and bottles. The batch is mixed in a closed vessel, thickened, pH corrected, deaerated and held before filling. ART Mechatronics supplies the mixing, transfer, filling, capping and packaging machinery used on facewash lines, together with the controls that link them.

blocks.title: Water Charging & Raw Material Weighing
desc: Treated water is held in a storage tank and metered into the batch, while surfactants, gums, powders and actives are weighed against the formulation card.
Powdered raw materials are sieved as they are charged so that lumps do not carry into the mixing vessel.

blocks.title: Surfactant Wetting & Blending
desc: Surfactants are drawn into the water phase in a jacketed vessel under slow agitation, which wets the raw material without whipping air into the batch.
Warm water is circulated through the jacket to help the surfactant blend dissolve evenly.

blocks.title: Thickening & pH Correction
desc: Thickeners are hydrated and the pH is corrected so that the cleanser builds the body and clarity expected of the grade being made.
Shear mixing disperses the thickener fully and prevents gel lumps forming in the batch.

blocks.title: Actives, Beads & Perfume Addition
desc: Exfoliating granules, clays, plant extracts, colour and perfume are added late in the cycle under gentle stirring so that beads stay whole and volatiles are not lost.
Vacuum is then applied to pull entrapped air out of the gel before it is transferred.

blocks.title: Bulk Holding & Filling
desc: The approved batch is held in a bulk tank and drawn to the filling line, where tubes and bottles are filled, then sealed or capped.
Filled packs are coded and labelled as they leave the filler.

blocks.title: Cartoning & Despatch Packing
desc: Packs are checkweighed, placed into unit cartons and collated into shipper cases.
Cases are wrapped on pallets for despatch.

blocks.title: Thickening, pH Correction & Deaeration

blocks.title: Bottle Filling & Labelling

intro: Lotion manufacturing emulsifies an oil phase of emollients, esters and waxes into a water phase of humectants and stabilisers to give a pourable skincare emulsion. The batch is homogenised, cooled under slow stirring, then perfume, preservative and heat-sensitive actives are added before filling into bottles and pump packs. blocks.text: Lotion manufacturing emulsifies an oil phase of emollients, esters and waxes into a water phase of humectants and stabilisers to give a pourable skincare emulsion. blocks.title: Oil & Water Phase Preparation
desc: The water phase with humectants and stabilisers and the oil phase with emollients, esters and waxes are prepared separately in jacketed vessels.
Both phases are heated by steam through the jacket until the waxes are molten and the gums are fully hydrated.

blocks.title: Emulsification
desc: The oil phase is drawn into the water phase in the jacketed vessel under high shear, so that the oil is broken into a fine, stable dispersion.
Working under vacuum keeps air out of the emulsion while it is being formed.

blocks.title: Controlled Cooling & Late Additions
desc: Chilled water is circulated through the jacket while the batch is stirred slowly, so the emulsion sets without breaking.
Perfume, preservative and heat-sensitive actives are added once the batch has cooled.

blocks.title: Bulk Holding & Release
desc: The finished emulsion is transferred to a bulk tank and held while appearance, pH and viscosity are checked against the specification.
Batch records are captured by the plant automation system before the bulk is released to filling.

blocks.title: Bottle & Pump Pack Filling
desc: Containers are rinsed and filled by piston filler, then fitted with pumps, discs or screw caps.
Filled packs are labelled on line.

blocks.title: Coding, Leak Check & Cartoning
desc: Packs are coded, leak checked and placed into unit cartons.
Cartons are collated into shipper cases for despatch.

metaDesc: Wood pellet plant machinery from ART Mechatronics: chipping, screening, drying, fine milling, pelletising, cooling and bagging for wood pellet fuel production.
intro: Wood pellet production converts logs, sawmill offcuts and sawdust into a dense, uniform solid fuel. The wood is chipped, screened to remove stones and tramp metal, dried, then milled to a fine sawdust and compressed through a die, where its own lignin binds each pellet. blocks.text: Wood pellet production converts logs, sawmill offcuts and sawdust into a dense, uniform solid fuel. The wood is chipped, screened to remove stones and tramp metal, dried, then milled to a fine sawdust and compressed through a die, where its own lignin binds each pellet. Cooled and screened pellets are bagged for boilers, stoves and industrial furnaces.

blocks.title: Intake & Chipping
desc: Logs, slabs, offcuts and sawmill residue are received and reduced to chips of a workable size.
Chipping first gives the dryer and the mill a feed that behaves consistently.

blocks.title: Screening & Contaminant Removal
desc: Chips are screened, with oversize pieces returned for re-chipping, while stones, nails, staples and other tramp metal are taken out and light material is drawn off by air.
Contaminants left in the feed damage mill hammers and press dies.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Green wood carries a lot of moisture, so the chips are dried before milling.
Wood that is too wet will not hold its shape when pressed, and wood that is too dry does not bind.

blocks.title: Fine Milling
desc: Dried chips are milled down to sawdust fine enough to pass through the press die.
The milled dust is collected and conveyed to the press in a closed circuit to keep airborne wood dust out of the shed.

blocks.title: Conditioning & Pelletising
desc: The sawdust is conditioned with steam to soften it, then forced through a die under pressure.
Heat and pressure release the lignin naturally present in wood, which sets as the pellet leaves the die.

blocks.title: Cooling & Fines Removal
desc: Pellets leave the die hot and soft, and are cooled so they harden.
Loose fines are sieved and aspirated off and returned to the press feed rather than going into the bag.

blocks.title: Weighing, Bagging & Dispatch
desc: Cooled pellets are weighed into bags, closed and stacked for dispatch.
Bagged fuel is easier to store and to sell by weight than loose pellets.

blocks.text: Biomass pellet production turns agricultural residues such as rice husk, groundnut shell, bagasse, mustard stalk and straw into a handleable solid fuel. The residue is chopped to a uniform length, cleaned of soil, sand and tramp iron, dried, ground, then blended and compressed into pellets. Cooling, screening and bagging follow, giving a fuel used in boilers, gasifiers and hot air generators.

blocks.title: Residue Intake & Feeding
desc: Loose husk, baled straw and cane trash arrive in sacks or bales and are opened out into a feed hopper.
Residues differ in bulk density, so the feed rate is controlled rather than tipped straight into the line.

blocks.title: Chopping & Size Reduction
desc: Long stalk, straw and bagasse are cut down to a short, even length before anything else happens.
Unlike wood, this material is fibrous and stringy, so it is chopped and shredded rather than chipped.

blocks.title: Cleaning & De-stoning
desc: Field-collected residue carries soil, sand, grit and stones picked up during harvesting and heaping, along with baling wire and nails.
Earth is separated out by air and by density and iron is pulled out magnetically, since abrasive and hard material wears out dies and hammers.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Residue that has been stored in the open or cut green is dried down before grinding.
Light, low-density material dries in a moving air stream rather than in a heavy rotating drum.

blocks.title: Grinding
desc: Dried residue is broken down to a loose, even meal.
Grinding is done under extraction because husk and stalk dust is light and travels.

blocks.title: Blending & Densification
desc: Different residues are blended so the press sees a consistent feed instead of alternating batches of husk and stalk.
The blend is then compressed into pellets.

blocks.title: Cooling, Screening & Bagging
desc: Pellets are cooled, screened to take out broken material and fines, and filled into woven sacks.
Sack weight is checked and recorded before the sack is closed.

metaTitle: Charcoal Pellet & Briquette Plant | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Charcoal pellet and briquette plant machinery: crushing, pulverising, screening, binder mixing, pressing, drying and dust-controlled packing lines.
intro: Charcoal pellet production takes lump charcoal, charcoal fines and coconut shell char and reforms them into uniform pellets and briquettes. Because the material is already carbonised, it is not dried at the start but crushed to a powder, screened, mixed with a starch or clay binder, and pressed. The shaped fuel is then dried to harden it before packing.

blocks.text: Charcoal pellet production takes lump charcoal, charcoal fines and coconut shell char and reforms them into uniform pellets and briquettes. Because the material is already carbonised, it is not dried at the start but crushed to a powder, screened, mixed with a starch or clay binder, and pressed. The shaped fuel is then dried to harden it before packing.

blocks.title: Charcoal Intake & Covered Storage
desc: Lump charcoal, kiln fines and coconut shell char are received and kept under cover so they stay dry.
Every tipping and transfer point is put under extraction, because charcoal sheds fine black dust.

blocks.title: Crushing & Pulverising
desc: Lumps are broken down and then reduced to a fine powder.
Coarse particles will not bind, so the whole charge is taken down to powder before any binder is added.

blocks.title: Powder Screening & Grading
desc: The powder is screened, with oversize returned to the mill and the fine fraction taken forward.
Sand, soil and unburnt pieces carried over from carbonisation are separated out at this point.

blocks.title: Binder Preparation & Mixing
desc: A starch or clay binder is prepared with water and blended into the charcoal powder.
Charcoal has no natural binder of its own, so the mix is worked until it holds a shape when pressed by hand.

blocks.title: Pressing into Pellets & Briquettes
desc: The damp mix is pressed or extruded into pellets, sticks or briquettes and cut to length.
The shape is chosen to suit the end use, from barbecue and shisha charcoal to industrial fuel.

blocks.title: Drying & Hardening
desc: The pressed pieces are dried to drive off the water brought in with the binder.
Drying is what hardens them; charcoal that is packed damp will crumble and can spoil in storage.

blocks.title: Packing & Dust Control
desc: Hardened pellets and briquettes are weighed, filled into printed bags, coded and wrapped for dispatch.
Packing runs under central dust collection so black dust is not carried into the finished stock.

h1: Cement Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Cement Plant Machinery & Equipment | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Cement processing plant machinery from ART Mechatronics: crushing, raw meal grinding, clinker grinding, conveying, silo storage, bagging and dust control.
intro: Cement processing converts quarried limestone, clay and corrective additives into a fine hydraulic binder. The raw materials are crushed, blended and ground into raw meal, burned in a kiln to form clinker, then inter-ground with gypsum. ART Mechatronics supplies crushing, grinding, conveying, storage, dust control and bagging equipment for cement plants and grinding units.

blocks.text: Cement processing converts quarried limestone, clay and corrective additives into a fine hydraulic binder. The raw materials are crushed, blended and ground into raw meal, burned in a kiln to form clinker, then inter-ground with gypsum. ART Mechatronics supplies crushing, grinding, conveying, storage, dust control and bagging equipment for cement plants and grinding units.

blocks.title: Raw Material Crushing
desc: Quarried limestone arrives with clay, laterite and other correctives and is size-reduced before it can be ground.
Feeders draw material from the receiving hopper at a steady rate into the crusher.

blocks.title: Stacking & Reclaiming
desc: Crushed material is stacked in long piles and reclaimed across the layers, which evens out the variation that comes with the quarry face.
Belt conveyors move material between the stockpile and the mill feed bins.

blocks.title: Raw Meal Grinding & Blending
desc: The corrected mix is ground to raw meal and classified, with coarse material returned to the mill.
Weigh feeders set the proportion of each component before grinding.

blocks.title: Pyroprocessing & Clinker Cooling
desc: Raw meal is preheated and burned in the kiln, where it fuses into clinker nodules.
Clinker leaves the kiln hot and is cooled before storage or grinding, and the hot air recovered from cooling is returned to the process.

blocks.title: Clinker Grinding with Gypsum
desc: Cooled clinker is ground together with gypsum, which controls the setting behaviour of the finished cement.
Tramp iron is removed ahead of the mill and the ground product is classified to the fineness the grade calls for.

blocks.title: Storage, Packing & Despatch
desc: Finished cement is stored in silos and drawn off either as bulk for tankers or through a bag packer.
Filled bags are closed, stacked and moved to the loading bay.

blocks.title: Dust & Emission Control
desc: A cement plant releases dust at every transfer point, so crushers, mills, silos and packers are vented to collectors.
Recovered dust is returned to the process instead of being discharged.

h1: Ready-Mix Concrete (RMC) Batching Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: RMC Batching Plant Machinery & Equipment | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Ready-mix concrete batching plant machinery: aggregate handling, cement silos, weighing and dosing, mixers, automation control panels and dust collection.
intro: Ready-mix concrete (RMC) is batched at a central plant, where aggregate, sand, cement, fly ash, water and admixtures are weighed to a fixed recipe, mixed, and discharged into transit mixers for delivery to site. ART Mechatronics supplies batching plants with aggregate handling, silo storage, weighing, mixing, control panels and dust collection.

blocks.text: Ready-mix concrete (RMC) is batched at a central plant, where aggregate, sand, cement, fly ash, water and admixtures are weighed to a fixed recipe, mixed, and discharged into transit mixers for delivery to site. ART Mechatronics supplies batching plants with aggregate handling, silo storage, weighing, mixing, control panels and dust collection.

blocks.title: Aggregate & Sand Reception
desc: Coarse aggregate and sand are tipped into ground bins and drawn out below by feeders.
An inclined belt lifts the material to the batching bins above the mixer.

blocks.title: Cement & Fly Ash Silo Feeding
desc: Cement and fly ash arrive in bulk tankers and are blown into silos, then drawn to the weigh hopper by screw conveyor.
Bagged binders can be added through a dump station where a silo is not used.

blocks.title: Weighing, Dosing & Water Control
desc: Each ingredient is weighed separately against the recipe, and the water added is corrected for the moisture already carried by the sand.
Admixtures are dosed from holding tanks.

blocks.title: Mixing
desc: The weighed batch is discharged into the mixer and blended until the concrete is uniform through the load.
Batch sequence, mixing time and discharge are handled from the plant control system.

blocks.title: Discharge & Despatch
desc: Mixed concrete is discharged through a chute into a transit mixer, which keeps it turning on the way to site.
Batch records are logged against each delivery.

blocks.title: Dust & Washout Control
desc: Silo tops, weigh hoppers and the mixer are vented to collectors so that cement powder is not lost to the air.
Wash water and settled solids from cleaning the mixer are collected separately.

h1: Dry Mix Mortar Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Dry Mix Mortar Plant Machinery & Equipment | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Dry mix mortar plant machinery: sand drying and screening, additive dosing, ribbon and plough shear mixing, bag packing, palletising and dust extraction.
intro: Dry mix mortar production combines dried, graded sand with cement, lime, fillers and chemical additives into a single blended powder that is mixed with water on site. The sand is dried and screened, the ingredients are dosed by weight, blended dry and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies drying, screening, dosing, mixing, packing and dust control equipment for mortar plants.

blocks.text: Dry mix mortar production combines dried, graded sand with cement, lime, fillers and chemical additives into a single blended powder that is mixed with water on site. The sand is dried and screened, the ingredients are dosed by weight, blended dry and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies drying, screening, dosing, mixing, packing and dust control equipment for mortar plants.

blocks.title: Sand Drying
desc: Dry mix mortar cannot be made with damp sand, because the cement in the bag would begin to hydrate in storage.
Washed sand is therefore dried before it enters the plant.

blocks.title: Screening & Fraction Storage
desc: Dried sand is screened into narrow size fractions, which are stored separately so that each mortar grade can be built from the fractions it needs.
Oversize is diverted out of the line.

blocks.title: Binder & Additive Dosing
desc: Cement, lime and fillers are drawn from silos, while small-quantity additives such as cellulose ethers and polymer powders are added through a dump station.
Every component is weighed before it reaches the mixer.

blocks.title: Dry Mixing
desc: The weighed materials are blended dry until the additives, which make up only a small part of the batch, are spread through it.
Mixing time and sequence are set from the control system.

blocks.title: Packing & Palletising
desc: Finished mortar is drawn from a holding bin into valve or open-mouth bags, closed, and coded with the batch details.
Bags are stacked and wrapped for despatch.

blocks.title: Dust Control
desc: Drying, screening, mixing and packing all release fine powder, so those points are kept under extraction.
Recovered fines are returned to the process.

h1: Sand Washing & Processing Plant Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Sand Washing & Processing Plant Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Sand processing plant machinery: scalping, washing and silt removal, drying, screening into fractions, magnetic and gravity separation, storage and bagging.
intro: Sand processing turns river, pit or crusher-run sand into graded construction and industrial grades. The feed is scalped, washed to remove silt and clay, dewatered and dried, then screened into size fractions, with iron and stone contaminants separated out before storage or bagging. ART Mechatronics supplies washing, drying, screening, separation, conveying and packing equipment for sand plants.

blocks.text: Sand processing turns river, pit or crusher-run sand into graded construction and industrial grades. The feed is scalped, washed to remove silt and clay, dewatered and dried, then screened into size fractions, with iron and stone contaminants separated out before storage or bagging. ART Mechatronics supplies washing, drying, screening, separation, conveying and packing equipment for sand plants.

blocks.title: Feeding & Scalping
desc: Raw sand is tipped into a reception hopper and drawn out at a controlled rate.
A scalping screen takes out oversize stone and debris before washing.

blocks.title: Washing & Silt Removal
desc: Sand is agitated with water so that clay, silt and organic matter are lifted away from the grains.
Wash water is settled and recirculated rather than run to waste.

blocks.title: Dewatering & Drying
desc: Washed sand still holds surface water, which is drained off before the sand goes to the dryer.
Drying is needed for sand that will be bagged or used in dry blended products.

blocks.title: Grading into Fractions
desc: Dried sand is separated into size fractions, since plaster, concrete and industrial uses each call for a different grading.
Very fine dust is drawn off by air classification.

blocks.title: Iron & Contaminant Removal
desc: Magnets take out tramp iron picked up in handling, and density-based separation removes heavy grains and small stone.
This step matters most for glass and foundry grades.

blocks.title: Storage, Packing & Loading
desc: Graded sand is held in silos or bins and drawn off for bulk loading or bagging.
Bags are closed and stacked for despatch.

h1: Stone Crushing & Aggregate Plant Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Stone Crushing Plant Machinery & Equipment | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Stone crushing plant machinery: primary and secondary crushers, screening, washing, conveying, stockpile reclaim, loading and dust suppression systems.
intro: Stone processing reduces quarried rock into graded aggregate for concrete, roads and railway ballast. Blasted stone is fed to a primary crusher, reduced further in secondary and tertiary stages, screened into commercial sizes, washed where a clean product is required, and stockpiled for loading. ART Mechatronics supplies crushing, screening, washing, conveying and dust suppression equipment for stone crushing plants.

blocks.text: Stone processing reduces quarried rock into graded aggregate for concrete, roads and railway ballast. Blasted stone is fed to a primary crusher, reduced further in secondary and tertiary stages, screened into commercial sizes, washed where a clean product is required, and stockpiled for loading. ART Mechatronics supplies crushing, screening, washing, conveying and dust suppression equipment for stone crushing plants.

blocks.title: Primary Crushing
desc: Blasted rock is tipped into a feed hopper and drawn forward onto the primary crusher, which brings the largest lumps down to a size the plant can carry.
A grizzly feeder separates the fines ahead of the crusher so they are not crushed again.

blocks.title: Secondary & Tertiary Crushing
desc: Crushed stone passes through further stages that reduce it towards the sizes actually sold and improve the particle shape.
Oversize returns to the crusher in a closed circuit.

blocks.title: Screening into Sizes
desc: The crushed product is screened into the graded aggregate sizes used for concrete, road layers and ballast.
Each fraction leaves the screen on its own conveyor to its own stockpile.

blocks.title: Washing
desc: Where a clean aggregate is specified, the stone is washed to take crusher dust and clay coating off the surface.
Wash water is settled before it is reused.

blocks.title: Stockpiling & Loading
desc: Finished fractions are stacked in separate stockpiles and reclaimed for loading into tippers.
Telescopic conveyors build the piles without extra handling by loader.

blocks.title: Dust Suppression & Control
desc: Crushing and screening throw dust into the air, so transfer points are enclosed and vented and water sprays are used at the crusher.
Collected dust joins the fines stockpile.

h1: Interlocking Paver Block Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Paver Block Plant Machinery & Equipment | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Interlocking paver block plant machinery: aggregate batching, base and face mix preparation, vibro-press moulding, curing, stacking, wrapping and despatch.
intro: Interlocking paver blocks are made by batching aggregate, sand, cement and pigment, preparing a coarse base mix and a finer coloured face mix, then moulding both together under vibration and pressure. The green blocks are cured, stacked and wrapped for despatch. ART Mechatronics supplies batching, mixing, moulding, curing, handling and packing equipment for paver block plants.

blocks.text: Interlocking paver blocks are made by batching aggregate, sand, cement and pigment, preparing a coarse base mix and a finer coloured face mix, then moulding both together under vibration and pressure. The green blocks are cured, stacked and wrapped for despatch. ART Mechatronics supplies batching, mixing, moulding, curing, handling and packing equipment for paver block plants.

blocks.title: Aggregate & Cement Batching
desc: Stone dust, aggregate, cement and pigment are drawn from separate bins and weighed for each batch.
Bins are refilled by loader or conveyor between batches.

blocks.title: Base & Face Mix Preparation
desc: A paver is built from two mixes: a coarse base concrete that carries the load and a finer coloured face mix that forms the wearing surface.
The two are mixed separately and fed to the moulding machine in sequence.

blocks.title: Moulding & Vibro-Compaction
desc: The base mix is filled into the mould, the face mix is laid over it, and the block is compacted by vibration under pressure.
Changing the mould changes the paver shape and interlocking pattern.

blocks.title: Curing
desc: Green blocks are carried on pallets to curing racks or a chamber and kept damp, or steam-cured, until they can be handled.
Handling a block before it has cured breaks the fresh edges.

blocks.title: Stacking, Wrapping & Despatch
desc: Cured pavers are lifted off the pallets, stacked into cubes and wrapped for the yard.
Empty pallets return to the moulding machine.

blocks.title: Dust Extraction
desc: Cement handling and the batching bins are the main dust sources in a paver plant and are kept under extraction.
Collected fines go back into the base mix.

h1: Marble Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Marble Processing Plant Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Marble processing machinery: block squaring and sawing, resin filling and curing, calibration, polishing, edge trimming, grading, handling and packing.
intro: Marble processing converts quarried blocks into finished slabs and tiles. Blocks are squared and sawn into slabs, natural veins and pits are filled with resin and oven-cured, the slab is calibrated flat, polished to a gloss, trimmed to size and graded before packing. ART Mechatronics supplies cutting, drying, grinding, polishing, handling and packing equipment for marble processing units.

blocks.text: Marble processing converts quarried blocks into finished slabs and tiles. Blocks are squared and sawn into slabs, natural veins and pits are filled with resin and oven-cured, the slab is calibrated flat, polished to a gloss, trimmed to size and graded before packing. ART Mechatronics supplies cutting, drying, grinding, polishing, handling and packing equipment for marble processing units.

blocks.title: Block Handling & Squaring
desc: Quarry blocks are received in the yard, checked for cracks and squared so that they sit true on the saw.
Blocks move between stations on trolleys and roller tracks.

blocks.title: Slab Sawing
desc: The block is sawn into slabs of even thickness, with water carrying away the cut waste and cooling the blades.
Thicker cuts are taken for cut-to-size work and thinner ones for slabs.

blocks.title: Resin Filling & Curing
desc: Marble carries natural veins, pits and hairline cracks, which are filled with resin and reinforced before the surface is worked.
The filled slab passes through a drying oven so that the resin sets.

blocks.title: Calibration & Grinding
desc: The slab is ground flat to an even thickness before polishing, because a polishing head cannot correct an uneven surface.
Coarse heads take out the saw marks first.

blocks.title: Polishing
desc: Successively finer abrasive heads bring the marble surface up to a gloss.
The slab is washed and blown dry at the end of the line.

blocks.title: Cutting to Size & Grading
desc: Slabs are edge-trimmed and cut into tiles or cut-to-size pieces, then graded by shade and vein pattern.
Each piece is checked for chips and thickness.

blocks.title: Packing & Despatch
desc: Finished pieces are packed into crates or bundles with edge protection and labelled by lot.
Crates are wrapped and moved to the loading bay.

h1: Granite Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Granite Processing Plant Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Granite processing machinery: block sawing, epoxy and mesh curing, polishing, honing and flaming, cutting to size, slurry handling and dust extraction.
intro: Granite processing turns hard quarried blocks into slabs and cut-to-size pieces. Blocks are squared and sawn, slabs are reinforced with epoxy and mesh and cured, then finished as polished, honed or flame-textured surfaces before edge cutting and grading. Cutting water carries stone slurry that must be settled. ART Mechatronics supplies sawing, finishing, handling, slurry and dust equipment for granite units.

blocks.text: Granite processing turns hard quarried blocks into slabs and cut-to-size pieces. Blocks are squared and sawn, slabs are reinforced with epoxy and mesh and cured, then finished as polished, honed or flame-textured surfaces before edge cutting and grading. Cutting water carries stone slurry that must be settled. ART Mechatronics supplies sawing, finishing, handling, slurry and dust equipment for granite units.

blocks.title: Block Inspection & Sawing
desc: Granite blocks are inspected for colour and cracks, squared, and sawn into slabs.
Cutting runs with water, which cools the cutting edge and flushes the cut.

blocks.title: Epoxy Coating & Curing
desc: Slabs are coated with epoxy, and fractured or softer material is backed with mesh, so that the slab survives handling and polishing.
The coating is set in a drying tunnel before the surface is worked.

blocks.title: Surface Finishing
desc: Granite is finished as polished, honed or flame-textured, depending on where it will be laid.
Flaming uses a burner to spall the surface, while polishing and honing use abrasive heads.

blocks.title: Cutting to Size & Inspection
desc: Slabs are edge-trimmed and cut into the sizes ordered, then checked for colour match and finish.
Pieces are numbered so that a job can be laid in the sequence it was cut.

blocks.title: Slurry & Dust Management
desc: Sawing and polishing produce a stone slurry that has to be settled out so the water can be used again.
Dry cutting and flaming points are kept under extraction.

blocks.title: Packing & Loading
desc: Finished slabs are loaded into A-frames or crates with separators between them and labelled by lot.
Crates are wrapped and moved to despatch.

h1: Ceramic Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Ceramic Plant Machinery & Equipment | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Ceramic processing machinery: batch weighing, ball milling into slip, screening and de-ironing, spray drying, pressing, glazing, firing, sorting and packing.
intro: Ceramic processing prepares a body of clay, feldspar and quartz for sanitaryware, tableware and ceramic products. The batch is weighed, wet-ground into slip, screened and de-ironed, spray-dried into free-flowing granulate, pressed or cast to shape, glazed, fired in a kiln, then inspected and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies milling, spray drying, forming, firing and packing equipment for ceramic plants.

blocks.text: Ceramic processing prepares a body of clay, feldspar and quartz for sanitaryware, tableware and ceramic products. The batch is weighed, wet-ground into slip, screened and de-ironed, spray-dried into free-flowing granulate, pressed or cast to shape, glazed, fired in a kiln, then inspected and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies milling, spray drying, forming, firing and packing equipment for ceramic plants.

blocks.title: Body Batch Preparation
desc: Clay, feldspar and quartz are received, lump material is broken down, and each raw material is weighed to the body recipe.
Materials are held in separate bins so that recipes can be changed between batches.

blocks.title: Wet Grinding into Slip
desc: The weighed batch is ground with water in a ball mill until the body becomes a pourable slip.
The slip is held in stirred tanks so that the solids do not settle out.

blocks.title: Screening & De-Ironing
desc: Slip is screened to take out coarse residue and passed over magnets, because iron specks show as dark spots after firing.
Rejected residue is taken out of the circuit.

blocks.title: Spray Drying to Granulate
desc: The slip is sprayed into a hot air stream, which drives off the water and leaves free-flowing granules that press well.
Fines carried out with the air are recovered in a cyclone.

blocks.title: Forming & Pressing
desc: Granulate is pressed in dies, or slip is cast in moulds for sanitaryware, to give the green shape.
Green pieces are dried before any glaze is applied.

blocks.title: Glazing & Firing
desc: Glaze is applied to the dried body and the piece is fired, which vitrifies the body and fuses the glaze to it.
Heat recovered from the kiln is taken back to the dryers.

blocks.title: Inspection & Packing
desc: Fired ware is inspected for cracks, warping and glaze faults, then sorted into grades.
Accepted pieces are packed into cartons and palletised.

metaTitle: Tile Manufacturing Plant Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Tile plant machinery: powder silos, hydraulic pressing, dryers, glazing and digital decoration, kiln firing, polishing, shade sorting, boxing and palletising.
intro: Tile manufacturing presses prepared ceramic powder into green tiles, dries them, applies glaze and printed decoration, and fires them in a kiln. Fired tiles are polished or rectified where the finish calls for it, sorted by shade and size, then boxed and palletised. ART Mechatronics supplies pressing, drying, decoration, firing, polishing, sorting and packing equipment for tile lines.

blocks.text: Tile manufacturing presses prepared ceramic powder into green tiles, dries them, applies glaze and printed decoration, and fires them in a kiln. Fired tiles are polished or rectified where the finish calls for it, sorted by shade and size, then boxed and palletised. ART Mechatronics supplies pressing, drying, decoration, firing, polishing, sorting and packing equipment for tile lines.

blocks.title: Powder Storage & Ageing
desc: Spray-dried powder is held in silos so that moisture spreads evenly through it before pressing.
Feeders draw powder from the silos to the press hoppers.

blocks.title: Pressing & Drying
desc: Powder is pressed in a die to form the green tile, which still holds moisture and has little strength.
The green tile is dried before any glaze is applied to it.

blocks.title: Glazing & Decoration
desc: Engobe and glaze are applied to the dried tile and the pattern is printed onto the surface.
Glaze is kept stirred and screened so that it stays uniform along the line.

blocks.title: Kiln Firing & Cooling
desc: Decorated tiles pass through the kiln, where the body vitrifies and the glaze fuses, then through a cooling section.
Waste heat from the cooling zone is taken back to the dryers.

blocks.title: Polishing & Rectification
desc: Vitrified tiles are polished and squared on the edges where the finish calls for it.
The tile is washed after grinding so that no slurry dries on the face.

blocks.title: Shade Sorting & Inspection
desc: Fired tiles vary in tone and in size, so they are sorted into shade and calibre groups and checked for surface faults.
Rejects are taken off the line before packing.

blocks.title: Boxing & Palletising
desc: Tiles of one shade and calibre are boxed together, coded, and stacked on pallets.
Pallets are wrapped and labelled for the warehouse.

h1: Fly Ash Handling & Processing Plant Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Fly Ash Handling & Processing Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Fly ash processing machinery: pneumatic conveying, silo storage, pond ash drying, air classification, grinding, bulk and bag despatch with dust control.
intro: Fly ash processing takes the fine ash collected from thermal power plant flue gas and prepares it for use in blended cement, concrete, bricks and blocks. Dry ash is conveyed pneumatically into silos, while pond ash is dried first. The ash is then classified, sometimes ground, and despatched in bulk tankers or bags. ART Mechatronics supplies conveying, drying, classifying, grinding and bagging equipment.

blocks.text: Fly ash processing takes the fine ash collected from thermal power plant flue gas and prepares it for use in blended cement, concrete, bricks and blocks. Dry ash is conveyed pneumatically into silos, while pond ash is dried first. The ash is then classified, sometimes ground, and despatched in bulk tankers or bags. ART Mechatronics supplies conveying, drying, classifying, grinding and bagging equipment.

blocks.title: Collection & Pneumatic Conveying
desc: Fly ash is drawn from the hoppers under the power plant's precipitator and moved in a closed pneumatic line, because dry ash cannot be handled in the open.
Air and ash are separated again at the silo.

blocks.title: Silo Storage & Extraction
desc: Ash is stored in silos and kept aerated at the cone so that it continues to flow.
Extraction to the process or to the loading spout is by screw conveyor or elevator.

blocks.title: Pond Ash Drying
desc: Ash recovered from ash ponds is wet and lumpy and has to be dried before it can be classified or ground.
Dried ash rejoins the dry handling line.

blocks.title: Classification into Fine Fractions
desc: Fly ash is separated by air into a fine fraction used in cement and concrete and a coarse fraction used in bricks and fill.
Fines are recovered from the air stream in cyclones.

blocks.title: Grinding
desc: Coarse ash and pond ash are ground where a finer, more reactive product is wanted.
Tramp iron is removed ahead of the mill.

blocks.title: Bulk & Bag Despatch
desc: Processed ash leaves either through a bulk loading spout into a tanker or through a bagging line.
Bags are closed, stacked and moved to loading.

blocks.title: Dust & Emission Control
desc: Silo vents, transfer points and the bagging line are held under negative pressure so that ash does not escape into the plant.
Collected ash is returned to the silo.

h1: Gypsum Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Gypsum Plant Machinery & Calcining Equipment | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Gypsum processing machinery: rock crushing, drying and grinding, calcining, cooling, fine milling, additive blending, bagging and palletising lines.
intro: Gypsum processing converts mined gypsum rock, or by-product gypsum, into plaster and plasterboard binder. The rock is crushed, dried and ground, then calcined so that chemically combined water is driven off and the gypsum becomes hemihydrate plaster. The plaster is cooled, milled fine, blended with additives and bagged. ART Mechatronics supplies crushing, drying, calcining, milling and packing equipment.

blocks.text: Gypsum processing converts mined gypsum rock, or by-product gypsum, into plaster and plasterboard binder. The rock is crushed, dried and ground, then calcined so that chemically combined water is driven off and the gypsum becomes hemihydrate plaster. The plaster is cooled, milled fine, blended with additives and bagged. ART Mechatronics supplies crushing, drying, calcining, milling and packing equipment.

blocks.title: Rock Crushing & Screening
desc: Mined gypsum rock is crushed and screened to a size the mill can take.
By-product gypsum from fertiliser or flue gas plants joins the line at this stage instead.

blocks.title: Drying & Grinding
desc: Free moisture is driven off and the rock is ground to a powder before it goes to the calciner.
Ground gypsum is lifted to the calciner feed bin.

blocks.title: Calcination
desc: Heating the ground gypsum drives off part of the chemically combined water and converts it into hemihydrate, the plaster used in building products.
Heat is supplied indirectly or by hot gas, depending on the plaster grade being made.

blocks.title: Cooling & Conditioning
desc: Freshly calcined plaster leaves the calciner hot and reactive, and is cooled and held before use so that its setting behaviour settles down.
Cooled plaster goes to storage silos.

blocks.title: Fine Milling & Classification
desc: Plaster is milled to the fineness the end product needs and classified, with coarse material returned to the mill.
Grades of different fineness are stored separately.

blocks.title: Blending with Additives
desc: Retarders, accelerators and fillers are weighed in and blended so that the plaster sets in the time the application needs.
Batches are mixed dry, with no water added at the plant.

blocks.title: Packing & Palletising
desc: Blended plaster is packed into bags, closed and coded, then stacked for despatch.
Packing points are vented so that fine plaster is not lost into the packing hall.

h1: Tyre (Tire) Manufacturing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Tyre Manufacturing Plant & Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Tyre plant material handling and utility systems: carbon black and silica intake, weighing and dosing, conveying, curing-hall utilities, dust and fume extraction.
intro: Tyre manufacturing combines natural and synthetic rubber with carbon black, silica, oils, textile fabric and steel cord, which are mixed, calendered, extruded, built into a green tyre and cured in a mould. ART Mechatronics supplies the surrounding plant: powder intake, weighing and dosing, conveying, curing-hall utilities, and dust and fume extraction for tyre factories.

blocks.text: Tyre manufacturing combines natural and synthetic rubber with carbon black, silica, oils, textile fabric and steel cord, which are mixed, calendered, extruded, built into a green tyre and cured in a mould. ART Mechatronics supplies the surrounding plant: powder intake, weighing and dosing, conveying, curing-hall utilities, and dust and fume extraction for tyre factories.

blocks.title: Raw Material Intake & Storage
desc: Carbon black, silica, fillers and process chemicals arrive in sacks and bulk containers and are tipped, screened for tramp metal and moved into storage.
Keeping each filler in its own storage route stops cross-contamination between compound recipes.

blocks.title: Weighing & Dosing to Recipe
desc: Fillers, oils and curing chemicals are weighed out against the compound recipe and released into the mixer feed.
Recipe control at this point is what makes one batch of compound behave like the last.

blocks.title: Mixing & Compound Handling
desc: Weighed ingredients are fed to the internal mixer, and the discharged compound is sheeted, cooled and stacked before it goes forward.
Powder released around the mixer charging hole is captured at source rather than allowed into the hall.

blocks.title: Extrusion, Calendering & Tyre Building
desc: Treads and sidewalls are extruded, fabric and steel cord are rubber-coated on the calender, and the components are assembled into a green tyre on the building drum.
Cooled, tension-free component handling between these stations protects the shape of each part.

blocks.title: Curing & Plant Utilities
desc: Green tyres are cured in heated moulds, which the plant supports with steam, hot and chilled water and cooling circuits.
Vulcanisation fumes released as presses open are drawn away from the operating floor.

blocks.title: Inspection, Marking & Despatch
desc: Cured tyres are trimmed, examined for internal and surface defects, marked and stacked for despatch.
Rejects are separated on the line so they never reach the loading bay.

h1: Inner Tube Manufacturing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Inner Tube Manufacturing Plant & Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Inner tube plant equipment: butyl compound handling, extrusion cooling, talc dust extraction, curing utilities, leak testing and carton packing lines.
intro: Inner tube manufacturing extrudes butyl or natural rubber compound into a continuous sleeve, which is cut to length, fitted with a valve, joined into a ring and cured in a mould, then inflated and leak-tested. ART Mechatronics supplies the compound handling, talc dust extraction, curing utilities, testing conveyors and packing equipment around these tube lines.

blocks.text: Inner tube manufacturing extrudes butyl or natural rubber compound into a continuous sleeve, which is cut to length, fitted with a valve, joined into a ring and cured in a mould, then inflated and leak-tested. ART Mechatronics supplies the compound handling, talc dust extraction, curing utilities, testing conveyors and packing equipment around these tube lines.

blocks.title: Compound Preparation & Feeding
desc: Butyl or natural rubber compound is prepared with fillers and curing chemicals, the dry ingredients being pre-blended before they reach the extruder feed.
Powder handling is enclosed so filler does not settle on the tube stock.

blocks.title: Sleeve Extrusion & Cooling
desc: The compound is extruded as a continuous sleeve with no longitudinal joint, then cooled so it holds its wall thickness before handling.
Talc is applied to keep the inner walls from sticking together, and the airborne talc is extracted at the applicator.

blocks.title: Cutting, Valve Fitting & Splicing
desc: Sleeve is cut to length, the valve is fitted and secured, and the two ends are joined to close the tube into a ring.
The valve seat is the most common leak point, so this station is worked with fixed positioning and repeatable pressure.

blocks.title: Curing & Utilities
desc: Tubes are cured in heated moulds, supported by the plant steam, hot water and cooling circuits.

blocks.title: Inflation & Leak Testing
desc: Every tube is inflated and held under water or under pressure so that pinholes and splice faults show up.
Failed tubes are diverted off the line rather than repaired in the flow.

blocks.title: Folding, Cartoning & Despatch
desc: Passed tubes are dusted, folded, coded and cartoned by size and valve type for despatch.

h1: Rubber Seal Manufacturing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Rubber Seal Manufacturing Plant & Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Rubber and oil seal plant equipment: compound handling, metal case washing lines, bonding fume extraction, moulding utilities, deflashing dust control and packing.
intro: Rubber seal manufacturing bonds a moulded elastomer lip onto a metal case: the case is washed and coated with bonding agent, compound preforms are moulded onto it under heat, and the seal is then deflashed, spring-fitted and dimensionally checked. ART Mechatronics supplies the compound handling, washing and adhesive extraction, moulding utilities, and inspection and packing equipment.

blocks.text: Rubber seal manufacturing bonds a moulded elastomer lip onto a metal case: the case is washed and coated with bonding agent, compound preforms are moulded onto it under heat, and the seal is then deflashed, spring-fitted and dimensionally checked. ART Mechatronics supplies the compound handling, washing and adhesive extraction, moulding utilities, and inspection and packing equipment.

blocks.title: Compound & Preform Preparation
desc: Elastomer compound is mixed with fillers and curing chemicals and formed into preforms sized for the seal being run.
Preform weight consistency is what keeps the moulded lip filling the same way every cycle.

blocks.title: Metal Case Cleaning & Bonding Coat
desc: Stamped metal cases are degreased, rinsed and dried, then coated with primer and bonding agent.
Solvent vapour from the coating station is drawn off at the booth so it does not spread through the shop.

blocks.title: Moulding & Curing Utilities
desc: Compound and case are brought together in a heated mould so the rubber cures and bonds to the metal in one operation.
The presses are served by the plant heating and cooling circuits and by local fume capture.

blocks.title: Deflashing & Lip Finishing
desc: Flash left at the mould parting line is trimmed away and the sealing lip is finished to its final profile.
Rubber dust from trimming and grinding is collected at the machine hood.

blocks.title: Spring Fitting & Inspection
desc: The garter spring is fitted into its groove and each seal is checked for lip condition, bond and dimensions.

blocks.title: Packing & Despatch
desc: Seals are pouched or boxed by part number, coded and collated into outer cartons for despatch.

metaDesc: Gasket plant equipment: filler handling and sieving, sheet line conveying, curing utilities, cutting-area dust extraction, offcut granulating, counting and packing.
intro: Gasket manufacturing rolls compounded rubber, cork or fibre into sheet, cures the sheet, and then cuts gaskets to shape by die-cutting or punching before the edges are cleaned and the parts inspected. ART Mechatronics supplies the filler handling, sheet-line conveying, curing utilities, cutting-area dust extraction, offcut recovery and packing equipment used in gasket plants.

blocks.text: Gasket manufacturing rolls compounded rubber, cork or fibre into sheet, cures the sheet, and then cuts gaskets to shape by die-cutting or punching before the edges are cleaned and the parts inspected. ART Mechatronics supplies the filler handling, sheet-line conveying, curing utilities, cutting-area dust extraction, offcut recovery and packing equipment used in gasket plants.

blocks.title: Filler Intake & Compound Mixing
desc: Mineral fillers, fibre and process chemicals are tipped, sieved and blended with the rubber or binder into a sheeting compound.
Sieving before mixing keeps lumps and foreign matter out of the sheet.

blocks.title: Sheeting & Calendering
desc: The compound is rolled into continuous sheet of the required thickness, cooled and wound or stacked.
Sheet gauge decided here governs how the gasket seats later, so the line runs at a steady take-off.

blocks.title: Curing & Utilities
desc: Rubber-bonded sheet is cured under heat and pressure, drawing on the plant steam and cooling circuits.

blocks.title: Cutting & Punching
desc: Gaskets are die-cut, punched or slit from the cured sheet to the drawing profile, including bolt holes.
Dust and fine trim released at the cutting table are extracted so they do not settle on the cut faces.

blocks.title: Offcut Recovery & Inspection
desc: The sheet skeleton left after cutting is collected and size-reduced so it can be routed back into suitable grades.
Finished gaskets are checked for profile, hole positions and surface faults.

blocks.title: Counting, Kitting & Despatch
desc: Gaskets are counted into sets or single part numbers, marked and packed into cartons for despatch.

h1: O-Ring Manufacturing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: O-Ring Manufacturing Plant & Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: O-ring plant equipment: compound and preform handling, moulding utilities, deflashing dust extraction, post-curing ovens, vision inspection and pouch counting lines.
intro: O-ring manufacturing moulds precision elastomer rings from compound preforms, removes the flash left at the mould parting line, post-cures the rings to drive off residues, and inspects each ring for dimensional and surface defects. ART Mechatronics supplies the compound handling, moulding utilities, deflashing dust extraction, post-cure ovens and the counting and pouch packing lines.

blocks.text: O-ring manufacturing moulds precision elastomer rings from compound preforms, removes the flash left at the mould parting line, post-cures the rings to drive off residues, and inspects each ring for dimensional and surface defects. ART Mechatronics supplies the compound handling, moulding utilities, deflashing dust extraction, post-cure ovens and the counting and pouch packing lines.

blocks.title: Compound Preparation & Preforming
desc: Elastomer compound is mixed and formed into cord or slug preforms matched to the cross-section being moulded.
Preform accuracy is what keeps the mould cavities filling without excess flash.

blocks.title: Moulding Support Utilities
desc: Preforms are cured in multi-cavity moulds, served by the plant heating, chilled water and control systems.

blocks.title: Deflashing & Tumbling
desc: Rings are separated from the mould sprue and tumbled so the thin flash breaks away cleanly.
The rubber fines released during tumbling are drawn off and collected.

blocks.title: Post-Curing
desc: Rings are held in circulating hot air to complete the cure and drive off volatile residues.

metaDesc: Glove dipping line equipment: latex compounding tanks, former washing, leaching and vulcanising utilities, chlorination fume scrubbing, leak testing and boxing lines.
intro: Rubber glove manufacturing dips cleaned ceramic formers into coagulant and then into compounded latex, and the deposited film is leached, beaded, vulcanised and surface-treated before the gloves are stripped, dried and leak-tested. ART Mechatronics supplies the latex compounding tanks, former washing, hot air and steam utilities, chlorination fume scrubbing and glove counting and boxing lines.

blocks.text: Rubber glove manufacturing dips cleaned ceramic formers into coagulant and then into compounded latex, and the deposited film is leached, beaded, vulcanised and surface-treated before the gloves are stripped, dried and leak-tested. ART Mechatronics supplies the latex compounding tanks, former washing, hot air and steam utilities, chlorination fume scrubbing and glove counting and boxing lines.

blocks.title: Latex Compounding & Storage
desc: Curing chemicals and dispersions are blended into the latex and the compound is held under gentle agitation until it is drawn to the line.
Steady agitation keeps the dispersion uniform so the deposited film stays even.

blocks.title: Former Cleaning & Coagulant Dipping
desc: Ceramic formers are washed, rinsed and dried before entering the coagulant tank, which prepares the surface for latex pick-up.
Any residue left on a former shows as a defect in the finished glove.

blocks.title: Latex Dipping, Leaching & Vulcanising
desc: Formers pass through the latex tank to build up the film, then through leaching tanks that wash out water-soluble residues, and finally through the curing ovens.
Oven and tank heating is carried by the plant hot water, steam and air handling systems.

blocks.title: Surface Treatment, Stripping & Drying
desc: Gloves are chlorinated or polymer-coated so they can be donned easily, then stripped from the formers and tumble-dried.
Chlorination exhaust is scrubbed before release and the working area is kept under extraction.

blocks.title: Leak Testing & Inspection
desc: Gloves are tested for pinholes and checked visually for tears, thin patches and beading faults.
Failures are removed from the flow before counting begins.

blocks.title: Counting, Boxing & Despatch
desc: Gloves are counted into dispenser boxes by size, coded, collated into outers and wrapped for despatch.

blocks.text: Rubber footwear manufacturing builds the upper from cut and stitched components, bonds it to a rubber sole with solvent adhesive over a last, and vulcanises the assembled shoe so upper and sole cure together. blocks.title: Compound & Component Preparation
desc: Sole and foxing compound is mixed with fillers and curing chemicals, while textile and sheet components are cut to pattern.
Compound and cut parts are kept in matched batches so a shoe is built from one recipe.

blocks.title: Upper Making & Stitching

blocks.title: Roughing, Cementing & Lasting

Buffing dust and solvent vapour are captured at the bench so the cement bond stays clean and the air stays breathable.

blocks.title: Boxing, Cartoning & Despatch

intro: Conveyor belt manufacturing coats fabric plies or steel cord with rubber on a calender, lays the coated plies and cover sheets into a carcass, and vulcanises the assembly in a heated press so covers and carcass bond into one belt. blocks.text: Conveyor belt manufacturing coats fabric plies or steel cord with rubber on a calender, lays the coated plies and cover sheets into a carcass, and vulcanises the assembly in a heated press so covers and carcass bond into one belt. ART Mechatronics supplies the compound handling, solvent fume extraction, press utilities and roll handling equipment.

blocks.title: Compound & Fabric Preparation
desc: Cover and skim compounds are mixed from rubber, fillers and curing chemicals, while fabric or steel cord is creeled ready for coating.
Filler intake is enclosed and vented so carbon black does not reach the fabric store.

blocks.title: Calendering & Ply Coating
desc: Rubber is rolled onto the fabric plies or steel cord, and solvent cement applied at this stage is dried before winding.
Solvent vapour from the cement application is extracted along the line.

blocks.title: Belt Building
desc: Coated plies and top and bottom cover sheets are laid up in sequence to the specified belt construction.
Heavy rolls and long lay-up lengths are moved mechanically rather than manhandled.

blocks.title: Press Vulcanising & Utilities
desc: The built belt is vulcanised in heated platens in successive lengths, drawing on the plant steam, thermic fluid and cooling water circuits.

blocks.title: Trimming, Cooling & Winding
desc: Belt edges are trimmed to width, the belt is cooled under tension and wound into rolls.
Edge trim is collected and size-reduced instead of accumulating beside the press.

blocks.title: Roll Handling & Despatch
desc: Finished rolls are lifted, marked with belt type and length details, wrapped and loaded for despatch.

blocks.text: Footwear sole manufacturing mills rubber or EVA compound into sheet, blanks the sheet into preforms, and moulds each preform into a sole, which is then trimmed, buffed on the bonding face, washed and printed before pairing. blocks.title: Compound Mixing & Sheeting
desc: Rubber or EVA is mixed with fillers, blowing agents and pigment, then milled into sheet and cooled.
Sheet is stacked flat so blanks cut from it stay to gauge.

blocks.title: Blank Cutting
desc: Sheet is cut into blanks matched to sole size and cavity, and fed to the press stations in sorted trays.

blocks.title: Moulding & Expansion Utilities
desc: Blanks are moulded under heat, and expanded grades are held and stabilised after release from the mould.
Press heating and post-mould cooling are carried by the plant utility circuits.

blocks.title: Trimming & Buffing
desc: Flash is trimmed from the sole edge and the bonding face is buffed so adhesive will key to it.
Buffing releases fine rubber dust, which is drawn off at each machine hood.

blocks.title: Washing, Printing & Inspection
desc: Soles are washed to remove release agent and dust, dried, printed with size and branding marks, and checked.

blocks.title: Pairing, Packing & Despatch
desc: Left and right soles are paired by size, counted, bagged and packed into cartons for the shoe line.

intro: Anti-vibration mount manufacturing bonds a rubber element to metal end fittings: the metal parts are blast-cleaned, degreased and coated with bonding agent, the compound is moulded onto them under heat, and the finished mount is deflashed, inspected and protected. blocks.text: Anti-vibration mount manufacturing bonds a rubber element to metal end fittings: the metal parts are blast-cleaned, degreased and coated with bonding agent, the compound is moulded onto them under heat, and the finished mount is deflashed, inspected and protected. ART Mechatronics supplies the compound handling, bonding-line extraction, moulding utilities and the finishing and packing equipment.

blocks.title: Metal Part Cleaning & Bonding Agent
desc: Fittings are blast-cleaned, degreased, rinsed and dried, then coated with primer and bonding agent.
Blast dust and solvent vapour are extracted separately, because a contaminated metal face is the usual cause of a failed bond.

blocks.title: Compound Preparation & Preforming
desc: Rubber compound is mixed to the required grade, milled into sheet and cut into preforms sized for the mount being made.

blocks.title: Bonding, Moulding & Curing Utilities
desc: Prepared fittings and preforms are loaded into the mould, where the rubber cures and bonds to the metal in a single operation.
Press heating, hot air post-cure and chilled water are served by the plant utility circuits.

blocks.title: Deflashing & Surface Finishing
desc: Flash is removed from the rubber-to-metal junction and exposed metal surfaces are cleaned up.
Rubber and metal dust from finishing are collected at source.

blocks.title: Testing & Inspection
desc: Mounts are checked for bond integrity, rubber condition and dimensions, and non-conforming parts are separated.

blocks.title: Protection, Packing & Despatch
desc: Threads and metal faces are protected, parts are coded by part number and packed into cartons for despatch.

metaDesc: Rubber mat and flooring plant equipment: crumb granulating, steel and fibre separation, screening, binder mixing, press utilities, dust extraction and roll handling.
intro: Rubber mat and flooring manufacturing granulates rubber crumb or mills fresh compound, screens it to the fractions wanted, blends it with binder and pigment, and presses or moulds the blend into tiles, mats and rolls that are then cut to size. blocks.text: Rubber mat and flooring manufacturing granulates rubber crumb or mills fresh compound, screens it to the fractions wanted, blends it with binder and pigment, and presses or moulds the blend into tiles, mats and rolls that are then cut to size. ART Mechatronics supplies the granulating, separating, screening, mixing, dust extraction and press utility equipment.

blocks.title: Granulating & Crumb Preparation
desc: Feedstock is size-reduced in stages, and steel wire and textile fibre are pulled out of the crumb stream.
Clean separation at this point decides how the finished surface looks and wears.

blocks.title: Screening & Grading
desc: Crumb is screened into coarse, medium and fine fractions, each held for a different layer or product.
Oversize is returned to the granulator rather than carried forward.

blocks.title: Binder Mixing & Colouring
desc: Graded crumb is dosed with binder and pigment and mixed until the coating is even across the batch.

blocks.title: Pressing, Moulding & Utilities
desc: The blend is spread into moulds or a continuous bed and cured under heat and pressure into tiles or sheet.
Press heating and post-press cooling come from the plant utility circuits.

blocks.title: Cutting, Trimming & Rolling
desc: Cured sheet is trimmed to width, cut into tiles or mats, or wound into rolls of the ordered length.
Cutting dust and trim are extracted and collected at the line.

blocks.title: Stacking, Wrapping & Despatch
desc: Tiles are counted and stacked, rolls are wrapped and marked with pattern and size, and both are palletised.

blocks.title: Powder Intake & Sieving
desc: Mineral filler, abrasive and pigment are tipped from sacks, screened and conveyed to the mixing floor.
Screening removes lumps that would otherwise show as hard spots in the finished eraser.

blocks.title: Weighing & Compound Mixing
desc: Rubber or vinyl, plasticiser, filler, abrasive and pigment are weighed to recipe and mixed into a uniform compound.
Colour and abrasive distribution are set here and cannot be corrected further down the line.

blocks.title: Sleeving, Printing & Inspection

blocks.title: Counting, Packing & Despatch

blocks.title: Trim Recovery & Extraction Control
desc: Edge trim and reject tissue collected by the extraction network are baled for return to the mill.
The extraction and conveying system is run and monitored from a central control panel.

intro: Cardboard production forms recovered paper and pulp into duplex, grey and multi-layer board, which is dried, calendered, reeled and then sheeted to size. Around the board machine sit the waste paper yard, baling and fibre recovery, trim and dust extraction, sheet stacking and the palletising and wrapping lines that move finished board to dispatch.

blocks.text: Cardboard production forms recovered paper and pulp into duplex, grey and multi-layer board, which is dried, calendered, reeled and then sheeted to size. blocks.title: Waste Paper Intake & Baling
desc: Recovered paper and board arrive loose or in bales, are sorted by grade and fed forward.
Tramp metal is pulled out of the stream before the fibre goes any further into the mill.

blocks.title: Pulping & Stock Feed
desc: Recovered fibre is broken down in water and cleaned before it reaches the board machine.
Our scope in this section is the feed conveying, storage and reject handling around the pulper, not the pulping line itself.

blocks.title: Board Forming & Drying
desc: Layers of stock are couched together, pressed and dried into multi-layer board, then calendered and reeled.
Steam, hot water and heat recovery plant serve the drying section.

blocks.title: Sheeting & Stacking
desc: Reels are slit and cross-cut into sheets of the ordered size and stacked.
Trim strips and board dust from the cutters are drawn off pneumatically and separated before the fan.

blocks.title: Palletising, Wrapping & Dispatch
desc: Stacked sheets and reels are palletised, wrapped and moved to the dispatch bay.

blocks.text: Mono carton making converts printed duplex or folding box board into single-piece retail cartons through die cutting, stripping, creasing and folder-gluing. blocks.title: Board Reception & Sheet Handling
desc: Printed board sheets arrive in stacks and are lifted and fed to the die cutter.
Stack height and transfer between floors are handled on lifting and vertical conveying equipment.

blocks.title: Die Cutting, Stripping & Creasing
desc: Sheets are die cut to the carton profile, the waste is stripped out and the crease lines are formed.
Board offcuts and fine dust leave the machine continuously and are extracted at the die and the stripping station.

blocks.title: Folding, Gluing & Inspection
desc: Blanks are folded and side-seam glued into flat cartons.
Each carton is checked for correct fold, glue line and print, and faulty ones are taken off the belt.

blocks.title: Counting, Bundling & Case Packing
desc: Flat cartons are counted into bundles and packed into unit and master cases for the customer's filling line.

blocks.title: Palletising & Waste Board Recovery
desc: Cases are palletised and wrapped for dispatch.
Stripped board waste collected from the extraction system is shredded and baled for recycling.

blocks.title: Line Control & Extraction Management
desc: The die cutting, folder-gluer and packing sections are sequenced and monitored from a single control point.
Board dust drawn off the die cutter is collected centrally and filtered before the air is returned to the hall.

blocks.title: Newsprint Reel Storage & Transport
desc: Reels are held in the reel hall and moved to the press reel stands as each edition is prepared.
Reels are heavy and awkward, so they are shifted on powered handling and lifting equipment.

blocks.title: Printing & Folding
desc: The web runs through the press and into the folder, where copies are cut, folded and delivered.
Paper dust and web trim released at the folder are extracted, and the press hall air is handled so dust and ink mist do not carry back to the printing units.

blocks.title: Counting, Stacking & Bundling
desc: Copies leaving the folder are counted into route quantities and stacked.
Each stack is compressed and strapped, and the bundle is labelled with its route before it leaves the mailroom.

blocks.title: Loading & Distribution
desc: Finished bundles are carried to the loading bay and loaded into vehicles route by route.

blocks.title: Returns & Waste Baling
desc: Unsold copies, plate-change waste and web breaks come back to the plant.
This paper is broken up and baled for sale to recyclers, with the collection ducting vented through a dust collector.

blocks.title: Sheet Handling & Folding
desc: Printed sheets are moved from the press hall to the folders and folded down into sections.
Stacks are transferred between floors and machines on handling equipment rather than carried.

blocks.title: Gathering & Binding

Gathered blocks move between the binding stations on linked conveying.

blocks.title: Three-Side Trimming
desc: The bound block is trimmed at head, foot and fore-edge to the finished size.
The knives throw off shavings and fine paper dust, which are drawn away from the trimmer and separated before collection.

blocks.title: Inspection, Counting & Shrink Wrapping
desc: Finished books are checked, counted into pack quantities and shrink wrapped.
Packs are coded so each batch can be traced back to the run.

blocks.text: Car parking lifts stack vehicles vertically inside a hotel, mall, hospital or high-rise building, using the height of a bay instead of extra floor area. blocks.title: Site Survey and Layout Planning
desc: The available bay, headroom, column positions and vehicle access path are measured before a parking configuration is fixed.
Other vertical handling needs in the same building are reviewed at this stage so shafts and pits are shared where the layout allows.

blocks.title: Pit, Shaft and Guide Structure
desc: The pit or shaft opening, anchor points and clearances are prepared to suit the configuration chosen at survey.
Guide columns and cross members are set out and aligned so the platform travels along a fixed path.

blocks.title: Platform, Drive and Actuation
desc: The lifting platform, drive and locking arrangement are fitted onto the erected guide structure.
Mechanical and pneumatic elements are connected and checked by hand before the lift is powered.

blocks.title: Controls and Safety Interlocks
desc: The control panel, operating station and interlocks are wired so that platform movement is tied to gate and bay position.
Where a building already runs a central system, the lift is prepared for integration with it.

blocks.title: Erection and Commissioning at Site
desc: The assembled lift is aligned in the pit or shaft and run through no-load and loaded trials.
Access equipment and handling trolleys are used during erection before the bay is cleared for use.

blocks.title: Handover, Spares and Maintenance
desc: Drawings, operating instructions and a maintenance schedule are handed over with the installation.
Wear parts and replacement items are supplied against the same drawings so the lift can be serviced as built.

metaDesc: Ventilation blower systems from ART Mechatronics: fans, ducting, filtration, fume and dust extraction for hotel kitchens, basements, car parks and plant rooms.
intro: Blower ventilation moves air through kitchens, basements, car parks, laundries and plant rooms, replacing stale or fume-laden air with fresh supply air. A ventilation blower is selected for the duct layout it serves and is paired with filtration and extraction equipment where the exhaust carries dust, grease or fumes. ART Mechatronics supplies and installs ventilation blower systems.

blocks.text: Blower ventilation moves air through kitchens, basements, car parks, laundries and plant rooms, replacing stale or fume-laden air with fresh supply air. A ventilation blower is selected for the duct layout it serves and is paired with filtration and extraction equipment where the exhaust carries dust, grease or fumes. ART Mechatronics supplies and installs ventilation blower systems.

blocks.title: Air Movement Survey
desc: Each space is assessed for what the air has to carry away, whether that is cooking fumes, vehicle exhaust, humidity or process dust.
Supply and exhaust points are then marked so air moves across the room rather than short-circuiting back to the fan.

blocks.title: Fan and Duct Selection
desc: The blower is matched to the duct run it has to serve, including bends, risers and terminal grilles.
Where incoming air needs tempering or the exhaust holds usable heat, in-line heating and recovery equipment is included in the same run.

blocks.title: Filtration and Extraction
desc: Grease, lint and dust are taken out close to the source rather than left to travel through the ducting.
Local hoods and extraction arms are used at fixed points such as ranges, workshops and dispensing areas.

blocks.title: Exhaust Treatment Before Discharge
desc: Where the discharge would otherwise carry dust or fumes to neighbouring property, the exhaust is treated before it leaves the building.
Dry or wet treatment is chosen according to whether the load is particulate or vapour.

blocks.title: Controls and Air Balancing
desc: Fans are wired for manual, timed or interlocked operation depending on how the space is used.
Dampers and fan settings are then adjusted at site to balance the branches of the duct run.

blocks.title: Installation, Trials and Handover
desc: Ducting, fans and air handling equipment are erected, supported and run under load.
Filter changes, cleaning access and spare items are explained to the maintenance team at handover.

blocks.text: Centralised cooling conditions an entire hotel, mall or hospital from one plant room instead of separate units in each room. ART Mechatronics supplies, installs and commissions centralised cooling plant for hospitality and commercial projects.

blocks.title: Cooling Load Assessment and Plant Room Layout
desc: Occupied areas, kitchens, banquet halls and equipment rooms are reviewed to establish where cooling is needed and when.
The plant room is then laid out for access, pipe routing and future service.

blocks.title: Chilled Water Generation
desc: Chillers cool the circulating water that the rest of the building draws on.
Heat exchangers separate the plant circuit from the building circuit where the design calls for it.

blocks.title: Heat Rejection
desc: Heat picked up from the building is rejected outdoors through cooling towers and their circulating water loop.
Fans and tower internals are positioned to keep warm discharge away from the tower intake.

blocks.title: Air Side Distribution
desc: Air handling units take chilled water from the central loop and deliver conditioned air into the served zones.
Filtration, in-line heating and humidity control are added on the air side where the space calls for it.

blocks.title: Central Controls and Monitoring
desc: Plant and air side equipment are brought onto one control system so the building is operated from a single point.
Sequencing, interlocks and alarms are configured for the way the property runs through the day.

blocks.title: Commissioning and Service Support
desc: Circuits are filled, flushed and balanced, and the plant is run through trials before the building is handed over.
Routine service items and spares are listed so the plant is maintained from a known parts list.
