h1: Chiller Units for Cold Room, Kitchen and Process Cooling
metaTitle: Chiller Units | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Chiller units supplied and installed by ART Mechatronics for cold rooms, kitchens, jacketed vessels and process cooling, with cooling towers and control panels.
intro: A chiller unit removes heat from water or a process fluid and circulates it to wherever cooling is required, such as cold rooms, kitchen equipment, jacketed vessels or a production line. The unit runs a refrigeration circuit of compressor, condenser and evaporator, rejecting the collected heat to air or to a cooling tower. ART Mechatronics supplies and installs chiller units.

blocks.text: A chiller unit removes heat from water or a process fluid and circulates it to wherever cooling is required, such as cold rooms, kitchen equipment, jacketed vessels or a production line. The unit runs a refrigeration circuit of compressor, condenser and evaporator, rejecting the collected heat to air or to a cooling tower. ART Mechatronics supplies and installs chiller units.

blocks.title: Cooling Duty and Fluid Selection
desc: The loads to be served are listed first, since a kitchen, a cold room and a process line each ask for a different supply temperature.
Water or a suitable secondary fluid is chosen along with the pipe circuit that will carry it.

blocks.title: Refrigeration Circuit and Skid Assembly
desc: The compressor, condenser, evaporator and associated fittings are assembled onto a common frame.
Assembling the unit as a skid leaves the site work to services and final connections.

blocks.title: Heat Rejection and Condenser Water Loop
desc: Heat drawn out of the load is discharged either directly to air or through a cooling tower circuit.
Where a tower is used, the condenser water loop and its make-up storage are set up alongside the chiller.

blocks.title: Connection to Cooling Loads
desc: Chilled fluid is piped to the equipment it serves, from cold rooms and cooling tunnels to jacketed vessels and cooling conveyors.
Line sizing and insulation are worked out branch by branch across the circuit.

blocks.title: Control Panel and Safety Interlocks
desc: Start sequence, set points and trip conditions are configured in the panel supplied with the unit.
Flow and pressure interlocks are wired into the trip logic, and the unit can be linked to a wider plant control system.

blocks.title: Installation, Trials and Spares
desc: The unit is placed, connected, charged and run through trials with the served loads live.
Operating and service instructions are handed over together with the spares list.

intro: A boiler generates steam or hot water for hotel kitchens, laundries, guest room hot water and process heating. blocks.text: A boiler generates steam or hot water for hotel kitchens, laundries, guest room hot water and process heating. ART Mechatronics supplies and installs boilers.

blocks.title: Heat Demand and Fuel Selection
desc: The kitchens, laundry, guest floors and any process equipment are reviewed to establish what form of heat each one needs.
The fuel available at the site decides whether a fired boiler, a steam generator or a hot water generator suits the property.

blocks.title: Feed Water and Storage
desc: Feed water is treated and stored to limit the scale and dissolved solids carried into the vessel.
Storage and jacketed vessels hold the treated water and the condensate returned from the system.

blocks.title: Combustion and Heat Transfer
desc: The burner fires into the combustion chamber and the heat is passed to the water across the boiler surfaces.
Where a process needs heat without steam, a thermic fluid circuit is used in place of the water side.

blocks.title: Steam and Hot Water Distribution
desc: Steam and hot water are carried through insulated lines to kitchens, laundry equipment and guest floors.
Where a duty needs heated air rather than steam, a hot air generator feeds that duct run directly, and heat exchangers separate the boiler circuit from service water where the two must not mix.

blocks.title: Flue Gas Treatment and Heat Recovery
desc: Flue gas is treated before discharge where the fuel or the local rules require it.
Heat still held in the flue or in the exhaust air can be recovered and returned to the water or air side.

blocks.title: Controls, Commissioning and Spares
desc: Firing, water level and safety trips are configured in the control panel and tested before the boiler is released for use.
Operating staff are briefed on start-up, shutdown and blowdown routines, and the spares list is handed over.

metaDesc: Culinary herb processing plant and machinery: washing, de-watering, tray or freeze drying, cutting, classification and packing from ART Mechatronics.
intro: Culinary herb processing handles leafy herbs such as mint, basil, parsley and curry leaf, which are sold dried whole, cut or ground. The fresh herb is washed and de-watered, dried or freeze dried at low temperature to hold colour and aroma, cut to size and air classified to separate leaf from stalk. ART Mechatronics supplies washing, drying, cutting, classifying and packing machinery for culinary herbs.

blocks.text: Culinary herb processing handles leafy herbs such as mint, basil, parsley and curry leaf, which are sold dried whole, cut or ground. The fresh herb is washed and de-watered, dried or freeze dried at low temperature to hold colour and aroma, cut to size and air classified to separate leaf from stalk. ART Mechatronics supplies washing, drying, cutting, classifying and packing machinery for culinary herbs.

blocks.title: Reception & Washing
desc: Fresh herb is held cool on arrival, then washed and rinsed to remove soil, grit and insects.
Handling is kept gentle, because bruised leaf darkens before it reaches the dryer.

blocks.title: De-Watering
desc: Surface water is blown and shaken off the leaf so the dryer is not asked to remove wash water.
Even loading onto the dryer belt or tray keeps the drying rate uniform.

blocks.title: Drying or Freeze Drying
desc: Herbs are dried in low-temperature air, or freeze dried where the fresh colour and shape have to be retained.
Freeze drying is chosen for premium grades; tray and hot air drying serve standard grades.

blocks.title: Cutting & Classification
desc: Dried herb is cut or chopped to the cut size ordered and screened to remove fines.
Air classification separates the light leaf from heavier stalk, and magnets and metal detection follow the cutters.

blocks.title: Packing
desc: Dried herbs are bulky and light, so they are filled into sachets or pre-made bags and coded, with nitrogen flushing where aroma has to be protected.

h1: Mixed Spices Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Mixed Spices Processing Plant & Machinery | Turnkey Mixed Spices Line by ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Masala and mixed spice plant machinery: component cleaning, roasting, grinding, recipe dosing, blending, sieving and packing from ART Mechatronics.
intro: Mixed spice processing blends separately ground spices into masala products such as garam masala, sambar powder and curry powder. Each component is cleaned, roasted and ground on its own, weighed to the recipe, blended until the colour and aroma are uniform, sieved, checked for metal and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies dosing, blending, sieving, inspection and packing machinery for masala plants.

blocks.text: Mixed spice processing blends separately ground spices into masala products such as garam masala, sambar powder and curry powder. Each component is cleaned, roasted and ground on its own, weighed to the recipe, blended until the colour and aroma are uniform, sieved, checked for metal and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies dosing, blending, sieving, inspection and packing machinery for masala plants.

blocks.title: Intake & Component Cleaning
desc: Each spice is taken in separately and cleaned of dust, stones and tramp metal before it enters the blend line.
Keeping components separate at this stage means one contaminated lot does not spoil a whole batch.

blocks.title: Roasting & Grinding of Components
desc: Whole spices that need it are roasted to develop aroma, cooled, and then milled separately to their own mesh.
Grinding each component on its own is what lets hard seed and soft leaf both reach the right particle size.

blocks.title: Weighing & Dosing to Recipe
desc: Ground components are held in day bins and dosed by weight against the stored recipe.
Recipe control at the dosing point is what makes one batch taste like the last one.

blocks.title: Blending
desc: Components are blended until colour and aroma are uniform right through the batch.
Oily ingredients such as clove and cinnamon need a blender action that disperses them rather than letting them ball up.

blocks.title: Sieving & Inspection
desc: The blend is sifted to break up lumps and to hold the finished mesh.
Metal detection and inspection run before packing, since a blend draws contamination risk from every component in it.

blocks.title: Packing
desc: Masala is filled into pouches, sachets or jars on form fill seal lines, then labelled and cased.

intro: Animal feed manufacturing converts grains, oilseed meals, brans and mineral premixes into compound feed for livestock. Raw materials are cleaned, ground to a uniform particle size, batched by formula, mixed with liquids such as oil and molasses, then supplied as mash or steam-conditioned into pellets, cooled, screened and bagged. ART Mechatronics supplies the machinery for each of these stages.

blocks.text: Animal feed manufacturing converts grains, oilseed meals, brans and mineral premixes into compound feed for livestock. Raw materials are cleaned, ground to a uniform particle size, batched by formula, mixed with liquids such as oil and molasses, then supplied as mash or steam-conditioned into pellets, cooled, screened and bagged. ART Mechatronics supplies the machinery for each of these stages.

sections.title: Complete Animal Animal Feed Process Flow
sections.key: COMPLETE ANIMAL ANIMAL FEED PROCESS FLOW

blocks.title: Intake & Cleaning
desc: Incoming grain, cake and bran are screened to remove chaff, husk, stones and tramp metal.
Clean material is elevated to storage so that milling is not interrupted by foreign matter.

blocks.title: Grinding
desc: Cleaned ingredients are ground to the particle size the ration calls for, since particle size governs how well the mix holds together and how the animal digests it.
Ground meal is sieved and oversize material returned to the mill.

blocks.title: Batching & Dosing
desc: Each ingredient is drawn from its own bin and weighed against the formula for that batch.
Recipes and batch records are held in the plant control system so the same ration repeats from batch to batch.

blocks.title: Mixing & Liquid Addition
desc: The weighed batch is blended dry, then oil, molasses and liquid micro-ingredients are sprayed in while mixing continues.
Even distribution of the micro-ingredients through the batch is what makes the feed nutritionally consistent.

blocks.title: Conditioning, Pelleting & Cooling
desc: Mash is conditioned with steam to soften the starch, then pressed and formed into pellets.
Hot pellets are cooled and hardened before they are handled further, otherwise they crumble in transit.

blocks.title: Screening, Bagging & Palletising
desc: Fines are screened off and returned to the process, leaving whole pellets for despatch.
Feed is filled into sacks, stitched closed and stacked for loading.

intro: Aqua feed production makes sinking pellets for shrimp, prawn and other farmed aquatic species. The pellets are dried, oil-coated, graded and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies this machinery.

blocks.text: Aqua feed production makes sinking pellets for shrimp, prawn and other farmed aquatic species. Ingredients such as fishmeal, soya and wheat flour are ground to a fine powder, batched, mixed with binders, steam-conditioned and pressed into small-diameter pellets that must hold together in water. The pellets are dried, oil-coated, graded and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies this machinery.

sections.title: Complete Animal Aqua Feed Process Flow
sections.key: COMPLETE ANIMAL AQUA FEED PROCESS FLOW

blocks.title: Ingredient Intake & Cleaning
desc: Fishmeal, soya, squid meal and wheat flour are tipped from sacks and screened for string, husk and metal.
Because aquaculture feed is fed into open water, foreign matter is removed before it can reach the mill.

blocks.title: Fine Grinding & Sieving
desc: Aqua feed is ground far finer than livestock feed, because a shrimp takes small bites and the pellet must not shed particles into the pond.
The ground powder is sifted and coarse fractions are sent back for regrinding.

blocks.title: Batching & Premixing
desc: Vitamins, minerals and binder are weighed into a premix, then combined with the bulk ingredients for the batch.
The binder is what allows the finished pellet to stay intact once it is submerged.

blocks.title: Steam Conditioning & Pelleting
desc: The mix is conditioned with steam so the starch gelatinises and binds the pellet.
Conditioned mash is pressed into small-diameter sinking pellets sized for the species and growth stage.

blocks.title: Drying & Cooling
desc: Moisture picked up during conditioning is driven off so the pellets store without spoiling.
Dried pellets are cooled to ambient temperature and moisture is checked before coating.

blocks.title: Vacuum Oil Coating
desc: Fish oil, attractants and heat-sensitive additives are applied after pelleting rather than before, so they are not damaged by the conditioning heat.
Vacuum coating draws the oil into the pellet instead of leaving it on the surface, where it would wash off in water.

blocks.title: Grading & Packing
desc: Pellets are graded into size bands, since feed is matched to the size of the stock being fed.
Graded feed is checked for metal, filled and closed for despatch.

blocks.text: Pet feed manufacturing turns cereals, meat and poultry meals, fats and vitamin premixes into dry kibble for dogs and cats. The ground mash is cooked and shaped in an extruder, dried, coated with fat and palatant, cooled and then filled into retail bags or pouches. ART Mechatronics supplies grinding, extrusion, drying, coating and packing machinery for pet food plants.

sections.title: Complete Animal Pet Feed Process Flow
sections.key: COMPLETE ANIMAL PET FEED PROCESS FLOW

blocks.title: Raw Material Intake & Grinding
desc: Cereals, meat meal and poultry meal are ground to a fine, even meal.
Fine grinding matters here because kibble shape and surface finish depend on a uniform dough.

blocks.title: Batching & Mixing
desc: The ground meal is weighed to recipe with vitamin and mineral premixes and blended.
Recipes are held in the control system, so a brand's variants can be run in sequence without manual reset.

blocks.title: Extrusion Cooking & Shaping
desc: The mash is cooked with steam under pressure in the extruder, which gelatinises the starch and expands the dough as it leaves the die.
A rotating cutter at the die face shapes the kibble into the biscuit form the brand sells.

blocks.title: Drying & Cooling
desc: Kibble leaves the extruder wet and is dried on a moving bed of hot air until it is shelf-stable.
It is then cooled before coating, so the fat does not simply run off.

blocks.title: Fat & Palatant Coating
desc: Fat and palatant are sprayed onto the dried kibble in a tumbling drum so every piece is coated.
This outer coat carries most of the aroma and is what decides whether the animal accepts the food.

blocks.title: Retail Filling & Inspection
desc: Coated kibble is weighed out and filled into consumer bags, pouches or stand-up packs.
Every pack is checked for metal contamination and for correct fill weight before it leaves the line.

blocks.title: Coding & Secondary Packing
desc: Packs are coded with batch and date details, then collated into shippers.
Cases are stacked and wrapped for retail distribution.

blocks.text: Poultry feed production converts maize, soya de-oiled cake, rice bran and mineral premixes into mash, crumbs or pellets for broilers and layers. sections.title: Complete Animal Poultry Feed Process Flow
sections.key: COMPLETE ANIMAL POULTRY FEED PROCESS FLOW

blocks.title: Grain Intake & Cleaning
desc: Maize and de-oiled cake are pre-cleaned to take out husk, dust, stones and metal before milling.
Aspiration removes the light chaff that would otherwise carry through into the finished feed.

blocks.title: Grinding
desc: Cleaned grain is milled to the particle size the bird can handle, which differs between chick, grower and layer rations.
Ground meal is sieved and the mill is run under dust extraction.

blocks.title: Batching & Micro-Dosing
desc: Bulk ingredients are weighed by formula and micro-ingredients such as vitamins, enzymes and toxin binders are dosed separately in small quantities.
Micro-dosing is kept on its own line because these additives are used in very small proportions.

blocks.title: Mixing & Oil Addition
desc: The batch is blended and vegetable oil is sprayed in during mixing to raise the energy value of the ration.
Oil is held in a stirred tank so it stays homogeneous before dosing.

blocks.title: Conditioning, Pelleting & Crumbling
desc: Mash is steam-conditioned and pressed into pellets, then cooled.
For chick feed the cooled pellets are passed between rolls and broken into crumbs, which is the form young birds can eat.

blocks.title: Sieving, Bagging & Dispatch
desc: Crumbs and pellets are sieved to separate fines and off-size material.
Feed is bagged, weight-checked and moved to the loading bay.

blocks.text: Cattle feed manufacturing blends de-oiled cakes, brans, grain by-products, molasses and mineral mixture into compound feed for dairy and draught animals. sections.title: Complete Animal Cattle Feed Process Flow
sections.key: COMPLETE ANIMAL CATTLE FEED PROCESS FLOW

blocks.title: Raw Material Intake & Storage
desc: Oil cakes, brans, husk and grain by-products arrive in bulk and in bags and are moved into segregated storage.
Cattle feed uses many bulky, low-density ingredients, so handling and storage capacity shape the plant layout.

blocks.title: Crushing & Coarse Grinding
desc: Cake lumps and cottonseed are broken down and milled, but only to a coarse texture.
Ruminants need a coarser particle than poultry, so the ration is not ground to flour.

blocks.title: Weighing & Batching
desc: Each ground ingredient is weighed against the ration before it enters the mixer.
Mineral mixture and salt are added at this stage as part of the weighed batch.

blocks.title: Molasses & Bypass Fat Mixing
desc: Molasses is warmed so it flows, then sprayed into the mixer along with bypass fat while the batch is turning.
Molasses improves palatability and binds the dusty fraction of the ration.

blocks.title: Pelleting & Cooling
desc: The mixed ration is conditioned and pressed into pellets, which reduces wastage at the manger and stops the animal sorting the mix.
Pellets are cooled and hardened before bagging.

blocks.title: Bagging & Loading
desc: Finished feed is filled into sacks and stitched closed.
Sacks are conveyed to the vehicle for loading.

blocks.text: Fish feed production makes floating extruded pellets for carp, tilapia, catfish and other farmed fish. sections.title: Complete Animal Fish Feed Process Flow
sections.key: COMPLETE ANIMAL FISH FEED PROCESS FLOW

blocks.title: Raw Material Intake & Screening
desc: Fishmeal, soya, rice bran and maize are tipped, screened and freed of tramp metal.
Material is fed forward at a steady rate so the mill runs evenly.

blocks.title: Fine Grinding
desc: Ingredients are ground to a fine, uniform powder, because coarse particles stop the pellet expanding evenly in the extruder.
The powder is sieved and the mill runs under dust extraction.

blocks.title: Batching & Mixing
desc: The powder is weighed to formula with vitamin and mineral premixes and blended dry.
Moisture in the mix is checked before extrusion, as it governs how the pellet expands.

blocks.title: Extrusion & Cutting
desc: The mix is cooked with steam under pressure and forced through a die; the sudden drop in pressure expands the pellet and traps air inside it, which is what makes the pellet float.
A cutter at the die face sizes the pellet for the species being fed.

blocks.title: Drying & Cooling
desc: Expanded pellets carry a lot of moisture and are dried until they will store without moulding.
They are then cooled so that the oil applied next is absorbed rather than shed.

blocks.title: Oil Coating & Sizing
desc: Fish oil and heat-sensitive additives are sprayed onto the cooled pellets after extrusion.
Coated pellets are screened into size grades for fry, fingerling and grow-out feeding.

blocks.title: Inspection & Packing
desc: Bags are filled, coded with batch details and inspected before despatch.
Filled bags are stacked for storage and transport.

blocks.title: Dough Mixing & Resting
desc: Sifted flour and water are dosed and mixed, then the dough is held so the gluten relaxes before sheeting.
Resting is what allows a wide sheet to be rolled thin without tearing at the edges.

blocks.title: Sheeting to Thickness

blocks.title: Dough Mixing
desc: Flour is sifted and mixed with water and salts to a uniform dough ready for sheeting.

blocks.title: Sheeting & Slitting
desc: The dough is formed into a sheet, rolled down through successive passes and slit into thin strands.
Hakka noodles are cut narrower than flat noodles, so the slitting rolls are changed to suit.

blocks.title: Steaming
desc: The strands are steamed to gelatinise the starch and set the noodle before it is portioned.

blocks.title: Nesting & Portioning
desc: Steamed strands are folded into nests or cakes of a set portion size, which is how Hakka noodles are sold and cooked.
The nest holds the strands loose so they separate cleanly in boiling water.

blocks.title: Drying & Cooling
desc: The nests are dried with hot air until stable, then cooled before wrapping.

blocks.title: Packing
desc: Cooled nests are wrapped, coded, weight-checked and packed into cartons.

h1: White Rice Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: White Rice Processing Plant & Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: White rice milling machinery from ART Mechatronics - paddy cleaning, dehusking, whitening, polishing, grading, colour sorting and packing lines.
intro: White rice processing removes the husk and the outer bran layer from paddy to produce polished, uniform grain for table and export use. Cleaned paddy is first dehusked, the dehusked grain is then whitened and polished, and the milled rice is graded and colour sorted before packing. ART Mechatronics supplies machinery and turnkey plant systems for each of these stages.

blocks.text: White rice processing removes the husk and the outer bran layer from paddy to produce polished, uniform grain for table and export use. Cleaned paddy is first dehusked, the dehusked grain is then whitened and polished, and the milled rice is graded and colour sorted before packing. ART Mechatronics supplies machinery and turnkey plant systems for each of these stages.

blocks.title: Paddy Intake & Pre-Cleaning
desc: Incoming paddy is fed from the intake point and screened to remove straw, chaff, mud balls, stones and stray ferrous particles.
Clean paddy protects the huller rolls and keeps foreign matter out of the finished rice.

blocks.title: Dehusking & Husk Separation
desc: The husk is split off the grain and drawn away by aspiration, leaving brown rice mixed with a share of paddy that has not yet shelled.
That mixture is separated so unhusked grain returns to the huller and only dehusked rice moves forward.

blocks.title: Whitening
desc: The bran layer and germ are abraded off the brown rice, which is what turns the grain white.
Whitening is normally taken in stages rather than a single pass, and the bran removed is drawn off the machine for separate handling.

blocks.title: Polishing
desc: Polishing finishes the whitened grain, lifting residual bran dust off the surface and giving the smooth appearance expected of table rice.
Polished rice is cooled and settled before it goes on to grading.

blocks.title: Grading & Colour Sorting
desc: Whole grains, brokens and small brokens are separated by size, and the graded rice then passes an optical sorter that rejects discoloured, chalky and damaged grains.
Grading fixes the commercial grade of each stream, so head rice and brokens can be handled and sold separately.

blocks.title: Weighing, Inspection & Packing
desc: Graded rice is held in silos, blended where a particular grade mix is required, then weighed and filled into consumer packs or bulk sacks.
Filled packs are checked and pass metal detection before they are stitched or sealed and made ready for despatch.

metaDesc: Brown rice milling machinery from ART Mechatronics - paddy cleaning, drying, dehusking, husk separation, de-dusting, grading, colour sorting and barrier packing.
intro: Brown rice is paddy that has had only its husk removed, leaving the bran layer and germ on the grain. Processing therefore stops short of whitening: paddy is cleaned, dried and rested, dehusked, then graded, colour sorted and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies machinery and turnkey plant systems for brown rice milling lines.

blocks.text: Brown rice is paddy that has had only its husk removed, leaving the bran layer and germ on the grain. Processing therefore stops short of whitening: paddy is cleaned, dried and rested, dehusked, then graded, colour sorted and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies machinery and turnkey plant systems for brown rice milling lines.

blocks.title: Paddy Intake & Cleaning
desc: Paddy is received and cleaned of straw, chaff, soil, stones and ferrous particles before it enters the mill.
Because brown rice keeps its bran layer, anything not taken out at this stage stays on the finished grain.

blocks.title: Drying & Moisture Conditioning
desc: Paddy is dried and then rested in bins so moisture equalises through the grain before it reaches the huller.
Bran-bearing rice is sensitive to storage moisture, so the moisture level is checked before milling and again before packing.

blocks.title: Dehusking & Paddy Separation
desc: Only the outer husk is taken off; the bran layer and germ that give brown rice its colour and character are left intact.
Husk is carried away in the air stream and any grain that has not shelled is separated out and returned to the huller.

blocks.title: De-Dusting
desc: Loose bran dust and light husk fragments released during dehusking are drawn off the grain stream.
No whitening or polishing is carried out at this point, as the bran layer itself has to stay on the grain.

blocks.title: Grading & Colour Sorting
desc: Grain is separated by size into whole and broken fractions, and an optical sorter takes out immature, damaged and off-colour grains along with any paddy still carrying husk.
The sorter is set against the natural bran colour of the lot rather than a white grain surface.

blocks.title: Weighing & Protective Packing
desc: Sorted brown rice is weighed and filled into consumer packs, with vacuum or gas-flushed packing used where the contents have to be kept away from air.
The retained bran layer carries oil, so brown rice is commonly packed in barrier material rather than plain woven sacks.

h1: Dairy Milk Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Dairy Milk Processing Plant & Machinery | Turnkey Dairy Milk Line by ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Complete dairy milk processing plant and machinery from ART Mechatronics — material handling, processing, quality control and packaging, engineered as one turnkey line.
intro: Dairy milk processing takes raw buffalo or cow milk from collection through chilling, clarification, cream separation and standardisation, then heat treatment such as pasteurisation or sterilisation, homogenising and hygienic filling into pouches, bottles or cartons. ART Mechatronics supplies dairy milk plant and machinery for reception, thermal treatment, storage and packing on food-grade, cleanable lines.

blocks.text: Dairy milk processing takes raw buffalo or cow milk from collection through chilling, clarification, cream separation and standardisation, then heat treatment such as pasteurisation or sterilisation, homogenising and hygienic filling into pouches, bottles or cartons. ART Mechatronics supplies dairy milk plant and machinery for reception, thermal treatment, storage and packing on food-grade, cleanable lines.

blocks.title: Reception & Chilling
desc: Raw milk arriving from collection centres is weighed, tested and cooled before it enters insulated storage.
Chilling the milk as soon as it is received slows bacterial growth until processing begins.

blocks.title: Clarification & Cream Separation
desc: A centrifugal separator removes sediment and splits the milk into skim milk and cream.
Measured cream is blended back into the skim milk to set the fat level of the finished product.

blocks.title: Homogenising
desc: The standardised milk is forced through a homogeniser so the fat globules are broken down and evenly dispersed.
This keeps a cream layer from rising to the top during storage.

blocks.title: Heat Treatment
desc: Milk is pasteurised or sterilised and then cooled again through a heat exchanger.
Steam for the heating stage is raised in the plant boiler and fed to the process vessels.

blocks.title: Filling & Sealing
desc: Treated milk is filled into pouches, bottles or cups on enclosed filling lines and sealed straight away.
Each pack is coded with batch and date details as it leaves the filler.

blocks.title: Inspection & Cold Storage
desc: Filled packs are checked for fill weight, leaks and stray metal before they are crated.

blocks.text: Rice milk is a plant-based drink made by cooking cleaned rice, breaking down its starch into simpler sugars, then milling the mash, separating the solids and blending the liquid with water and oil before homogenising, heat treatment and filling. ART Mechatronics supplies rice milk plant and machinery covering grain cleaning, cooking, wet milling, separation and packing.

blocks.title: Grain Cleaning
desc: Incoming rice is passed over screens and a de-stoner to take out chaff, dust, stones and stray metal.
Clean grain protects the mill and keeps grit out of the finished drink.

blocks.title: Washing & Cooking
desc: Cleaned rice is washed and then cooked in a jacketed vessel until the starch granules swell and gelatinise.
Gelatinised starch is what the enzymes in the next stage are able to act on.

blocks.title: Enzymatic Conversion
desc: Enzymes are dosed into the cooked mash, which is held under gentle stirring while the starch is broken into simpler sugars.
This conversion is what gives rice milk its sweetness.

blocks.title: Wet Milling & Separation
desc: The converted mash is milled down to a fine slurry and the insoluble rice solids are drawn off.
What remains is the liquid base of the drink.

blocks.title: Blending & Homogenising
desc: Water, oil and mineral blends are mixed into the base to set body and mouthfeel.
The mix then passes through a homogeniser so it stays uniform and does not settle in the pack.

blocks.title: Heat Treatment & Filling
desc: The drink is heat-treated, cooled and filled into cartons, bottles or pouches on a closed line.
Sealed packs are coded and collated into cases for dispatch.

blocks.text: Coconut milk is extracted from the white kernel of mature coconuts, which are de-husked, de-shelled and pared before the kernel is shredded, pressed and the extract filtered, standardised, homogenised and sterilised for canning or aseptic packing. blocks.title: De-husking & Shelling
desc: Mature coconuts are de-husked and the hard shell is cracked away from the kernel.
Coconut water released at this stage is drained and collected separately.

blocks.title: Paring & Washing
desc: The brown testa is pared off the white kernel and the kernel is washed and rinsed.
Removing the skin keeps the extract white and free of dark specks.

blocks.title: Shredding & Extraction
desc: The pared kernel is shredded and the milk is pressed out in an expeller or press.
The residue can be moistened and pressed a second time to recover a lighter extract.

blocks.title: Filtering & Standardising
desc: The extract is strained and passed through a separator to take out fibre and adjust the fat content.
Stabilisers and emulsifiers are dosed in so the milk holds together in the pack.

blocks.title: Homogenising & Sterilising
desc: The standardised milk is homogenised and then sterilised so that it can be packed for ambient distribution.
Cooling follows immediately through a heat exchanger before filling.

blocks.title: Canning & Packing
desc: Coconut milk is filled into cans, retort pouches or cartons and seamed or sealed shut.
Packs are labelled, cased and palletised for domestic and export despatch.

blocks.text: Almond milk is made from shelled almonds that are cleaned, sorted, blanched and skinned, then soaked and wet-ground with water; the slurry is separated from the almond solids, blended, homogenised, heat-treated and filled. blocks.title: Cleaning & Sorting
desc: Shelled almonds are cleaned of dust and shell fragments, then sorted by colour and appearance.
Discoloured, shrivelled and damaged kernels are rejected before they can reach the grinder.

blocks.title: Blanching & Skin Removal
desc: Kernels are blanched in hot water so the brown skin loosens, and the skin is then rubbed away.
Skinning gives a paler drink with a milder, less astringent taste.

blocks.title: Soaking & Wet Grinding
desc: Blanched kernels are soaked and then ground with water into a smooth slurry.
Finer grinding releases more of the nut solids into the liquid.

blocks.title: Separation
desc: The slurry is separated so the almond pulp is drawn off and the milk passes on.
The pulp is pressed to release the liquid still held in it and then collected for use in flours, snacks and animal feed.

blocks.title: Blending & Homogenising
desc: Water, salt, oil and stabiliser blends are dosed in and mixed to a uniform batch.
Homogenising keeps the milk from separating into layers while it stands on the shelf.

blocks.title: Heat Treatment & Bottling
desc: The blended milk is pasteurised or sterilised, cooled and filled into bottles or cartons.
Filled packs are capped, labelled and collated for dispatch.

blocks.text: Soy milk is produced from cleaned, de-hulled soybeans that are soaked and hot-ground with water, after which the okara is separated, the extract cooked and deodorised to reduce beany notes, then blended, homogenised, sterilised and filled. blocks.title: Bean Cleaning & De-hulling
desc: Soybeans are cleaned of dust, stones and foreign matter, then de-hulled and the loose hulls blown clear.
Taking the hulls off reduces the beany character carried through into the milk.

blocks.title: Washing & Soaking
desc: De-hulled beans are washed and soaked in water until they soften and swell.
Softened beans break down more easily in the grinder and give a better yield of extract.

blocks.title: Hot Grinding
desc: Soaked beans are ground together with hot water to form the slurry.
Grinding hot checks the enzyme action responsible for the raw bean smell while the slurry is being made.

blocks.title: Okara Separation
desc: The slurry is separated into soy extract and okara, the insoluble bean residue.
Okara is drawn off continuously for food or feed use.

blocks.title: Cooking & Deodorising
desc: The extract is cooked to break down the anti-nutritional factors present in raw soybeans.
It is then deodorised under vacuum to strip out the remaining beany volatiles.

blocks.title: Blending, Homogenising & Filling
desc: Sugar, flavour and stabilisers are blended in and the milk is homogenised and sterilised.
It is then filled and sealed into pouches, bottles or cartons on an enclosed line.

blocks.title: Oat Cleaning
desc: Oat groats are pre-cleaned, screened and de-stoned to take out chaff, dust, stones and stray metal.
Clean groats protect the mill and keep grit out of the flour.

blocks.title: Dry Milling

blocks.title: Slurry Mixing & Enzymatic Conversion

intro: Dried fruit and vegetable processing removes moisture from fresh produce so that it can be stored and shipped without refrigeration. Washed material is peeled, cut to a uniform size, blanched to hold colour, then dried in hot air until it reaches a stable moisture level, and finally graded and packed in moisture-barrier packaging.

blocks.text: Dried fruit and vegetable processing removes moisture from fresh produce so that it can be stored and shipped without refrigeration. Washed material is peeled, cut to a uniform size, blanched to hold colour, then dried in hot air until it reaches a stable moisture level, and finally graded and packed in moisture-barrier packaging.

sections.title: Complete Dried Fruit & Vegetable Process Flow
sections.key: COMPLETE DRIED FRUIT & VEGETABLE PROCESS FLOW

blocks.title: Intake & Washing
desc: Crates and bins are tipped onto the line and the produce is washed to remove field soil, grit and loose leaves.
Stones and heavy foreign matter are taken out before the material reaches any cutting equipment.

blocks.title: Peeling & Cutting
desc: Skins are removed where the recipe calls for it and the produce is cut into slices, dice or shreds.
Uniform piece size matters here because pieces of different thickness dry at different rates.

blocks.title: Blanching & Cooling
desc: A short heat treatment halts the enzyme activity that causes browning and off-flavours during storage.
The blanched product is cooled immediately so it does not continue to cook on the belt.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Heated air is passed over the product in trays, on a moving belt or in a fluidised bed, depending on the piece size and how delicate the material is.
Moisture is checked through the batch so the drying is stopped at the right point rather than by the clock.

blocks.title: Grading & Inspection
desc: Dried pieces are separated by size and the discoloured, scorched or under-dried ones are rejected.
A metal check is made before the product enters packing.

blocks.title: Weighing & Packing
desc: The dried product is weighed to pack size and sealed in a barrier film or pouch, often with the air replaced by nitrogen.
Finished packs are weight-checked, coded and collated into cartons for dispatch.

blocks.text: Fresh fruit and vegetable processing prepares produce for sale without drying, freezing or cooking it. sections.title: Complete Fresh Fruit & Vegetable Process Flow
sections.key: COMPLETE FRESH FRUIT & VEGETABLE PROCESS FLOW

blocks.title: Reception & Pre-Cooling
desc: Produce is unloaded and brought down to working temperature before anything else is done to it.
Field heat carried into the plant shortens shelf life, so cooling comes first, not last.

blocks.title: Washing & Rinsing
desc: The produce is washed and then rinsed in clean water to carry away soil and surface debris.
Surface water is blown off before the produce moves on, and handling is kept gentle because bruised tissue browns once the pack is sealed.

blocks.title: Sorting & Grading
desc: Damaged, misshapen and off-colour units are taken out and the rest is graded to the sizes the buyer has specified.
Camera-based inspection supports the hand-sorting stations on the belt.

blocks.title: Trimming, Peeling & Cutting
desc: Stems, cores and skins are removed and the produce is cut into the wedges, florets, batons or shreds the pack calls for.
Clean blades give a clean cut face, which is what keeps a fresh-cut pack looking fresh.

blocks.title: Chilled Packing
desc: Portions are filled into trays, punnets or films and sealed, with modified atmosphere used where the product needs it.
Packs are weight-checked and labelled with the pack and use-by details.

blocks.title: Cold Storage & Dispatch
desc: Finished packs are palletised and held in a cold room until the vehicle is loaded.
The chain from the packing hall to dispatch is kept unbroken.

sections.title: Complete Frozen Fruit & Vegetable Process Flow
sections.key: COMPLETE FROZEN FRUIT & VEGETABLE PROCESS FLOW

blocks.title: Intake, Washing & Sorting
desc: Incoming produce is washed and passed over a sorter so that soft, spotted and off-colour units never reach the freezer.
Stones and other heavy contaminants are removed at this stage.

blocks.title: Peeling, De-Stemming & Cutting
desc: Skins, stems and stones are taken off and the produce is cut to the piece shape the pack requires.
Even pieces freeze evenly, which is what keeps them separate rather than clumped.

blocks.title: Blanching & Rapid Cooling
desc: Vegetables are blanched to stop enzyme activity, then chilled straight away so residual heat does not soften them.
Many fruits skip the blanch and go from cutting to cooling.

blocks.title: Freezing
desc: Cold air moving through a fluidised belt freezes the pieces individually so they stay loose and pourable.
Product is pre-cooled ahead of the freezer, while bulk, block and packed material goes into a blast room instead.

blocks.title: Inspection & Foreign-Body Control
desc: Frozen product is checked for metal and other foreign matter and any remaining defective pieces are removed.
Inspection is done after freezing because that is the form the customer receives.

blocks.title: Packing & Cold Storage
desc: The frozen product is weighed, bagged or bulk packed, coded and cartoned without letting it thaw.
Pallets go straight into the cold store to await dispatch.

sections.title: Complete Fruit & Vegetable Powder Process Flow
sections.key: COMPLETE FRUIT & VEGETABLE POWDER PROCESS FLOW

blocks.title: Cleaning & Preparation
desc: Produce is washed, peeled where needed and cut thin so that it will dry through rather than case-harden.
Material going down the spray-dried route is crushed to a pulp instead of being cut, and feed to the dryer is kept steady either way.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Solid pieces are dried in trays or on a belt; liquid feeds such as pulp and juice are spray dried directly into powder.
Heat-sensitive material that must keep its colour and aroma is freeze dried instead.

blocks.title: Grinding & Pulverising
desc: The dried material is broken down and then pulverised to powder.
Milling is run with extraction attached, because dry plant powder is light and travels through the room otherwise.

blocks.title: Sieving & Classification
desc: The ground powder is screened so that oversize particles and fibre are separated and returned for regrinding.
Air classification is used where a narrower particle band is wanted than a screen alone will give.

blocks.title: Blending & Dust Control
desc: Batches are blended so colour and flavour are consistent from pack to pack, and tramp metal is pulled out on the way.
Extraction and collection equipment is fitted at the mill and at transfer points to control airborne powder.

blocks.title: Filling & Packing
desc: Powder is dosed by auger into pouches, jars or sacks and sealed against moisture pick-up.
Each pack is weight-checked and coded before it leaves the line.

The washed raw material is crushed, cooked and reduced to remove water, then refined through a mill until it is smooth and dense. The paste is heat treated and filled into pouches, cans or drums.

sections.title: Complete Fruit & Vegetable Paste Process Flow
sections.key: COMPLETE FRUIT & VEGETABLE PASTE PROCESS FLOW

blocks.title: Washing & Sorting
desc: Raw material is washed and sorted so that rotten, mouldy and unripe units are taken out before crushing.
Whatever goes into the kettle sets the colour and taste of the finished paste, so this stage is not skipped.

blocks.title: Crushing & Pulping
desc: The produce is broken down into a coarse pulp and the skins and seeds are separated out.
Peel and seed left in the pulp show up later as specks and bitterness.

blocks.title: Cooking & Concentration
desc: The pulp is cooked in a jacketed vessel with continuous stirring and water is driven off to thicken it.
Steam is supplied from the utility side and heat is recovered through the exchanger.

blocks.title: Milling & Refining
desc: The concentrate is passed through a wet mill so the remaining fibre is broken down and the texture becomes smooth.
Shearing at this stage also disperses the solids through the batch.

blocks.title: Sterilisation & Holding
desc: The paste is heat treated to make it shelf stable, then cooled and held in a closed tank until filling.
Holding the hot paste in open vessels darkens it, so transfer is kept closed.

blocks.title: Filling & Packing
desc: Measured doses are filled into retort pouches, cans, jars or bulk drums depending on whether the buyer is retail or industrial.
Containers are closed, labelled and coded on the same line.

sections.title: Complete Fruit & Vegetable Puree Process Flow

blocks.title: Reception, Washing & Inspection
desc: Ripe fruit and vegetables are washed, rinsed and inspected on the belt so that spoiled units are removed.
Puree carries the flavour of everything that goes into it, so ripeness is checked at intake.

blocks.title: Stem, Stone & Peel Removal
desc: Stems, stones and skins are taken off before pulping, since they cannot be removed cleanly afterwards.
Which of these stages are used depends on the fruit or vegetable being run.

blocks.title: Pulping & Fine Finishing
desc: The prepared material is broken down and then passed through a finer stage that removes coarse fibre and skin fragments.
This is what separates a puree from a crushed pulp.

blocks.title: Heating & Homogenising
desc: The pulp is heated and then homogenised so the solids are broken down and dispersed through the batch.
Gentle stirring in a jacketed vessel keeps the batch even while it is held.

blocks.title: Pasteurising & Chilled Holding
desc: The puree is pasteurised and cooled quickly, then held in a closed tank ahead of filling.
Fast cooling protects the fresh colour and flavour the product is bought for.

blocks.title: Filling & Packing
desc: Puree is filled into bottles, spouted pouches or bulk containers, closed and labelled.
Seals are checked before the packs are collated, because a weak seal on a liquid pack fails in transit.

blocks.title: Washing, Grading & Icing
desc: Landed fish are washed of slime and sand and graded by species and size before the cutting line.
Grading at intake decides which fish go to fillet, which to whole frozen and which to drying.

Offal is conveyed to a separate collection point so the edible line stays clean.

blocks.text: Fresh non-vegetarian food covers chilled meat, poultry, fish and seafood sold without freezing. blocks.title: Chilled Intake & Cold Chain
desc: Chilled meat, poultry and fish are received and moved into refrigerated holding without a break in the cold chain.
Since the product is never frozen, temperature control at every step is what gives it its shelf life.

blocks.title: Cutting & Portioning in Chilled Rooms
desc: Cuts, fillets and portions are prepared in temperature-controlled rooms on food-grade surfaces.
Working cold keeps the cut surface firm and slows growth on the exposed meat.

blocks.title: Weighing & Tray Filling
desc: Portions are weighed to the target pack weight and laid into trays or pots.
Weighing before sealing avoids underweight packs being sealed and rejected later.

blocks.title: Modified Atmosphere & Vacuum Sealing
desc: Trays are sealed with a gas flush or drawn down under vacuum, depending on the product.
Seals are tested because a leaking pack loses the atmosphere that holds the product fresh.

blocks.title: Coding, Labelling & Inspection

Metal detection and vision checks run before the pack leaves the line.

blocks.title: Chilled Storage & Dispatch
desc: Finished packs are cased, palletised and held in chilled storage until the vehicle loads.

blocks.text: Dried non-vegetarian food includes dried fish and prawn, meat floss, egg powder and dried pet-food ingredients. blocks.title: Cleaning, Salting & Pre-Cooking
desc: Raw fish, prawn or meat is washed and then salted, brined or cooked according to the product.
Salting and cooking draw out water and set the protein before the drying stage begins.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Material is spread on trays or a moving belt and dried in heated air until it reaches the target dryness.
Air temperature and flow are controlled so the surface does not case-harden and trap moisture inside.

blocks.title: Freeze Drying
desc: Heat-sensitive items such as prawn, egg and pet treats can be frozen and dried under vacuum instead of hot air.
Freeze drying removes water from the frozen material under vacuum, so the piece keeps its shape and rehydrates when water is added.

blocks.title: Milling, Flaking & Sieving
desc: Dried material is broken down into floss, flakes or powder and screened to the size the buyer wants.
Oversize is returned to the mill so the batch leaves at one particle size.

blocks.title: Moisture Control & Holding
desc: Moisture is measured on the dried batch, and the holding area is kept dehumidified before packing.
Dried protein picks up moisture from the air, so the room condition matters as much as the dryer.

blocks.title: Pouch Packing
desc: The dried product is weighed and filled into pouches, sealed with a nitrogen flush and cased.
A gas flush and a tight seal are what keep dried protein from going rancid on the shelf.

Checkweighing confirms the declared weight before the pack is cased.

h1: Powdered Chemical Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Powdered Chemical Processing Plant & Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Powdered chemical processing covers dosing, dry blending, drying, milling, sieving and contained packing. ART Mechatronics supplies the plant and machinery.
intro: Powdered chemical manufacturing converts liquid, slurry or granular raw materials into a dry, free-flowing powder of controlled particle size. The route usually combines dosing, dry blending or reaction, drying, milling and sieving, followed by contained filling. Dust containment and contamination control run through the whole line. ART Mechatronics supplies powder processing and packing plants for chemical manufacturers.

blocks.text: Powdered chemical manufacturing converts liquid, slurry or granular raw materials into a dry, free-flowing powder of controlled particle size. The route usually combines dosing, dry blending or reaction, drying, milling and sieving, followed by contained filling. Dust containment and contamination control run through the whole line. ART Mechatronics supplies powder processing and packing plants for chemical manufacturers.

blocks.title: Raw Material Intake & Dosing
desc: Bagged and bulk solids are tipped and conveyed to day storage, while liquid and slurry feeds are held in tanks alongside them.
Each ingredient is weighed out to the batch recipe, and that charging sets the composition of everything downstream.

blocks.title: Dry Blending & Reaction
desc: Weighed solids are blended, and where the formulation calls for it, granulated or reacted in the mixer.
How long the batch is worked in the mixer is what decides whether successive packs drawn from it match.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Depending on the route, a solution or slurry is spray dried, or the wet mass from the mixer is dried and the moisture driven off.
The dryer is chosen to suit the feed and the heat sensitivity of the chemical, since drying is what stabilises the powder against caking in storage.

blocks.title: Milling & Particle Sizing
desc: Dried lumps and agglomerates are reduced and milled down to the particle size the application requires.
Particle size governs how the powder dissolves, disperses and flows in the customer's own process.

blocks.title: Sieving & Contaminant Removal
desc: Milled powder is screened to take out oversize, and passed over magnets and detectors to pull out ferrous and metal fragments.
Off-size and foreign matter are rejected before the powder reaches the filling machine.

blocks.title: Dust Extraction & Containment
desc: Airborne dust is captured at the mill, sieve and packing points and carried to collection.
Extraction at these points is what keeps dust out of the workspace and stops one grade carrying over into the next.

blocks.title: Filling & Packing
desc: Finished powder is auger-filled into pouches, sacks or drums, sealed, and stacked for despatch.
Pack format follows the trade the chemical is sold into, from small retail packs to bulk industrial drums.

intro: Liquid chemical manufacturing blends, reacts and disperses raw materials in tanks and reactors to produce solutions, emulsions, suspensions or slurries. blocks.text: Liquid chemical manufacturing blends, reacts and disperses raw materials in tanks and reactors to produce solutions, emulsions, suspensions or slurries. Typical stages are charging and dosing, heated reaction under agitation, homogenising, cooling and clarification, then filling into bottles, jerry cans or drums with capping, labelling and leak checks. ART Mechatronics supplies liquid processing and filling lines for chemical plants.

blocks.title: Raw Material Storage & Charging
desc: Liquid raw materials are held in bulk tanks while powders and additives are tipped and conveyed to the vessel.
Each ingredient is weighed or metered against the batch sheet before it enters the reactor.

blocks.title: Reaction & Heating
desc: The charged batch is stirred in a jacketed vessel while heat is supplied through the jacket and held at the recipe condition.
Continuous agitation keeps the batch even and stops solids settling out during the reaction.

blocks.title: Mixing, Dispersion & Homogenising
desc: Emulsions, dispersions and viscous formulations are worked under shear to break down droplets and agglomerates.
The shear stage is what decides how well the liquid holds together instead of separating in storage.

blocks.title: Cooling & Clarification
desc: The finished batch is cooled and any undissolved solids or separated phases are drawn off before it is held in a day tank.
Cooling brings the liquid to a temperature at which it can be safely filled into its container.

blocks.title: Filling into Containers
desc: Containers are rinsed and filled by volume or weight, from small bottles up to jerry cans and drums.
The filling method is matched to the viscosity of the liquid and to the pack being run.

blocks.title: Capping, Labelling & Coding
desc: Filled containers are capped or sealed, labelled and given batch and date coding.
Coding keeps each container traceable back to the batch it was filled from.

blocks.title: Inspection & Secondary Packing
desc: Packs are checked for leaks, weight and fill level, then cartoned or wrapped onto pallets for despatch.
Faulty or short-filled containers are taken off the line before the consignment is made up.

blocks.title: Waste Paper Yard & Feed Preparation
desc: Baled recovered paper and agricultural residue are opened, sorted and fed towards the pulper.
Wire, staples and other tramp metal are pulled out of the stream on the way in.

blocks.title: Stock Preparation & Sheet Forming

Our supply around this section covers the feed and reject conveying, stock tanks and plant-wide control rather than the machine itself.

h1: Corrugated Paper Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Corrugated Paper Plant & Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Steam and utility plant, trim extraction, waste baling, bundling and palletising equipment for corrugated board and box plants from ART Mechatronics.
intro: Corrugated paper is produced by fluting one paper web with heat and steam and gluing it between kraft liners on a corrugator, giving board that is then cut, printed, slotted, die cut and folded into boxes. Trim, offcuts and paper dust come off continuously, and finished bundles are strapped, palletised and wrapped.

blocks.text: Corrugated paper is produced by fluting one paper web with heat and steam and gluing it between kraft liners on a corrugator, giving board that is then cut, printed, slotted, die cut and folded into boxes. Trim, offcuts and paper dust come off continuously, and finished bundles are strapped, palletised and wrapped.

blocks.title: Liner & Fluting Reel Handling
desc: Kraft liner and fluting medium reels are stored and brought to the mill roll stands.
Reels are lifted and positioned with handling equipment so the corrugator can be spliced without stopping.

blocks.title: Corrugating & Board Forming
desc: One web is fluted between heated rolls and glued to the liners on the single facer and double backer.
Steam and heat plant serve the corrugator, and the starch adhesive is prepared and held in the glue kitchen alongside it.

blocks.title: Cutting, Trim Extraction & Stacking
desc: The board is slit, cross-cut and stacked at the dry end of the corrugator.
Edge trim and dust are drawn off by a pneumatic system, separated from the air, and taken straight to the baler.

blocks.title: Printing, Slotting & Die Cutting
desc: Sheets are printed, slotted and die cut into box blanks on the converting machines.
Waste board and dust from this section are extracted at the machine and each blank is checked before it goes forward.

blocks.title: Folding, Joining & Bundling
desc: Blanks are folded and joined at the manufacturer's joint by glue or wire stitching.
Finished boxes are counted into bundles and strapped flat.

blocks.title: Palletising & Dispatch
desc: Bundles are palletised, wrapped and loaded out to the customer's plant.

h1: Copier Paper Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Copier Paper Plant & Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Sheeter trim extraction, air conditioning, ream counting, wrapping, box packing and palletising equipment for copier paper plants from ART Mechatronics.
intro: Copier paper is made by cutting jumbo paper reels into cut-size sheets on a sheeter, counting the sheets into reams, and wrapping each ream before it is boxed. Sheeting produces edge trim and paper dust, and the reams are weight checked, coded, packed into cartons and palletised for dispatch.

blocks.text: Copier paper is made by cutting jumbo paper reels into cut-size sheets on a sheeter, counting the sheets into reams, and wrapping each ream before it is boxed. Sheeting produces edge trim and paper dust, and the reams are weight checked, coded, packed into cartons and palletised for dispatch.

blocks.title: Jumbo Reel Handling & Hall Conditioning
desc: Jumbo reels are stored and brought to the sheeter reel stands.
Cut-size paper is sensitive to moisture, so the sheeting and packing halls are conditioned and dehumidified.

blocks.title: Sheeting & Trim Extraction
desc: Reels are slit lengthways and cross-cut into sheets of the ordered cut size.
Edge trim and paper dust from the cutting section are pulled away at the knives and separated before collection.

blocks.title: Sheet Counting & Ream Formation
desc: Sheets are counted and jogged into square reams.
Short counts, torn sheets and misaligned stacks are picked up and taken off the line.

blocks.title: Ream Wrapping & Coding
desc: Each ream is wrapped and sealed in printed paper or film.
The wrapped ream is coded and weight checked before it goes forward to packing.

blocks.title: Box Packing & Palletising
desc: Reams are collated and loaded into cartons, which are then palletised and wrapped for dispatch.

blocks.title: Trim Recovery & Plant Automation
desc: Trim and reject sheets collected by the extraction network are baled for return to the mill.
The sheeting, wrapping and palletising sections are sequenced together from one control system.

h1: Tobacco Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Tobacco Processing Plant & Machinery | Turnkey Tobacco Line by ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Complete tobacco processing plant and machinery from ART Mechatronics — material handling, processing, quality control and packaging, engineered as one turnkey line.
intro: Tobacco processing covers a family of products — cured leaf, cigarette and cigar filler, shisha and hookah blends, chewing forms such as khaini and zarda, oral pouches, snuff and tobacco powder. ART Mechatronics supplies plant and machinery for the shared stages: leaf conditioning, cutting, drying, blending, dust control and packing, with equipment configured for the format being made.

blocks.text: Tobacco processing covers a family of products — cured leaf, cigarette and cigar filler, shisha and hookah blends, chewing forms such as khaini and zarda, oral pouches, snuff and tobacco powder. ART Mechatronics supplies plant and machinery for the shared stages: leaf conditioning, cutting, drying, blending, dust control and packing, with equipment configured for the format being made.

blocks.title: Leaf intake and cleaning
desc: Cured leaf arrives in bales and is opened out, fed onto the line and separated from sand, string and metal.
Loose dust and light trash are drawn off before the leaf goes forward.

blocks.title: Conditioning
desc: Leaf is brought to a workable moisture with warm, humidified air so it flexes instead of shattering when cut.
Moisture is checked on the way through.

blocks.title: Cutting and shredding
desc: Conditioned leaf and stem are cut to the width the product calls for — fine cut for cigarette and rolling tobacco, coarser for shisha and cigar filler.
Cut material is screened to take out fines.

blocks.title: Drying and cooling
desc: Cut tobacco is dried to bring the moisture back down after conditioning, then cooled before it is stored or blended.
The dryer type follows the batch or continuous layout of the plant.

blocks.title: Blending, casing and flavouring
desc: Different grades are weighed out and mixed to a recipe, and casing or flavour is applied where the product uses it — shisha, dokha and flavoured rolling tobacco branch here.
Chewing blends such as khaini and zarda take their additives at this stage.

blocks.title: Grinding for powder and pouch products
desc: Snuff, tobacco powder, filter khaini and oral pouch fillings need the blend reduced to a fine particle and then classified.
This branch runs under dust extraction because the material is airborne.

blocks.title: Filling, packing and coding
desc: Finished tobacco is filled by weight into pouches, tins or pouch sachets, sealed, coded and cased.
Oral pouch products are formed and filled on their own dedicated equipment.

h1: Snacks Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Snacks Processing Plant & Machinery | Turnkey Snacks Line by ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Complete snacks processing plant and machinery from ART Mechatronics — material handling, processing, quality control and packaging, engineered as one turnkey line.
intro: Snack manufacturing spans fried, roasted, puffed and extruded lines — potato chips and crisps, savoury namkeen, flavoured peanuts, roasted makhana and grams, popcorn, breakfast flakes and seasoned seeds. ART Mechatronics supplies the plant behind them: raw-material cleaning and preparation, frying or roasting, seasoning, and weighing and pouch packing, arranged to suit the snack being produced.

blocks.text: Snack manufacturing spans fried, roasted, puffed and extruded lines — potato chips and crisps, savoury namkeen, flavoured peanuts, roasted makhana and grams, popcorn, breakfast flakes and seasoned seeds. ART Mechatronics supplies the plant behind them: raw-material cleaning and preparation, frying or roasting, seasoning, and weighing and pouch packing, arranged to suit the snack being produced.

blocks.title: Cleaning and grading the raw material
desc: Potatoes, grains, pulses, nuts or seeds are taken in, freed of stones, soil and metal, then graded to size.
Washing is used on the tuber and vegetable lines.

blocks.title: Preparation
desc: Depending on the snack the material is peeled, sliced, diced or blanched before cooking.
Chips and crisps are sliced here; namkeen doughs and extruded pellets are prepared instead.

blocks.title: Frying, roasting or puffing
desc: This is where the category branches. Chips, crisps and namkeen are fried; peanuts, grams, makhana and seeds are roasted; puffed snacks and flakes go through an extruder.
Popcorn and cereal flakes take the hot-air route.

blocks.title: De-oiling and cooling
desc: Surplus surface oil is drained and blown off, then the product is brought down to ambient before seasoning so the flavour holds.
Cooling is done on a moving belt or in a tunnel.

blocks.title: Seasoning
desc: Dry seasoning or a slurry is metered onto the snack in a rotating drum or pan so it coats the whole surface.
Feed rate and dosing are matched so the coating stays even along the run.

blocks.title: Weighing, inspection and primary packing
desc: Seasoned snack is collected in a weigher, dropped into a formed pouch, gas-flushed where the product needs it, sealed and checked.
Every pack passes metal detection and a checkweigher.

blocks.title: Secondary packing and palletising
desc: Pouches are collated into cartons or cases, then stacked and wrapped for despatch.

h1: Nuts Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Nuts Processing Plant & Machinery | Turnkey Nuts Line by ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Complete nuts processing plant and machinery from ART Mechatronics — material handling, processing, quality control and packaging, engineered as one turnkey line.
intro: Nut processing covers groundnut, cashew, almond, walnut, pistachio, areca and betel nut, coconut, foxnut and dates. Although each kernel is handled differently, the route is common: cleaning and grading, shell and skin removal, drying or roasting, sorting, and packing. ART Mechatronics supplies plant and machinery for these stages and for the material handling between them.

blocks.text: Nut processing covers groundnut, cashew, almond, walnut, pistachio, areca and betel nut, coconut, foxnut and dates. Although each kernel is handled differently, the route is common: cleaning and grading, shell and skin removal, drying or roasting, sorting, and packing. ART Mechatronics supplies plant and machinery for these stages and for the material handling between them.

blocks.title: Intake, cleaning and de-stoning
desc: Nuts in shell are taken in and cleaned of soil, stones, sticks and tramp metal on a screen and aspiration cleaner.
Cleaned stock is held in bins ahead of shelling.

blocks.title: Shelling and dehusking
desc: The shell or husk is cracked and opened, then kernel and shell are separated by air and by weight.
Areca, betel and coconut go through their own dehusking route.

blocks.title: Skin removal and polishing
desc: The testa or skin is loosened and taken off, and kernels are polished where the product is sold blanched.
Almonds and groundnuts are the main lines that use this stage.

blocks.title: Drying or roasting
desc: Kernels are dried down for storage, or roasted where the product is a roasted nut, and then cooled before sorting.
Dates and foxnut branch to their own drying schedules.

blocks.title: Grading and sorting
desc: Kernels are graded to size, then sorted to remove discoloured, split and foreign pieces.
Sorting is done optically and by hand pick on the belt.

blocks.title: Value-added branches
desc: Some kernels go on to be split, milled into butter or paste, or pressed for oil rather than sold whole.
Groundnut is the usual candidate for all three.

blocks.title: Weighing and packing
desc: Finished kernels are weighed, checked for foreign body and filled into pouches, vacuum packs or jars.
Pack format follows whether the nut goes to retail or to bulk trade.

h1: Flour Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Flour Processing Plant & Machinery | Turnkey Flour Line by ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Complete flour processing plant and machinery from ART Mechatronics — material handling, processing, quality control and packaging, engineered as one turnkey line.
intro: Flour milling turns wheat, maize and mixed grains into atta, maida, corn flour and multigrain flour. Grain is cleaned, dampened and tempered, then reduced through mills and separated on sifters into flour, semolina and bran fractions before blending and packing. ART Mechatronics supplies the cleaning, milling, sifting, conveying, dust control and bagging equipment for these lines.

blocks.text: Flour milling turns wheat, maize and mixed grains into atta, maida, corn flour and multigrain flour. Grain is cleaned, dampened and tempered, then reduced through mills and separated on sifters into flour, semolina and bran fractions before blending and packing. ART Mechatronics supplies the cleaning, milling, sifting, conveying, dust control and bagging equipment for these lines.

blocks.title: Intake and pre-cleaning
desc: Grain is tipped, elevated and passed over screens and magnets to take out straw, dust, string and tramp metal before storage.
Cleaned grain is held in silos ahead of the mill.

blocks.title: Separation and scouring
desc: Stones, mud balls and light seeds are removed by density, and the grain surface is scoured to lift dust and loose skin.
The dust drawn off here is collected rather than released.

blocks.title: Dampening and tempering
desc: Water is metered onto the clean grain and the grain rests in bins so the moisture works into the bran layer and it peels away cleanly in the mill.
Moisture is checked before and after the rest period.

blocks.title: Milling and reduction
desc: Tempered grain passes through break and reduction rolls, or through a stone or hammer mill on atta and chakki-style lines, and is progressively reduced.
Stock is returned for further reduction after each sifting pass.

blocks.title: Sifting and grading of fractions
desc: Milled stock is separated on sifters into flour, semolina, middlings and bran, and light bran is drawn off in the air system.
Each fraction returns to the mill or goes to the flour bin.

blocks.title: Blending and multigrain mixing
desc: Flour streams are blended to the grade being sold, and multigrain lines dose and mix the additional grain flours at this point.

blocks.title: Bagging and despatch
desc: Flour is filled by weight into consumer packs or sacks, closed, checked and palletised.
A final metal check is made before the pack leaves the line.

h1: Rice Bran Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Rice Bran Processing Plant & Machinery | Turnkey Rice Bran Line by ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Complete rice bran processing plant and machinery from ART Mechatronics — material handling, processing, quality control and packaging, engineered as one turnkey line.
intro: Rice bran is the outer layer removed when brown rice is polished into white rice. Because it begins to degrade soon after milling, it is stabilised by heat, then sifted, and either bagged as a feed and food ingredient or pressed for rice bran oil, leaving de-oiled cake. ART Mechatronics supplies handling, stabilising, sifting and packing equipment for this line.

blocks.text: Rice bran is the outer layer removed when brown rice is polished into white rice. Because it begins to degrade soon after milling, it is stabilised by heat, then sifted, and either bagged as a feed and food ingredient or pressed for rice bran oil, leaving de-oiled cake. ART Mechatronics supplies handling, stabilising, sifting and packing equipment for this line.

blocks.title: Bran collection from the rice mill
desc: Bran drawn off the whitening and polishing machines is collected and conveyed to the stabilising plant.
It is moved in a closed system because the material is fine and airborne.

blocks.title: Separation of husk and broken rice
desc: Husk, bran flakes and small brokens carried over with the bran are separated by air and screen so only bran goes forward.
Tramp metal is taken out at the same point.

blocks.title: Stabilising
desc: The bran is heat treated so the enzymes that break down its oil stop acting, which is what allows it to be stored and traded.
Heat is supplied indirectly through the extruder or heat exchanger circuit.

blocks.title: Cooling and moisture reduction
desc: Stabilised bran is cooled and dried back down before storage.
Moisture is measured on the outfeed.

blocks.title: Oil extraction branch
desc: Where the bran is being processed for oil, it is pressed in an expeller and the crude oil is run to tank, leaving the pressed cake behind.
Oil is drummed or tankered out; the cake goes to the feed trade.

blocks.title: Sifting, bagging and despatch
desc: Stabilised bran or pressed cake is sifted to grade, weighed into sacks, stitched closed and moved out on conveyor.

metaTitle: Bakery Processing Plant & Machinery | Turnkey Bakery Line by ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Complete bakery processing plant and machinery from ART Mechatronics — material handling, processing, quality control and packaging, engineered as one turnkey line.
intro: Bakery production covers bread and buns, brown and multigrain loaves, rusk and toast, and biscuits and cookies. Flour, water and other ingredients are dosed and mixed into dough, divided and shaped, proved or laminated, baked, cooled and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies dosing, mixing, forming, proving, baking, cooling and packing equipment across these lines.

blocks.text: Bakery production covers bread and buns, brown and multigrain loaves, rusk and toast, and biscuits and cookies. Flour, water and other ingredients are dosed and mixed into dough, divided and shaped, proved or laminated, baked, cooled and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies dosing, mixing, forming, proving, baking, cooling and packing equipment across these lines.

blocks.title: Ingredient handling and dosing
desc: Flour is taken from silo or sack, sifted and weighed, and the minor ingredients are dosed to the recipe.
Water, fat, sugar and yeast are metered in on the same batch call.

blocks.title: Dough mixing
desc: The batch is mixed until the dough is developed. Bread doughs are taken to full development; biscuit and cookie doughs are mixed short.
Chilled water is used to hold the dough temperature down through the mix.

blocks.title: Dividing, shaping and proving
desc: Bread dough is divided, rounded, rested, moulded and panned, then proved in humidified air. Biscuit and cookie dough is sheeted, cut or wire-cut into pieces instead.
This is where the bread and the biscuit routes separate.

blocks.title: Baking
desc: The pieces are baked in a rack or tunnel oven. Rusk and toast lines return the baked loaf to the oven a second time after slicing.

blocks.title: Depanning and cooling
desc: Baked product is turned out of the pans and cooled on a spiral or belt cooling conveyor until it is firm enough to slice and wrap.

blocks.title: Slicing, stacking and primary packing
desc: Loaves are sliced and bagged; biscuits are stacked into slugs and flow wrapped.
Packs pass a metal check before they leave the line.

blocks.title: Case packing and palletising
desc: Wrapped packs are collated into cartons or trays, cased, stacked and wrapped for despatch.

intro: Confectionery covers wafers, chocolate, cakes and energy bars. Batters and masses are prepared and mixed, baked or refined and tempered, filled or creamed, cooled, cut into shape and wrapped. ART Mechatronics supplies the mixing, baking, cooling, cutting and wrapping equipment for these lines, along with the conveying and packing systems that link them.

blocks.text: Confectionery covers wafers, chocolate, cakes and energy bars. Batters and masses are prepared and mixed, baked or refined and tempered, filled or creamed, cooled, cut into shape and wrapped. ART Mechatronics supplies the mixing, baking, cooling, cutting and wrapping equipment for these lines, along with the conveying and packing systems that link them.

blocks.title: Ingredient dosing and batter preparation
desc: Ingredients are weighed to the recipe and worked into a batter, dough or mass.
Wafer batter is mixed thin; cake batter and bar masses are mixed heavy.

blocks.title: Refining and conching — the chocolate branch
desc: Chocolate mass is ground down and worked until the particles are reduced, then held warm and moving in a jacketed vessel.
This branch does not apply to the wafer, cake or bar lines.

blocks.title: Baking and depositing
desc: Wafer batter is baked into thin sheets, cake batter is deposited and baked, and bar masses are formed and set.
Heat is carried to the oven by hot air or a thermic fluid circuit.

blocks.title: Creaming, filling and enrobing
desc: Cream or filling is prepared and applied between wafer sheets, into cake, or over the bar, and the assembled book or bar goes forward.
Chocolate is deposited or enrobed at this stage.

blocks.title: Cooling and setting
desc: The filled product passes through a cooling tunnel so the fat sets before it is cut, and may be held in a cold room.

blocks.title: Cutting to shape
desc: Set books, slabs and cakes are cut into fingers, squares or bars.
Cut size follows the pack format rather than the process.

blocks.title: Wrapping and secondary packing
desc: Pieces are fed into a wrapper, cartoned, over-wrapped and palletised.

blocks.text: Condiments cover peanut butter, honey, syrups, ketchup and sauces, spreads, dips and dressings, and pickles and chutneys. Ingredients are cleaned and prepared, cooked or blended into a paste or liquid, milled and homogenised for texture, then filled into jars, bottles or pouches and capped. ART Mechatronics supplies preparation, cooking, milling, mixing and filling equipment for these lines.

blocks.title: Raw material cleaning and preparation
desc: Nuts, fruit, vegetables or spices are cleaned of stones and soil, washed, and cut or chopped down to a workable size.
Peanut lines de-stone and clean before roasting; pickle lines cut and salt.

blocks.title: Roasting and cooking
desc: Peanuts are roasted and cooled; sauce, ketchup and chutney bases are cooked in a jacketed kettle with the sugar, salt and acid of the recipe.
Honey and syrup lines warm the product rather than cook it.

blocks.title: Grinding and refining
desc: The cooked or roasted material is reduced to a paste and then refined so the finished texture is smooth or deliberately coarse.
Peanut butter, spreads and dips all pass this stage.

blocks.title: Blending, dosing and heat treatment
desc: Stabiliser, oil, salt and flavour are dosed in and the batch is blended, then heat treated and held in tank ahead of filling.

blocks.title: Filling and closing
desc: The condiment is filled by volume into jars, bottles or pouches and closed.
Thick pastes are piston filled; thin sauces and syrups run on nozzle filling.

blocks.title: Labelling, coding and case packing
desc: Closed containers are labelled, date coded and packed into cartons or cases for despatch.
