h1: Milk Shake Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Milk Shake Processing Plant & Machinery | Turnkey Milk Shake Line by ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Complete milk shake processing plant and machinery from ART Mechatronics — material handling, processing, quality control and packaging, engineered as one turnkey line.
intro: Milk shake is a flavoured dairy drink made by blending milk with sugar, stabilisers and flavouring, then homogenising the mix, heat treating it, cooling it and filling it into bottles, pouches or cans. ART Mechatronics supplies the mixing, homogenising, heat treatment, cooling, filling and cold-chain equipment used on these lines.

blocks.text: Milk shake is a flavoured dairy drink made by blending milk with sugar, stabilisers and flavouring, then homogenising the mix, heat treating it, cooling it and filling it into bottles, pouches or cans. ART Mechatronics supplies the mixing, homogenising, heat treatment, cooling, filling and cold-chain equipment used on these lines.

blocks.title: Milk reception and chilled storage

blocks.title: Intake, washing and grading
desc: Produce is tipped into a hopper, washed and rinsed clear of soil and field trash, then graded and colour sorted so damaged and unripe pieces are taken out.

blocks.title: Peeling, coring and cutting
desc: Skin is removed where the product needs it, seeds and stems are taken out, and the produce is sliced or diced to a size that will dry evenly.

blocks.title: Blanching and pre-treatment
desc: Cut pieces are blanched to stop enzyme activity and hold colour, and may be dipped or sulphited before drying, depending on the fruit or vegetable.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Moisture is driven off in a tunnel, tray or freeze dryer until the pieces are stable at ambient storage.
Freeze drying is used where the piece shape and colour have to be kept.

blocks.title: Milling and sieving to flake or powder
desc: Dried pieces are milled and then sieved and classified so the flake or powder is held to one particle range.

blocks.title: Pulp and paste branch
desc: Where the output is pulp or puree rather than powder, the washed produce is crushed, refined and held in tank instead of dried.

blocks.title: Weighing and packing
desc: Flake, powder or pulp is filled into pouches or bulk packs, gas flushed where oxygen would spoil it, checked and cased.

blocks.title: Dehusking and shell removal
desc: Mature nuts are taken in, the fibrous husk is stripped off and the hard shell is cracked away from the kernel.

blocks.title: Paring and washing
desc: The brown testa is pared off the kernel so only white meat goes forward, and the pared kernel is washed and rinsed.

blocks.title: Cutting and disintegrating
desc: White kernel is cut and then broken down to the particle the grade calls for — fine, medium or chip.
Oversize is returned to the cutter.

blocks.title: Blanching and sterilising
desc: The cut meat is blanched with steam and then cooled before it enters the dryer.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Moisture is driven off in a hot-air dryer until the desiccated coconut is stable for storage and trade.

blocks.title: Sifting into grades
desc: Dried coconut is screened and classified into the fine, medium and coarse grades that are sold separately.

blocks.title: Weighing and packing
desc: Each grade is weighed out, vacuum or bulk packed, metal checked and cased for despatch.

intro: Industrial mineral processing turns quartz, feldspar, calcite, dolomite, talc and barytes into graded powders for paint, ceramics, plastics, glass and construction. The ore is crushed and sized, washed and dried, freed of iron, then ground and micronised, air-classified to the required fineness and packed. blocks.text: Industrial mineral processing turns quartz, feldspar, calcite, dolomite, talc and barytes into graded powders for paint, ceramics, plastics, glass and construction. The ore is crushed and sized, washed and dried, freed of iron, then ground and micronised, air-classified to the required fineness and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies crushing, drying, grinding, classifying, separation and packing equipment for mineral grinding units.

blocks.title: Crushing & Sizing
desc: Run-of-mine quartz, feldspar, calcite or talc is crushed and screened down to a mill feed size.
Lumps are hand-sorted at this stage where colour or purity decides the grade.

blocks.title: Washing & Drying
desc: Ore carrying clay or surface dirt is washed and then dried, because dry grinding needs dry feed.
Dried material is held in bins ahead of the mills.

blocks.title: Iron Removal
desc: Many mineral grades are sold on low iron content, so tramp iron and iron-bearing grains are taken out ahead of grinding.
Density-based separation removes the heavier unwanted particles.

blocks.title: Grinding & Micronising
desc: The mineral is ground down and then micronised to the fine powder that paint, plastics and ceramic buyers specify.
The mill is chosen to suit the hardness of the mineral being handled.

blocks.title: Air Classification & Sieving
desc: Ground powder is classified in air to the required fineness, with coarse material returned to the mill.
Sieving gives a final check on top size before packing.

blocks.title: Packing & Palletising
desc: Powder is weighed into bags or bulk bags, closed and stacked.
Grades are kept apart through packing so that one does not contaminate another.

blocks.title: Dust Collection
desc: Fine mineral powder becomes airborne easily, so mills, classifiers and packing points are kept under extraction.
Recovered powder is returned to the product stream.

h1: Coconut Flakes Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Coconut Flakes Processing Plant | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Coconut flake processing plants from ART Mechatronics covering kernel paring, slicing, blanching, sweetening, drying, roasting, grading and packing.
intro: Coconut flakes are broad slices of pared coconut kernel, dried and often toasted or sweetened for use in bakery, cereals, snacks and confectionery. Mature kernel is dehusked, deshelled and pared, sliced into flakes, blanched, dried and where required roasted, then graded and packed. ART Mechatronics builds coconut flake lines covering slicing, drying, roasting, grading and packing.

blocks.text: Coconut flakes are broad slices of pared coconut kernel, dried and often toasted or sweetened for use in bakery, cereals, snacks and confectionery. Mature kernel is dehusked, deshelled and pared, sliced into flakes, blanched, dried and where required roasted, then graded and packed. ART Mechatronics builds coconut flake lines covering slicing, drying, roasting, grading and packing.

blocks.title: Kernel Preparation
desc: Nuts are dehusked and deshelled and the testa is pared off, because a flake is a broad visible piece and any brown skin shows in the pack.
Pared kernel is rinsed and drained before slicing.

blocks.title: Slicing into Flakes
desc: Pared kernel is sliced into wide flat flakes rather than shredded, which is what separates flakes from desiccated coconut.
Slice thickness is set on the cutter to suit whether the flake will be dried plain or toasted.

blocks.title: Blanching & Sweetening
desc: Flakes are blanched, and where a sweetened flake is called for they are coated with syrup in a pan mixer before drying.
Syrup is prepared in a jacketed vessel so that the coating is applied at a steady consistency.

blocks.title: Drying
desc: Flakes are dried in a continuous hot-air dryer, laid out in a single layer so that they dry without curling together.
Moisture is checked on the dried flake before it moves to roasting or grading.

blocks.title: Roasting
desc: Where a toasted flake is required, dried flakes are roasted to develop colour and flavour, then cooled straight away so that colour does not carry on developing.
Fines released in roasting are drawn off before packing.

blocks.title: Grading & Packing
desc: Flakes are graded and broken pieces screened out so that the pack shows whole flakes.
Graded flakes are weighed, formed into pouches with nitrogen flushing where required, and inspected for metal before cartoning.

metaDesc: Coconut oil milling and refining plants from ART Mechatronics covering copra cleaning, conditioning, expelling, clarification, refining, cake handling and filling.
intro: Coconut oil is pressed from dried coconut kernel, or copra, and is used in cooking, food manufacturing, cosmetics and oleochemicals. Cleaned copra is sized, conditioned with heat, pressed in expellers, and the crude oil is settled and clarified before refining, deodorising and filling. ART Mechatronics supplies coconut oil milling and refining plants together with cake handling and packing.

blocks.text: Coconut oil is pressed from dried coconut kernel, or copra, and is used in cooking, food manufacturing, cosmetics and oleochemicals. Cleaned copra is sized, conditioned with heat, pressed in expellers, and the crude oil is settled and clarified before refining, deodorising and filling. ART Mechatronics supplies coconut oil milling and refining plants together with cake handling and packing.

blocks.title: Copra Cleaning & Sizing
desc: Incoming copra is cleaned of dust, fibre, stones and tramp metal, then broken down to a uniform size for the press.
Cleaning ahead of the mill protects the expeller worms from stones and metal carried in with the copra.

blocks.title: Conditioning & Cooking
desc: Sized copra is heated and conditioned so that the oil cells are opened and the meal enters the press in a workable state.
Conditioning is run on indirect steam heat from the plant boiler.

blocks.title: Expelling
desc: Conditioned meal is pressed in screw expellers, which separate crude oil from the solid cake.
Crude oil runs to a settling tank while the cake is carried off on a separate conveyor.

blocks.title: Settling & Clarification
desc: Crude oil is settled and clarified so that fines and press sediment carried over from the expeller are removed.
Recovered sediment is returned to the press feed rather than discarded.

blocks.title: Refining & Deodorising
desc: Where refined oil is being made, the clarified oil is neutralised, bleached and deodorised in heated, agitated vessels to give a bland, light-coloured oil.
Virgin oil lines skip this stage, since virgin coconut oil is sold on its natural aroma.

blocks.title: Cake Handling
desc: Press cake is cooled, broken down and milled into copra meal for animal feed, which is a saleable co-product of the mill.
Meal is bagged and stitched on its own packing line.

blocks.title: Filling & Packing
desc: Finished oil is filled into pouches, bottles, jerry cans or drums according to the pack ordered.
Filled packs are capped, labelled, coded and case packed for despatch.

intro: Gram processing covers black gram (urad) and green gram (moong), whose husk clings tightly to the kernel. The seed is cleaned, scratched or pitted, treated with oil and water, tempered and dried, then dehusked and split in repeated light passes rather than one heavy pass. blocks.text: Gram processing covers black gram (urad) and green gram (moong), whose husk clings tightly to the kernel. The seed is cleaned, scratched or pitted, treated with oil and water, tempered and dried, then dehusked and split in repeated light passes rather than one heavy pass. Dal and flour are then sorted and packed. ART Mechatronics supplies complete gram milling lines.

blocks.title: Intake & Cleaning
desc: Urad and moong arrive with field trash, dust, stones and metal, all of which are removed before milling.
Cleaned grain is held in bins until the conditioning stage is ready to take it.

blocks.title: Pitting & Oil-Water Conditioning
desc: The husk of gram sticks to the kernel, so the seed surface is first scratched, or pitted, to open a path for the treatment.
Oil and water are then mixed through the grain so that the husk lifts away in the milling that follows.

blocks.title: Tempering & Drying
desc: Treated grain is held so the moisture can move into the seed, then dried before it goes to the huller.
Moisture is checked on each batch as it comes off the dryer.

blocks.title: Dehusking & Splitting
desc: Grain passes through the huller in repeated light passes rather than in a single heavy pass, and is lifted back to the huller between passes.
Husk is drawn off between passes and the dehusked kernel is then split to give dhuli dal.

blocks.title: Polishing & Grading
desc: Split gram dal is polished and then separated into whole, split and broken fractions.
Powder and small brokens are carried away on their own stream.

blocks.title: Flour Milling
desc: Part of the urad and moong dal is ground into flour for papad, vada and batter use.
The ground stock is sifted and the coarse fraction is returned to the mill.

blocks.title: Sorting & Packing
desc: Colour sorting removes husk-bearing, discoloured and off-grade grains before packing.
Dal goes into consumer pouches and bulk sacks, and every pack is coded.

intro: Maize processing separates the cleaned kernel into germ, bran and endosperm so that grits, meal and maize flour can be milled from it. blocks.text: Maize processing separates the cleaned kernel into germ, bran and endosperm so that grits, meal and maize flour can be milled from it. Kernels are tempered, degerminated, dried and graded, with the oil-bearing germ drawn off as its own stream. ART Mechatronics supplies maize cleaning, degerming, milling, grading and packing plants for food and feed producers.

blocks.title: Intake, Cleaning & De-Stoning
desc: Maize is received into storage and cleaned of cob pieces, husk, dust, stones and tramp metal.
Clean grain protects the degerming and milling machines that follow.

blocks.title: Tempering Before Degerming
desc: Water is added and the maize is rested so the bran and germ loosen from the endosperm.
Moisture is checked before the grain is degermed.

blocks.title: Degerming & Germ Separation
desc: Tempered kernels are opened so the germ and bran come free of the endosperm, then separated by density and air.
Germ is taken out whole so it can be pressed rather than milled.

blocks.title: Drying & Cooling of Grits
desc: Degermed grits are dried back from tempering moisture and cooled before milling and storage.

blocks.title: Milling & Grading into Grits, Meal and Flour
desc: Dried endosperm is reduced and sifted into grits, meal and maize flour, with the fractions kept apart by size and by air.

blocks.title: Germ Handling & Oil Recovery
desc: The separated germ is conveyed to an expeller, pressed for maize oil, and the cake is taken off for feed use.

blocks.title: Packing & Despatch
desc: Grits, meal and flour are weighed, bagged, stitched, inspected and palletised for food and feed customers.

blocks.text: Wheat processing mills cleaned grain into atta, maida, bran and mill by-products for bakeries, chakki brands and retail packs. Wheat is screened, de-stoned, scoured and tempered with water before it is reduced on roller or stone mills and sifted into flour grades. blocks.title: Intake & Trash Removal
desc: Wheat is tipped into an intake pit, elevated and screened so straw, string, dust and undersize seed are taken out on arrival.
Magnets remove ferrous pieces before the grain reaches any mill.

blocks.title: De-Stoning & Scouring
desc: Stones and mud balls are separated by density, and the kernel surface is scoured to lift crease dirt and loose bran.
Light seed and dust leave with the aspirated air.

blocks.title: Tempering & Conditioning
desc: Measured water is added and the wheat rests in conditioning bins so the bran toughens and the endosperm softens.
Well-tempered wheat gives cleaner bran separation in the mill.

blocks.title: Milling on Roller or Stone Mills
desc: Conditioned wheat is reduced through roller passages for maida and suji, or ground on stone mills where whole-wheat chakki atta is the product.
Stock is moved between machines mechanically and pneumatically.

blocks.title: Sifting & Flour Grading
desc: Ground stock is sifted and air-classified into atta, maida, suji and bran streams.
Oversize stock returns for a further reduction passage.

blocks.title: Blending & Storage
desc: Flour streams are blended to a consistent grade, and any permitted additives are dosed in before storage.

blocks.title: Flour Packing
desc: Flour is auger-filled into retail packs or bagged for trade, then stitched, coded, weighed and checked.

blocks.text: Corn processing covers the food lines that turn cleaned corn and corn grits into flakes, extruded snacks and corn flour. blocks.title: Cleaning & Grit Preparation
desc: Corn is cleaned and de-stoned, then broken and graded to the grit size the flake or snack line needs.
Off-size fractions are diverted to flour or feed.

blocks.title: Cooking with Flavour Slurry
desc: Grits are cooked under steam with a slurry of sugar, salt and malt until the starch is gelatinised.
The cooked mass is discharged and broken up so the pieces separate before drying.

blocks.title: Drying & Tempering
desc: Cooked grits are dried and then held in tempering bins so moisture equalises through each piece.
Even moisture is what allows a flake to roll without tearing.

blocks.title: Flaking & Toasting
desc: Tempered grits are pressed between rolls into thin flakes and then toasted so they blister and crisp.
Flakes are cooled on the way out of the oven.

blocks.title: Extruded Snack & Coating Stream
desc: Corn meal fed to an extruder expands into puffs and rings, which are then tumbled with oil and seasoning in a coating pan.
Coated snacks are cooled before they reach the weigher.

blocks.title: Weighing, Gas-Flush Packing & Inspection

Fruit arrives loose, is tipped onto a collecting table, washed and surface dried, then sorted and graded by size, colour and defect. Graded fruit is either packed whole for the fresh market or sent on to drying, freezing, pulping and juice lines.

blocks.title: Reception & Tipping
desc: Crates and bins are emptied onto a collecting table that spreads the fruit into a single, even flow.
A holding bin lets the line keep running between vehicle deliveries.

blocks.title: Washing & Surface Drying
desc: Fruit is washed and rinsed to remove field dust and residues, then surface dried with moving air.
Brushing gives the skin an even finish before the fruit reaches the graders.

blocks.title: Sorting & Grading
desc: Fruit is separated by colour, size and visible defect so each grade goes to the market that pays for it.
Rejected and second-grade fruit is diverted rather than discarded, and feeds the processing lines.

blocks.title: Peeling, De-Seeding & Cutting
desc: Fruit routed to processing is peeled, halved or de-seeded and cut to the shape the downstream line needs.
Whole fruit for the fresh market bypasses this stage entirely.

blocks.title: Onward Processing Routes
desc: Cut fruit goes to the dryer, to the freezer or to crushing for pulp and juice, depending on the order being run.
A short blanch is used ahead of drying and freezing for the varieties that need it.

blocks.title: Packing & Dispatch
desc: Graded fruit is packed into trays, punnets or films, then labelled and date coded.
Packs are collated into cartons and palletised for transport.

h1: Cosmetic Cream Processing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Cosmetic Cream Processing Plant & Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Cosmetic cream manufacturing plant and machinery from ART Mechatronics: wax melting, vacuum emulsification, scraped cooling, jar and tube filling, lid pressing.
intro: Cosmetic cream manufacturing produces a thick emulsion, such as face cream, cold cream, moisturiser or a balm style skincare product, packed into jars, tubes and wide mouth bottles. Waxes and butters are melted, emulsified under vacuum, cooled under slow scraping agitation, then perfumed and filled. ART Mechatronics supplies vacuum emulsification, cooling, filling and packing machinery for cosmetic cream plants.

blocks.text: Cosmetic cream manufacturing produces a thick emulsion, such as face cream, cold cream, moisturiser or a balm style skincare product, packed into jars, tubes and wide mouth bottles. Waxes and butters are melted, emulsified under vacuum, cooled under slow scraping agitation, then perfumed and filled. ART Mechatronics supplies vacuum emulsification, cooling, filling and packing machinery for cosmetic cream plants.

blocks.title: Weighing & Wax Melting
desc: Waxes, butters and solid emulsifiers are melted in a jacketed vessel heated by thermic fluid, while the water phase is prepared alongside it.
Powdered actives and gums are sieved during weighing so they disperse cleanly into the phases.

blocks.title: Vacuum Emulsification
desc: The molten phase is drawn into the water phase under vacuum and worked at high shear until the cream body is formed.
Working under vacuum keeps air out of a heavy emulsion, from which trapped bubbles cannot rise on their own.

blocks.title: Cooling With Slow Agitation
desc: Cooling water is circulated through the jacket while a slow scraping stir keeps the cream moving against the vessel wall.
This is where the cream gains its final texture and stiffness.

blocks.title: Perfume, Actives & Final Working
desc: Perfume, preservative and heat-sensitive actives are added once the batch has cooled, and the cream is worked once more to make it uniform.
The batch is then held for appearance, pH and consistency checks.

blocks.title: Jar & Tube Filling
desc: The cream is fed to a piston filler that meters a thick product into jars, tubes and wide mouth bottles.
Tubes are sealed, and inner discs, lids and closures are applied on the same line.

blocks.title: Labelling, Cartoning & Despatch
desc: Jars are labelled with a wraparound applicator, coded and checkweighed.
Packs go into mono cartons, then into shipper cases which are wrapped for despatch.

h1: Pharmaceutical Syrup Manufacturing Plant & Machinery Solutions
metaTitle: Pharmaceutical Syrup Plant & Machinery | ART Mechatronics
metaDesc: Pharmaceutical syrup plant machinery — jacketed syrup vessels, high shear mixing, homogenising, bulk storage, bottle rinsing and filling, capping and labelling.
intro: Pharmaceutical syrup manufacturing dissolves active ingredients, sugar or sugar-free base, preservatives and flavours into a stable liquid dose. Purified water and syrup base are prepared in a jacketed vessel, actives are mixed and homogenised, the bulk is filtered and held, then bottles are rinsed, filled, capped, labelled and cartoned. ART Mechatronics supplies liquid oral plant machinery for syrup preparation, storage, filling and packing.

blocks.text: Pharmaceutical syrup manufacturing dissolves active ingredients, sugar or sugar-free base, preservatives and flavours into a stable liquid dose. Purified water and syrup base are prepared in a jacketed vessel, actives are mixed and homogenised, the bulk is filtered and held, then bottles are rinsed, filled, capped, labelled and cartoned. ART Mechatronics supplies liquid oral plant machinery for syrup preparation, storage, filling and packing.

blocks.title: Syrup Base Preparation
desc: Sugar or a sugar-free base is dissolved into purified water in a steam-jacketed vessel under continuous stirring.
Heating in a jacket rather than a direct flame keeps the base from scorching.

blocks.title: Mixing & Homogenising
desc: Actives, preservatives, colours and flavours are added to the base and mixed until fully dissolved or evenly suspended.
Suspensions are homogenised or milled so the solid phase stays dispersed instead of settling out.

blocks.title: Cooling, Filtration & Bulk Storage
desc: The batch is cooled, filtered to remove undissolved matter, and held in a storage vessel until the filling line calls for it.
The holding vessel is kept closed and under filtered air.

blocks.title: Bottle Rinsing & Filling
desc: Empty bottles are rinsed and inverted to drain before they reach the filler.
Syrup is dosed by volume, with nozzle tracking used on products that foam during filling.

blocks.title: Capping & Sealing
desc: Bottles are capped and sealed, and the closure is checked so the pack does not leak in transit.
Measuring cups or dosing caps are applied at this stage where the pack carries one.

blocks.title: Labelling, Coding & Cartoning
desc: Labels are applied around the bottle and batch, manufacturing and expiry details are printed on.
Camera checks confirm label and code presence before the bottle is cartoned with its leaflet and cased.
